sections.subtopic: Experimental Foundations - The Faraday and Henry Experiments
sections.title: Why this chapter exists: running Oersted backwards

board_events.text: Oersted and Ampere: a CURRENT makes a magnetic field
By the 1820s this was settled physics. Electricity produces magnetism.
The obvious next question
Can a magnetic field produce a current? Can we run the arrow the other way?
Michael Faraday in England and Joseph Henry in the USA answered YES, working independently.
But with a subtlety that took years to pin down. That subtlety IS this chapter.
Every generator, transformer and induction motor alive today descends from their answer.
Understanding the experiments makes every later formula feel inevitable rather than arbitrary.

segments.text: <curious> Let me start with a question physicists were stuck on two centuries ago. By the eighteen twenties, thanks to Oersted and Ampere, everybody knew one direction of the story cold: push a current through a wire, and a magnetic field appears around it.
Electricity makes magnetism. That was solid, repeatable, textbook physics. Compass needles swinging near current-carrying wires had made the point beyond argument.
So the natural question almost asks itself. If electricity produces magnetism, can magnetism produce electricity? Can you run the whole thing backwards?
It sounds like it should be easy. Take a magnet, take a coil of wire, put them together, and collect your current. Physicists tried exactly that, for years, and mostly got nothing at all.

Two people cracked it, working completely independently of each other. Michael Faraday in England, and Joseph Henry in the United States. Both of them found that yes, magnetism can absolutely produce electricity.
But the answer came with a condition attached, and that condition is subtle enough that it took years to nail down precisely. That one subtlety is the whole content of this chapter.

And I want you to feel the stakes here. Every generator in every power station, every transformer on every street pole, every induction motor in every fan and pump, is a direct descendant of what these two men found.

Here is why we start with the experiments rather than the formula. If you meet Faraday's law cold, it looks arbitrary. If you meet it after the experiments, it looks inevitable. That is the difference between memorising and knowing.

<curious> चलिए शुरू करते हैं उस question से जिस पर physicists दो सदी पहले अटके हुए थे। अठारह सौ बीस तक, Oersted और Ampere की वजह से, सबको एक direction अच्छी तरह पता था: wire में current भेजो, उसके चारों तरफ magnetic field आ जाती है।
यानी electricity से magnetism बनती है। ये बिलकुल solid, repeatable physics थी। Current-carrying wire के पास compass needle का घूमना इस बात को साबित कर चुका था।
तो अगला सवाल अपने आप बन जाता है। अगर electricity से magnetism बनती है, तो क्या magnetism से electricity बन सकती है? क्या पूरी चीज़ को उल्टा चलाया जा सकता है?
सुनने में लगता है आसान होगा। एक magnet लो, एक coil लो, दोनों को पास रखो, current मिल जाएगा। Physicists ने सालों तक यही किया, और ज़्यादातर बार कुछ भी नहीं मिला।
दो लोगों ने इसे solve किया, एक दूसरे से बिलकुल independently. England में Michael Faraday, और America में Joseph Henry. दोनों ने पाया कि हाँ, magnetism से electricity ज़रूर बन सकती है।
लेकिन जवाब के साथ एक condition जुड़ी हुई थी, और वो condition इतनी subtle है कि उसे ठीक से समझने में सालों लगे। वही एक subtlety इस पूरे chapter का content है।
और मैं चाहती हूँ कि आप इसकी अहमियत महसूस करें। हर power station का generator, हर street pole का transformer, हर fan और pump का induction motor, इन्हीं दो लोगों की खोज का सीधा वंशज है।

अब ये समझिए कि हम formula से नहीं, experiments से क्यों शुरू कर रहे हैं। अगर Faraday's law सीधे मिले तो arbitrary लगता है। Experiments के बाद मिले तो inevitable लगता है। यही फ़र्क़ है रटने और समझने में।

board_events.text: Push the magnet toward the coil and the needle deflects. Pull it away and it deflects the OTHER way.
Hold the magnet dead still, even right inside the coil, and the needle drops to ZERO.
Move the magnet faster and the deflection is larger. Move the coil instead of the magnet and it works identically.
Experiment 2: a coil in place of the magnet
Swap the bar magnet for a second coil carrying a steady current. Move it in and out. The galvanometer behaves exactly as before.

segments.text: Start with the simplest experiment in the whole chapter. A coil of wire, connected to a galvanometer, which is just a sensitive current detector with a needle that sits at zero in the middle and can swing either way.

And here is the detail that should make you sit up. There is no cell, no battery, no power source anywhere in this circuit. If that needle ever moves, the current driving it came from nowhere we put there.
Look at the setup on the board. Coil on the right wired to the galvanometer, bar magnet on the left, and everything at rest to begin with. Needle sitting quietly at zero.
Now push the magnet toward the coil. The needle jumps. Pull the magnet back out, and the needle swings the opposite way. So the direction of the effect tracks the direction of the motion.

<excited> And now the observation that decides everything. Stop moving the magnet. Hold it perfectly still, even parked right inside the coil where the field is strongest. The needle falls back to zero. A strong magnet, sitting there doing nothing, produces nothing.

Two more findings. Move the magnet faster and you get a bigger deflection, so the rate of the motion matters, not just the fact of it. And if you hold the magnet still and move the coil instead, you get the same result. Only the relative motion counts.

Experiment two attacks a possible objection. Maybe there is something special about bar magnets. So replace the magnet with a second coil carrying a steady current from a battery, because a current-carrying coil is itself a magnet.

Move that second coil toward and away from the first, and the galvanometer deflects exactly as it did before. So this was never about magnets specifically. It is about the magnetic field linking the coil. That is the seed of mutual induction, which we reach later in the chapter.

शुरुआत करते हैं पूरे chapter के सबसे simple experiment से। एक coil of wire, जो एक galvanometer से जुड़ी है, यानी एक sensitive current detector जिसकी needle बीच में zero पर रहती है और दोनों तरफ घूम सकती है।
और अब वो detail जो आपको चौकन्ना कर देनी चाहिए। इस circuit में कहीं भी कोई cell नहीं, कोई battery नहीं, कोई power source नहीं। अगर needle हिली, तो उसे चलाने वाला current कहीं बाहर से नहीं आया।
Board पर setup देखिए। दाईं तरफ coil galvanometer से जुड़ी हुई, बाईं तरफ bar magnet, और शुरू में सब कुछ स्थिर। Needle चुपचाप zero पर।
अब magnet को coil की तरफ push कीजिए। Needle उछल पड़ती है। Magnet को वापस खींचिए, needle उल्टी तरफ घूम जाती है। यानी effect की direction, motion की direction के साथ बदलती है।

<excited> और अब वो observation जो सब कुछ तय कर देती है। Magnet हिलाना बंद कीजिए। बिलकुल स्थिर पकड़िए, चाहे coil के अंदर ही क्यों न हो जहाँ field सबसे strong है। Needle वापस zero पर आ जाती है। एक powerful magnet, चुपचाप बैठा हुआ, कुछ भी produce नहीं करता।

दो और बातें। Magnet तेज़ हिलाइए तो deflection बड़ा मिलता है, यानी motion का rate matter करता है, सिर्फ़ motion होना नहीं। और अगर magnet स्थिर रखकर coil हिलाएँ, तो भी वही result. सिर्फ़ relative motion मायने रखती है।

Experiment two एक possible objection पर वार करता है। शायद bar magnet में ही कुछ ख़ास हो? तो magnet हटाकर एक दूसरी coil रखिए जिसमें battery से steady current बह रहा है, क्योंकि current-carrying coil खुद एक magnet होती है।

उस दूसरी coil को पास लाइए और दूर ले जाइए, galvanometer बिलकुल पहले जैसा deflect करता है। तो बात कभी magnets की थी ही नहीं। बात है coil से link होने वाली magnetic field की। यही mutual induction का बीज है, जो हम आगे chapter में पढ़ेंगे।

board_events.text: At the instant the key is PRESSED, the galvanometer gives a momentary kick.
While the current stays steady, the galvanometer reads ZERO. No matter how large that current is.
At the instant the key is RELEASED, the galvanometer kicks the other way. Varying the resistor does the same thing.
The unifying statement
An emf is induced whenever the magnetic FLUX linked with a circuit changes with time. The faster the change, the larger the emf.

segments.text: <curious> Now the experiment that settles the argument, and it is the one where absolutely nothing moves. No magnet sliding, no coil travelling, everything clamped down and still.

Two coils sit close together, both fixed. The first one, the primary, is connected to a battery through a key, which is just a switch, and a variable resistor. The second one, the secondary, is connected to nothing but the galvanometer.

Study the picture. Primary on the left with its battery and key, secondary on the right with its galvanometer. There is no electrical connection between the two circuits whatsoever. They only sit near each other.
Press the key. Current in the primary suddenly rises from nothing to its full value. And in that instant, the galvanometer in the completely separate secondary circuit gives a momentary kick.

<excited> Then leave the key pressed. Current is now flowing steadily in the primary, making a healthy magnetic field. And the galvanometer reads exactly zero. Crank the current up as high as you like. Still zero. A big steady current does nothing at all.

Now release the key. The primary current collapses to nothing, and the galvanometer kicks the other way. And you get the same momentary kicks if, instead of switching, you just twiddle the variable resistor so the primary current changes smoothly.

So strip away the apparatus from all three experiments and ask what they share. Not motion, because experiment three had none. Not the presence of a field, because a steady field gave nothing. What they share is a magnetic field that is changing.

And here is the sentence the whole rest of the chapter makes quantitative. An emf is induced in a circuit whenever the magnetic flux linked with it changes with time, and the faster that flux changes, the larger the induced emf. Everything from here is that sentence in mathematical clothing.
<curious> अब वो experiment जो पूरी बहस ख़त्म कर देता है, और ये वही है जिसमें बिलकुल कुछ नहीं हिलता। न magnet सरकता है, न coil चलती है, सब कुछ कसकर बाँधा हुआ और स्थिर।

दो coils पास-पास रखी हैं, दोनों fixed. पहली वाली, primary, एक key यानी switch और variable resistor के ज़रिए battery से जुड़ी है। दूसरी वाली, secondary, सिर्फ़ galvanometer से जुड़ी है, और किसी चीज़ से नहीं।
तस्वीर ध्यान से देखिए। बाईं तरफ primary अपनी battery और key के साथ, दाईं तरफ secondary अपने galvanometer के साथ। दोनों circuits के बीच कोई electrical connection नहीं है। बस दोनों पास में रखी हैं।
अब key दबाइए। Primary में current अचानक zero से अपनी पूरी value तक चढ़ता है। और ठीक उसी पल, बिलकुल अलग secondary circuit का galvanometer एक झटका देता है।

<excited> अब key दबी रहने दीजिए। Primary में steady current बह रहा है, अच्छी ख़ासी magnetic field बन रही है। और galvanometer बिलकुल zero पढ़ता है। Current जितना बड़ा करना है कर लीजिए। फिर भी zero. बड़ा steady current कुछ नहीं करता।

अब key छोड़ दीजिए। Primary current गिरकर zero हो जाता है, और galvanometer उल्टी तरफ झटका देता है। और वही झटके तब भी मिलते हैं जब switching की जगह आप बस variable resistor घुमाकर primary current smoothly बदल दें।

तो तीनों experiments से apparatus हटाइए और पूछिए कि common क्या है। Motion नहीं, क्योंकि तीसरे में motion थी ही नहीं। Field का होना भी नहीं, क्योंकि steady field ने कुछ नहीं दिया। Common है एक magnetic field जो बदल रही है।

और अब वो वाक्य जिसे बाक़ी पूरा chapter quantitative बनाता है। किसी circuit में emf तब induce होती है जब उससे linked magnetic flux समय के साथ बदले, और flux जितनी तेज़ी से बदले, induced emf उतनी बड़ी। आगे सब कुछ इसी वाक्य का गणितीय रूप है।

sections.subtopic: Experimental Foundations - The Faraday and Henry Experiments
sections.title: Board answer: what do the three experiments establish?

board_events.text: CBSE 2 to 3 marks: state the conclusion of the Faraday and Henry experiments
Step 1. Name the observation: a galvanometer in a battery-free circuit deflects under certain conditions.
Step 2. List when it deflects: magnet moving relative to coil; second coil moving; primary current switched on or off or varied.
Step 3. List when it does NOT deflect: magnet stationary; primary current steady, however large.
Step 4. The marks live here. Name the common factor: changing magnetic flux, not motion and not field.
Step 5. State the law in words: an induced emf appears whenever the flux linked with the circuit changes, and grows with the rate of change.
Common lost mark: writing only that a magnet moving near a coil induces current. That describes experiment one and misses experiment three entirely.
Henry independently observed the same effect and went on to discover self-induction, which is subtopic three of this chapter.

segments.text: Let us turn this into marks, because C B S E asks this as a two to three mark question in exactly this shape: describe the experiments, or state what they conclude.

Step one. Name the observation clearly. A galvanometer sitting in a circuit that contains no battery at all nevertheless shows a deflection under certain conditions. Saying no battery is present is worth stating, because it is what makes the result remarkable.

Step two. List the cases where it deflects. The magnet moves relative to the coil, either one of them moving. A second current-carrying coil is moved near the first. The primary current is switched on, switched off, or varied with a resistor.

Step three, and this is where most answers get thin. List the cases where it does not deflect. The magnet held stationary, even inside the coil. And the primary current held steady, however large that current is.

Step four is where the marks actually live. Name the common factor across every case. Deflection appears whenever the magnetic flux threading the circuit is changing, and vanishes whenever that flux is constant. Not motion, because experiment three had no motion. Not field strength, because a huge steady field gave nothing.

Step five. Now state the law in words. An induced emf appears in a circuit whenever the magnetic flux linked with it changes, and the emf grows with the rate at which that flux changes. Write that sentence and you have secured the conclusion mark.

<whisper> Here is the mark students routinely drop. They write that moving a magnet near a coil induces a current, full stop. That is a correct description of experiment one and it completely misses experiment three, which is the decisive one. An examiner reading it cannot award the conclusion mark.

One closing detail worth a line if the question is worth three marks. Joseph Henry observed the same effect independently in America, and went on from it to discover self-induction, which is exactly what we develop in subtopic three of this chapter.
अब इसे marks में बदलते हैं, क्योंकि C B S E यही question दो से तीन marks में ठीक इसी shape में पूछता है: experiments describe कीजिए, या बताइए कि वो क्या conclude करते हैं।

Step एक। Observation साफ़-साफ़ लिखिए। एक circuit जिसमें कोई battery ही नहीं है, उसका galvanometer फिर भी कुछ conditions में deflect करता है। ये लिखना ज़रूरी है कि battery नहीं है, क्योंकि यही बात इस result को remarkable बनाती है।
Step दो। वो cases गिनाइए जहाँ deflection होता है। Magnet coil के relative हिले, चाहे कोई भी हिले। दूसरी current-carrying coil को पास लाया जाए। Primary current on हो, off हो, या resistor से बदला जाए।

Step तीन, और यहीं ज़्यादातर answers कमज़ोर पड़ते हैं। वो cases भी गिनाइए जहाँ deflection नहीं होता। Magnet स्थिर पकड़ा हुआ, चाहे coil के अंदर ही हो। और primary current steady, चाहे वो current कितना भी बड़ा हो।

Step चार, यहीं असली marks हैं। सब cases में common factor बताइए। Deflection तब आता है जब circuit से गुज़रती magnetic flux बदल रही हो, और तब ग़ायब हो जाता है जब flux constant हो। Motion नहीं, क्योंकि तीसरे experiment में motion थी ही नहीं। Field की strength भी नहीं, क्योंकि बड़ी steady field ने कुछ नहीं दिया।

Step पाँच। अब law को शब्दों में लिखिए। किसी circuit में induced emf तब आती है जब उससे linked magnetic flux बदले, और emf उस बदलाव की rate के साथ बढ़ती है। ये वाक्य लिख दिया तो conclusion का mark पक्का।

<whisper> अब वो mark जो students अक्सर गँवाते हैं। वो लिख देते हैं कि coil के पास magnet हिलाने से current induce होता है, बस। ये experiment one का सही description है और experiment three को पूरी तरह छोड़ देता है, जो कि decisive वाला है। Examiner इसे पढ़कर conclusion का mark दे ही नहीं सकता।

आख़िर में एक detail, अगर question तीन marks का है तो एक line की क़ीमत रखती है। Joseph Henry ने यही effect America में independently देखा, और उसी से आगे बढ़कर self-induction खोजा, जो कि इस chapter के subtopic तीन का विषय है।

sections.subtopic: Experimental Foundations - The Faraday and Henry Experiments
sections.title: What the experiments are really testing you on

board_events.text: The one trap these experiments were designed to expose
A steady flux, however enormous, induces NOTHING. Only a changing flux induces an emf.
Experiment 3 exists precisely to kill the idea that a strong field or a large current is what matters.
Exam split
CBSE Boards: may ask a 2 to 3 mark describe-the-experiment or state-the-conclusion question directly.
NEET and JEE: rarely ask the experiments, but test the conclusion relentlessly, usually disguised as a numerical.
Reflex to build now: whenever a problem hands you a flux, a field, or a current, ask FIRST whether it is changing.
Relative motion is enough. Moving the magnet and moving the coil are physically the same experiment.

segments.text: Let me close this opening block by naming exactly what these experiments are testing, because they were practically designed to expose one specific misconception.
<whisper> Here it is. A steady flux, however enormous, induces nothing at all. Only a changing flux induces an emf. If you carry one sentence out of this section, carry that one.

And notice that experiment three exists precisely to kill the wrong idea. A student who believes strong field means big emf, or large current means big emf, is comfortable right up until they meet a fixed pair of coils with a large steady current and a galvanometer reading dead zero.
Now the exam split, because the three boards treat this differently and it is worth knowing where to spend effort.

C B S E may ask this directly, as a two to three mark question. Describe Faraday's experiment. Or, what do the experiments conclude. So the descriptive answer we just built is a real, bankable question, not background reading.

N E E T and J E E almost never ask you to describe the apparatus. What they do, relentlessly, is test the conclusion, usually disguised inside a numerical where the flux quietly turns out to be constant and the answer is zero.

So build this reflex now, before any formula arrives. Whenever a problem hands you a flux, a field, or a current, your first question is not what formula fits. It is: is this thing changing? If it is not, the induced emf is zero and you are already done.

One last small point that saves confusion later. Relative motion is all that matters. Moving the magnet toward the coil and moving the coil toward the magnet are not two experiments with two explanations. They are the same experiment seen from two chairs.
इस opening block को ख़त्म करते हुए ठीक-ठीक बताती हूँ कि ये experiments किस चीज़ का test हैं, क्योंकि ये लगभग एक ख़ास misconception को पकड़ने के लिए ही बने हैं।
<whisper> सुनिए। Steady flux, चाहे कितनी भी बड़ी हो, कुछ भी induce नहीं करती। सिर्फ़ बदलती हुई flux emf induce करती है। अगर इस section से एक ही वाक्य ले जाना है, तो यही ले जाइए।

और ग़ौर कीजिए कि experiment three इसी ग़लत सोच को मारने के लिए मौजूद है। जो student मानता है कि strong field मतलब बड़ी emf, या बड़ा current मतलब बड़ी emf, वो तब तक आराम में है जब तक उसे fixed coils की जोड़ी न मिले जिसमें बड़ा steady current हो और galvanometer बिलकुल zero दिखा रहा हो।
अब exam का बँटवारा, क्योंकि तीनों boards इसे अलग तरह से treat करते हैं और ये जानना ज़रूरी है कि मेहनत कहाँ लगानी है।

C B S E इसे सीधे पूछ सकता है, दो से तीन marks में। Faraday's experiment describe कीजिए। या, experiments क्या conclude करते हैं। तो जो descriptive answer हमने अभी बनाया, वो असली bankable question है, background reading नहीं।

N E E T और J E E लगभग कभी apparatus describe करने को नहीं कहते। वो जो करते हैं, लगातार करते हैं, वो है conclusion का test, अक्सर किसी numerical के भीतर छिपाकर जहाँ flux चुपचाप constant निकलती है और answer zero होता है।

तो ये reflex अभी बना लीजिए, किसी formula के आने से पहले। जब भी problem आपको flux, field, या current दे, आपका पहला सवाल ये नहीं है कि कौन सा formula लगेगा। पहला सवाल है: क्या ये चीज़ बदल रही है? अगर नहीं, तो induced emf zero है और आपका काम ख़त्म।

आख़िरी छोटी बात जो आगे confusion बचाती है। सिर्फ़ relative motion मायने रखती है। Magnet को coil की तरफ़ ले जाना और coil को magnet की तरफ़ ले जाना दो अलग experiments नहीं हैं जिनके दो explanations हों। वो एक ही experiment है, बस कुर्सी बदल गई है।

board_events.text: Flat and face-up: a lot passes through. Tilted edge-on: almost nothing.
Now swap raindrops for magnetic field lines
Magnetic flux $\Phi_B$ measures how much magnetic field passes through a given area.
A strong field threading straight through a large loop means high flux. The same field skimming parallel to the surface means ZERO flux.

segments.text: <curious> Picture yourself on a railway platform during the monsoon, holding a large empty picture frame out into the rain. Just the frame, no glass, no picture. How much rain passes through it in one second?
Think about what that depends on, because you already know the answer from experience. Three things, and only three.
How heavy the rain is coming down. How big your frame is. And how you tilt it. That is the complete list.

Look at the three frames on the board. On the left, held flat and face-up to the falling rain, a lot of water passes straight through. In the middle, tilted, less gets through. On the right, turned edge-on so the rain just grazes past, almost nothing goes through at all.

And notice the frame is exactly the same size in all three pictures. The rain is exactly as heavy. Only the tilt changed, and the amount getting through changed dramatically. Orientation is not a detail here, it is one of the three controls.
Now make one substitution and you have the physics. Swap the raindrops for magnetic field lines, and swap the picture frame for a loop of wire.
That gives us magnetic flux, written phi with a subscript B. It measures how much magnetic field passes through a given area. It is a counting of how many field lines pierce through the loop.

So a strong field threading straight through a large loop means high flux. The same field skimming parallel to the loop's surface means zero flux, because the lines slide past without piercing through at all. Same field, same loop, zero instead of maximum, purely from orientation.

<curious> ख़ुद को monsoon में railway platform पर खड़ा सोचिए, हाथ में एक बड़ा खाली picture frame है जिसे आपने बारिश में बाहर निकाला है। सिर्फ़ frame, न glass न picture. एक second में कितनी बारिश उसमें से गुज़रेगी?
सोचिए ये किस पर depend करता है, क्योंकि जवाब आपको experience से पहले से पता है। तीन चीज़ें, बस तीन।
बारिश कितनी तेज़ पड़ रही है। आपका frame कितना बड़ा है। और आपने उसे कितना tilt किया है। बस, पूरी list यही है।

Board पर तीनों frames देखिए। बाईं तरफ़, flat और ऊपर की तरफ़ मुँह किए, बहुत सारा पानी सीधा गुज़र रहा है। बीच में, tilted, कम गुज़र रहा है। दाईं तरफ़, edge-on घुमाया हुआ जहाँ बारिश बस छूकर निकल जाती है, लगभग कुछ भी नहीं गुज़रता।

और ध्यान दीजिए, frame तीनों तस्वीरों में बिलकुल उतना ही बड़ा है। बारिश भी उतनी ही तेज़ है। सिर्फ़ tilt बदला, और गुज़रने वाली मात्रा नाटकीय रूप से बदल गई। यहाँ orientation कोई detail नहीं है, वो तीन controls में से एक है।
अब एक substitution कीजिए और physics हाज़िर है। Raindrops की जगह magnetic field lines रख दीजिए, और picture frame की जगह wire का एक loop.
इससे मिलती है magnetic flux, जिसे phi with subscript B लिखते हैं। ये बताती है कि किसी दिए हुए area से कितनी magnetic field गुज़र रही है। ये गिनती है कि कितनी field lines loop को भेदकर निकल रही हैं।

तो strong field अगर बड़े loop से सीधी गुज़र रही है तो flux ज़्यादा। वही field अगर loop की surface के parallel सरक रही है तो flux zero, क्योंकि lines बिना भेदे बग़ल से निकल जाती हैं। वही field, वही loop, maximum की जगह zero, सिर्फ़ orientation की वजह से।

sections.subtopic: Magnetic Flux, Faraday's and Lenz's Laws
sections.title: Change, not amount: the observation Faraday chased for years

board_events.text: A coil, a galvanometer, and a bar magnet on a table
Nothing is happening. The galvanometer reads zero.
Push the magnet TOWARD the coil: the needle jumps.
Hold the magnet still, even right inside the coil: the needle drops back to zero.
Pull the magnet away: the needle jumps the OTHER way.
The single most important observation in this chapter
It is not the PRESENCE of a magnetic field that creates electricity in the coil. It is the CHANGE in flux through it.
Faraday's law: whenever flux linked with a circuit changes, an emf is induced, and the faster the change, the bigger the emf.

segments.text: Let me put the central observation of this chapter in front of you as plainly as I can, because everything else is downstream of it.
A small circular coil sits on a table, wired to a galvanometer. A bar magnet sits next to it. Right now nothing is happening and the galvanometer reads zero.
The instant you push the magnet towards the coil, the needle jumps. Something is driving current through that coil, and there is no battery anywhere.

<excited> Now hold the magnet still. Not far away, but right there, even parked inside the coil where the field is at its strongest. The needle drops back to zero. The field is still there. The field is still strong. And nothing is happening.
Pull the magnet away and the needle jumps the other way. So going in gives one sign, coming out gives the opposite sign. The effect tracks the motion, and dies the moment the motion dies.
Michael Faraday spent years chasing exactly this, and here is what it means. This is the single most important observation in the entire chapter, so let me say it very deliberately.
It is not the presence of a magnetic field that creates electricity in the coil. It is the change in flux through it. A steady, unchanging flux, no matter how enormous, induces nothing whatsoever.

And that gives us Faraday's law in words. Whenever the magnetic flux linked with a circuit changes, an emf is induced, meaning a voltage that can drive a current. And the faster the flux changes, the bigger that emf. A gentle, slow change gives a feeble emf. A sudden, violent change gives a strong one.
इस chapter की केंद्रीय observation को मैं जितना सीधा रख सकती हूँ उतना सीधा रखती हूँ, क्योंकि बाक़ी सब कुछ इसी से निकलता है।
एक छोटी circular coil table पर रखी है, galvanometer से जुड़ी हुई। बग़ल में एक bar magnet पड़ा है। अभी कुछ नहीं हो रहा और galvanometer zero पढ़ रहा है।
जिस पल आप magnet को coil की तरफ़ push करते हैं, needle उछल पड़ती है। कोई चीज़ उस coil में current चला रही है, और कहीं कोई battery है ही नहीं।

<excited> अब magnet को स्थिर पकड़ लीजिए। दूर नहीं, वहीं पास में, चाहे coil के अंदर ही जहाँ field सबसे strong है। Needle वापस zero पर गिर जाती है। Field अब भी मौजूद है। Field अब भी strong है। और कुछ नहीं हो रहा।
Magnet को दूर खींचिए, needle उल्टी तरफ़ उछलती है। यानी अंदर जाने पर एक sign, बाहर आने पर उल्टा sign. Effect motion के साथ चलता है, और motion ख़त्म होते ही मर जाता है।
Michael Faraday ने सालों तक ठीक इसी का पीछा किया, और इसका मतलब ये है। ये पूरे chapter की सबसे अहम observation है, तो मैं इसे बहुत सोच-समझकर कहती हूँ।
Coil में बिजली magnetic field की मौजूदगी से नहीं बनती। वो बनती है उसमें से गुज़रती flux के बदलाव से। Steady, अपरिवर्तित flux, चाहे कितनी भी बड़ी हो, कुछ भी induce नहीं करती।

और यहीं से मिलता है Faraday's law शब्दों में। जब भी किसी circuit से linked magnetic flux बदलती है, एक emf induce होती है, यानी एक voltage जो current चला सके। और flux जितनी तेज़ी से बदलेगी, वो emf उतनी बड़ी होगी। धीमा, हल्का बदलाव कमज़ोर emf देता है। अचानक, तेज़ बदलाव strong emf देता है।

board_events.text: Push a magnet's north pole toward a coil: the coil promptly turns its own near face into a north pole, to repel the intruder.
Pull the magnet away: the coil switches to a south pole, to cling on and resist the departure.
The coil always opposes whatever you are trying to do.
And this opposition is not arbitrary
It is the universe protecting conservation of energy. Lenz's law is energy conservation written into the minus sign.

segments.text: So Faraday tells us how big the induced emf is. But nature adds a twist that tells us which way it points, and that twist is Lenz's law.
Here is the statement. The induced current always flows in whatever direction fights the change that created it. Always. Without exception.
Look at the diagram. A bar magnet with its north pole facing a coil, moving towards it. Watch what the coil does in response.

The coil promptly turns its own near face into a north pole. Two north poles facing each other, and you know what that means. Repulsion. The coil is actively pushing back against the magnet you are trying to bring in.
Now reverse it. Pull the magnet away, and the coil switches its near face to a south pole, so it can cling on and resist the departure. Whatever you are doing, the coil does the opposite.
<chuckle> Think of nature as a stubborn, lazy referee who simply hates being disturbed. Push, and it pushes back. Pull, and it pulls back. It will not help you either way.
But here is the part that matters more than the picture, and it is the part students skip. This opposition is not an arbitrary rule that nature happened to pick. It could not have been otherwise.

It is the universe protecting the law of conservation of energy. If the coil helped you instead of resisting, you would get electrical energy for free. So Lenz's law is not a second law bolted onto Faraday's law. It is energy conservation written into the minus sign, and we will prove exactly that shortly.
तो Faraday बताता है कि induced emf कितनी बड़ी है। लेकिन nature एक twist जोड़ती है जो बताता है कि वो किस तरफ़ है, और वो twist है Lenz's law.
Statement ये है। Induced current हमेशा उस direction में बहता है जो उस change से लड़े जिसने उसे पैदा किया। हमेशा। बिना किसी exception के।
Diagram देखिए। एक bar magnet जिसका north pole coil की तरफ़ है, और वो coil की तरफ़ बढ़ रहा है। देखिए coil जवाब में क्या करती है।

Coil फ़ौरन अपने near face को north pole बना लेती है। दो north poles आमने-सामने, और आप जानते हैं इसका मतलब क्या है। Repulsion. Coil सक्रिय रूप से उस magnet को धकेल रही है जिसे आप अंदर लाने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं।
अब उल्टा कीजिए। Magnet को दूर खींचिए, और coil अपना near face south pole में बदल देती है, ताकि पकड़कर रोक सके। आप जो भी कर रहे हों, coil उसका उल्टा करती है।
<chuckle> Nature को एक ज़िद्दी, आलसी referee समझिए जिसे बस disturb होना पसंद नहीं। धकेलो, तो वो वापस धकेलेगा। खींचो, तो वो वापस खींचेगा। किसी भी हाल में मदद नहीं करेगा।
लेकिन अब वो हिस्सा जो तस्वीर से ज़्यादा अहम है, और यही students छोड़ देते हैं। ये opposition कोई मनमाना नियम नहीं है जो nature ने यूँ ही चुन लिया हो। ये इसके अलावा हो ही नहीं सकता था।

ये universe का conservation of energy को बचाना है। अगर coil विरोध करने की जगह आपकी मदद करती, तो आपको मुफ़्त में electrical energy मिल जाती। तो Lenz's law, Faraday's law पर चिपकाया हुआ दूसरा law नहीं है। ये minus sign में लिखा हुआ energy conservation है, और यही हम थोड़ी देर में prove करेंगे।

sections.title: The four assumptions you must respect

board_events.text: Limiting conditions on everything that follows
1. The simple formula $\Phi_B = BA\cos\theta$ assumes the field is UNIFORM across the whole area and the surface is flat.
For a non-uniform field, say near a current-carrying wire, you must integrate instead.
2. Induced emf depends only on the RATE OF CHANGE of flux. It does not depend on the resistance of the circuit.
The induced CURRENT does depend on resistance, through $I = \varepsilon/R$. A perfectly insulating loop still has an emf, but zero current.
3. A constant flux, even a huge one, produces zero emf. This is the trap that catches more students than any other in the chapter.

board_events.text: 4. The angle $\theta$ is always between $B$ and the AREA VECTOR, the normal to the surface. Never between $B$ and the plane of the loop.

segments.text: Before we write a single formula down, let me fence off the conditions under which they are valid. Four of them, and every one is a place students lose marks.
First. The simple flux formula, B A cos theta, assumes the field is uniform across the whole area and the surface is flat. That is a real restriction, not a formality.

If the field is non-uniform, say close to a current-carrying wire where the field weakens as you move away, that formula simply does not apply. You have to integrate instead, and we will do exactly that in a worked example later.

Second, and this one surprises people. The induced emf depends only on the rate of change of flux. It does not depend on the resistance of the circuit at all. Resistance never appears in Faraday's law.

The induced current, of course, does depend on resistance, through current equals emf divided by R. So here is the sharp version: a perfectly insulating loop still has a full induced emf across it, and zero current flowing. Emf and current are not the same thing, and this chapter will keep testing whether you know that.

Third. A constant flux, even a huge one, produces exactly zero emf. I have said this before and I will say it again later, because it is the trap that catches more students than any other in this chapter.

Fourth, look carefully at the figure. The angle theta is measured between the field and the area vector, which is the normal sticking out perpendicular to the surface. Never between the field and the plane of the loop.

This matters because problems love to say the field makes an angle alpha with the plane of the loop. If you plug that alpha straight in as theta, you get the wrong answer. In that case theta is ninety degrees minus alpha, and the flux becomes B A sin alpha. Read the wording every single time.
एक भी formula लिखने से पहले, मैं उन conditions की बाड़ लगा देती हूँ जिनमें ये valid हैं। चार हैं, और हर एक वो जगह है जहाँ students marks गँवाते हैं।
पहली। Simple flux formula, B A cos theta, ये मानकर चलता है कि field पूरे area पर uniform है और surface flat है। ये असली restriction है, औपचारिकता नहीं।

अगर field non-uniform है, जैसे current-carrying wire के पास जहाँ दूर जाते-जाते field कमज़ोर होती जाती है, तो वो formula चलेगा ही नहीं। वहाँ integrate करना पड़ेगा, और आगे एक worked example में हम ठीक यही करेंगे।
दूसरी, और ये लोगों को चौंकाती है। Induced emf सिर्फ़ flux के बदलने की rate पर depend करती है। Circuit की resistance पर बिलकुल नहीं। Faraday's law में resistance आती ही नहीं।

Induced current ज़रूर resistance पर depend करता है, current equals emf बटा R के ज़रिए। तो तीखा version ये है: एक perfectly insulating loop में भी पूरी induced emf मौजूद रहती है, और current zero बहता है। Emf और current एक चीज़ नहीं हैं, और ये chapter बार-बार यही test करेगा कि आप ये जानते हैं या नहीं।
तीसरी। Constant flux, चाहे कितनी भी बड़ी हो, बिलकुल zero emf देती है। ये मैं पहले भी कह चुकी हूँ और आगे भी कहूँगी, क्योंकि यही वो trap है जो इस chapter में सबसे ज़्यादा students को पकड़ता है।
चौथी, figure ध्यान से देखिए। Angle theta नापा जाता है field और area vector के बीच, यानी वो normal जो surface से perpendicular बाहर निकला है। Field और loop के plane के बीच कभी नहीं।

ये इसलिए मायने रखता है क्योंकि problems बड़े शौक़ से कहती हैं कि field, loop के plane से alpha angle बनाती है। अगर आपने वो alpha सीधे theta की जगह डाल दिया, answer ग़लत। उस case में theta होगा ninety degrees minus alpha, और flux बनेगी B A sin alpha. हर बार wording पढ़िए।

sections.subtopic: Magnetic Flux, Faraday's and Lenz's Laws
sections.title: Flux, uniform and non-uniform, and where the integral comes from

board_events.text: Magnetic flux, uniform field and flat area
Only the component of $B$ along the normal threads through. The in-plane component slides past and contributes nothing.
That perpendicular component is $B\cos\theta$, and multiplying by the area $A$ gives the result above.
Now let the field vary from point to point
Chop the surface into infinitesimal patches $d\vec{A}$, each so tiny that $B$ is effectively constant across it.
This integral form is what you reach for whenever $B$ changes from point to point. It is the central trick in JEE Advanced flux problems.

segments.text: Now let us make flux quantitative, and I want to build it rather than just hand it to you.
Here is the flux for a uniform field through a flat area. Phi B equals B dot A, the dot product of the field vector with the area vector, which works out to B A cos theta.

And the reason for the cos theta is worth seeing rather than memorising. Only the component of the field along the normal actually threads through the surface. The component lying in the plane of the surface just slides past and contributes nothing at all.

That perpendicular component has magnitude B cos theta. Multiply it by the area A and you have B A cos theta. That is the whole derivation, and it means you never have to remember whether it is sine or cosine. You can rebuild it in three seconds.
Now suppose the field is not uniform. It varies in both magnitude and direction as you move across the surface. The formula we just built assumes one single value of B, so it is dead.

The fix is the standard move of calculus. Chop the surface into infinitesimal patches, each one written d A as a vector, and each so tiny that the field is effectively constant across it. Over one tiny patch, our uniform-field formula is valid again.
The flux through one patch is B dot d A. Sum over every patch and the sum becomes an integral. Phi B equals the integral of B dot d A.

<whisper> And here is where this earns its keep. This integral form is what you reach for whenever the field changes from point to point, and it is the central trick in J E E Advanced flux problems. If you see a loop sitting near a straight current-carrying wire, this is the formula the problem wants.
अब flux को quantitative बनाते हैं, और मैं इसे बनाना चाहती हूँ, सीधे थमा देना नहीं।
Uniform field के लिए flat area से गुज़रती flux ये है। Phi B equals B dot A, यानी field vector और area vector का dot product, जो बनता है B A cos theta.

और cos theta क्यों आया, ये देखना ज़रूरी है, रटना नहीं। Surface को सिर्फ़ field का वो component भेदता है जो normal के साथ है। जो component surface के plane में पड़ा है वो बग़ल से सरक जाता है और कुछ contribute नहीं करता।

उस perpendicular component का magnitude है B cos theta. उसे area A से multiply कीजिए और मिल गया B A cos theta. यही पूरी derivation है, और इसका मतलब है कि आपको कभी याद नहीं रखना पड़ेगा कि sine आएगा या cosine. आप इसे तीन second में दोबारा बना सकते हैं।
अब मान लीजिए field uniform नहीं है। Surface पर चलते-चलते उसका magnitude भी बदलता है और direction भी। हमने जो formula बनाया वो एक ही B की value मानता है, तो वो ख़त्म।

इसका इलाज calculus की standard चाल है। Surface को बहुत छोटे-छोटे patches में काट दीजिए, हर एक को vector d A लिखिए, और हर एक इतना छोटा कि उस पर field practically constant हो। एक tiny patch पर हमारा uniform-field formula फिर से valid है।
एक patch से गुज़रती flux है B dot d A. सारे patches को जोड़िए और वो जोड़ integral बन जाता है। Phi B equals integral of B dot d A.

<whisper> और यहीं इसकी असली क़ीमत है। जब भी field एक point से दूसरे point तक बदले, आप यही integral form उठाते हैं, और यही J E E Advanced की flux problems की केंद्रीय चाल है। अगर loop किसी straight current-carrying wire के पास दिखे, तो problem यही formula माँग रही है।

sections.subtopic: Magnetic Flux, Faraday's and Lenz's Laws
sections.title: Faraday's law, induced current, induced charge, and the minus sign

board_events.text: Faraday's law of induction, single loop
For a coil of $N$ turns, Neumann's form
The minus sign is NOT a numerical factor. It is a direction-bookkeeper that encodes Lenz's law.
Units: flux in weber, where 1 Wb equals 1 T times metre squared equals 1 V times second. Dimensional formula $[ML^2T^{-2}A^{-1}]$. Induced emf in volt, $[ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}]$.

segments.text: Here is the formula sheet for this subtopic. Four equations, and I want you to see how they chain together rather than treating them as four separate things to memorise.

Faraday's law for a single loop. The induced emf equals minus the rate of change of magnetic flux. That is the entire law. Everything else in this chapter is this equation with a different thing being changed.
Now for a real coil, which has many turns. Each turn is linked by the flux, so each turn contributes its own emf, and they add.

That gives Neumann's form. Emf equals minus N times d phi B by d t. Dropping that N is a guaranteed mark loss in numericals, and it is one of the most common errors in the whole chapter. If the problem says two hundred turns, the two hundred belongs in your working.

The induced current follows from Ohm's law. Current equals the magnitude of the emf divided by R, which expands to N over R times the magnitude of the rate of change of flux. Notice R enters here and nowhere earlier.

And then this one, which is a genuine exam favourite. The total charge that flows equals N times the magnitude of the flux change, divided by R. Look carefully at what is missing from that formula: time. It is not there. We will prove why in the next section, and it is a beautiful little result.

<excited> Now the minus sign, which students mishandle constantly. It is not a numerical factor. You do not multiply anything by minus one. It is a direction-bookkeeper that encodes Lenz's law inside Faraday's law.

So when you compute a magnitude of emf, you simply drop it and reinstate direction separately using Lenz reasoning. On units, flux is measured in weber, where one weber equals one tesla metre squared, equals one volt second. Its dimensional formula is M L squared T to the minus two A to the minus one, and emf, being in volts, is M L squared T to the minus three A to the minus one.
ये रही इस subtopic की formula sheet. चार equations, और मैं चाहती हूँ आप देखें कि ये आपस में कैसे जुड़ती हैं, चार अलग-अलग चीज़ें रटने की जगह।
Single loop के लिए Faraday's law. Induced emf equals minus magnetic flux के बदलने की rate. बस, यही पूरा law है। इस chapter में बाक़ी सब इसी equation का रूप है, बस बदलने वाली चीज़ अलग होती है।
अब असली coil के लिए, जिसमें कई turns होते हैं। हर turn से flux linked है, तो हर turn अपनी emf देता है, और वो जुड़ जाती हैं।

इससे मिलती है Neumann's form. Emf equals minus N times d phi B by d t. Numericals में वो N छोड़ देना पक्का mark का नुक़सान है, और ये पूरे chapter की सबसे common ग़लतियों में से एक है। अगर problem कहती है two hundred turns, तो वो two hundred आपकी working में होना चाहिए।
Induced current Ohm's law से निकलता है। Current equals emf का magnitude बटा R, जो खुलकर बनता है N बटा R times flux के change की rate का magnitude. ग़ौर कीजिए R यहाँ आता है, इससे पहले कहीं नहीं।

और फिर ये वाला, जो exam का सच्चा favourite है। बहने वाला total charge equals N times flux change का magnitude, बटा R. ध्यान से देखिए उस formula में क्या ग़ायब है: time. है ही नहीं। अगले section में हम prove करेंगे ऐसा क्यों, और ये एक बेहद ख़ूबसूरत छोटा result है।

<excited> अब minus sign, जिसे students लगातार ग़लत handle करते हैं। ये कोई numerical factor नहीं है। आप किसी चीज़ को minus one से multiply नहीं करते। ये एक direction का हिसाब रखने वाला है जो Faraday's law के अंदर Lenz's law को encode करता है।

तो जब आप emf का magnitude निकालें, इसे बस छोड़ दीजिए और direction अलग से Lenz reasoning से तय कीजिए। Units की बात करें तो flux weber में नापी जाती है, जहाँ एक weber equals एक tesla metre squared, equals एक volt second. इसका dimensional formula है M L squared T to the minus two A to the minus one, और emf, volt में होने की वजह से, M L squared T to the minus three A to the minus one.

sections.subtopic: Magnetic Flux, Faraday's and Lenz's Laws
sections.title: Board derivation: why total charge does not care about time

board_events.text: Start from Faraday's law for $N$ turns
The induced current is $I = \varepsilon/R$, so the charge flowing in a small time $dt$ is $dq = I\,dt$.
The $dt$ cancels completely. That cancellation is the whole result.
Now integrate from the initial state to the final state:
Whether you yank the magnet out in a flash or ease it out slowly, the SAME total charge flows.

segments.text: This derivation is short, it is beautiful, and it is an exam favourite. It also gives you a shortcut that saves real time under pressure, so follow it closely.
We start where we always start, with Faraday's law for N turns. Emf equals minus N times the rate of change of flux.
Now bring in the circuit. The induced current is emf divided by R, and charge is current times time, so the charge that flows in a small time d t is d q equals I d t.
Substitute Faraday's law into that. You get d q equals emf over R d t, which is minus N over R times d phi B by d t, all multiplied by d t.

<excited> And now watch the d t. It appears in the denominator of the rate, and it appears again as the multiplier. They cancel completely. What is left is d q equals minus N over R times d phi B, with no time in it at all. That cancellation is the entire result.
Now integrate both sides, from the initial flux to the final flux. The right side is just the integral of d phi B, which is simply the total change in flux.

And out comes the answer. q equals N times the change in flux, divided by R. Look at what that formula contains: the number of turns, the net flux change, and the resistance. Look at what it does not contain: how long the change took, or how the flux varied along the way.

The physical insight is genuinely remarkable. Whether you yank the magnet out in a flash or ease it out slowly, exactly the same total charge flows. A fast pull gives a large current for a short time. A slow pull gives a small current for a long time. And they balance out exactly.
ये derivation छोटी है, ख़ूबसूरत है, और exam की favourite है। ये आपको एक ऐसा shortcut भी देती है जो pressure में असली time बचाता है, तो ध्यान से चलिए।
शुरुआत वहीं से जहाँ हमेशा करते हैं, N turns के लिए Faraday's law. Emf equals minus N times flux के बदलने की rate.
अब circuit को शामिल कीजिए। Induced current है emf बटा R, और charge होता है current into time, तो छोटे से time d t में बहने वाला charge है d q equals I d t.
उसमें Faraday's law डालिए। मिलता है d q equals emf बटा R d t, यानी minus N बटा R times d phi B by d t, और ये सब d t से multiplied.

<excited> अब d t पर नज़र रखिए। वो rate के denominator में है, और फिर multiplier के रूप में भी है। दोनों पूरी तरह cancel हो जाते हैं। जो बचता है वो है d q equals minus N बटा R times d phi B, जिसमें time है ही नहीं। वही cancellation पूरा result है।
अब दोनों तरफ़ integrate कीजिए, initial flux से final flux तक। दाईं तरफ़ सिर्फ़ d phi B का integral है, जो बस flux का कुल बदलाव है।

और जवाब सामने है। q equals N times flux का change, बटा R. देखिए उस formula में क्या है: turns की संख्या, net flux change, और resistance. और देखिए क्या नहीं है: बदलाव में कितना time लगा, या रास्ते में flux कैसे बदली।

इसकी physical insight वाक़ई remarkable है। चाहे आप magnet को झटके से बाहर खींचें या धीरे-धीरे निकालें, बिलकुल उतना ही total charge बहता है। तेज़ खींचने पर थोड़े time के लिए बड़ा current. धीरे खींचने पर ज़्यादा time के लिए छोटा current. और दोनों ठीक-ठीक बराबर हो जाते हैं।

sections.subtopic: Magnetic Flux, Faraday's and Lenz's Laws
sections.title: Board derivation: Lenz's law forced by conservation of energy

board_events.text: Suppose, for contradiction, that the induced current AIDED the change
Push a magnet toward a coil. The induced current would create a face that ATTRACTS the magnet.
That pulls it in faster, which induces a still larger current, which attracts it harder still.
An ever-accelerating magnet generating ever-growing electrical energy out of nothing. A perpetual motion machine.
Forbidden by conservation of energy. So the assumption is false: the induced current MUST oppose the change.
Where the electrical energy actually comes from
Because the coil opposes it, you must do work to push the magnet in. That mechanical work you supply is exactly the source of the electrical energy in the circuit.
Lenz's law is therefore not an independent rule bolted on top of Faraday's law. It is energy conservation written into the minus sign.

segments.text: Earlier I promised that Lenz's law is not an arbitrary rule. Let me now make good on that, with a proof by contradiction that C B S E genuinely asks for.
We suppose the opposite of what Lenz says, and we follow it until it breaks. So suppose the induced current aided the change instead of opposing it.
Push a magnet toward a coil. Under our false assumption, the induced current creates a face that attracts the magnet rather than repelling it.

Follow the consequence carefully, because it runs away fast. Attraction pulls the magnet in faster. Faster motion means a faster-changing flux, which induces a still larger current. A larger current means a stronger attraction, which pulls it in faster still.

<excited> And there is the absurdity. You have an ever-accelerating magnet generating ever-growing electrical energy, and nobody is supplying anything. That is a perpetual motion machine, producing energy out of nothing.

Conservation of energy forbids it absolutely. So our assumption was false, and there is only one alternative left. The induced current must oppose the change that created it. Lenz's law is not chosen, it is forced.
Now turn it around and ask the honest question: where does the electrical energy actually come from? Because it is real energy, dissipating as heat in the resistance.

Here is the answer. Precisely because the coil opposes you, you have to do work to push that magnet in against the opposition. That mechanical work from your hand is exactly the source of the electrical energy appearing in the circuit. Nothing is free. Lenz's law is not an independent rule bolted on top of Faraday's law. It is energy conservation, written into the minus sign.
पहले मैंने वादा किया था कि Lenz's law कोई मनमाना नियम नहीं है। अब उसे पूरा करती हूँ, एक proof by contradiction से जो C B S E सचमुच पूछता है।
हम वही मान लेते हैं जो Lenz कहता है उसका उल्टा, और उसे तब तक चलाते हैं जब तक वो टूट न जाए। तो मानिए कि induced current change का विरोध करने की जगह उसकी मदद करता है।
एक magnet को coil की तरफ़ धकेलिए। हमारी झूठी assumption के तहत, induced current ऐसा face बनाएगा जो magnet को repel करने की जगह attract करे।

अब नतीजे को ध्यान से follow कीजिए, क्योंकि ये तेज़ी से हाथ से निकल जाता है। Attraction magnet को और तेज़ खींचता है। ज़्यादा तेज़ motion यानी और तेज़ी से बदलती flux, जो और बड़ा current induce करती है। बड़ा current यानी और strong attraction, जो और तेज़ खींचता है।

<excited> और यही बेतुकापन है। आपके पास एक लगातार तेज़ होता magnet है जो लगातार बढ़ती electrical energy पैदा कर रहा है, और कोई कुछ दे नहीं रहा। ये perpetual motion machine है, जो शून्य से energy बना रही है।

Conservation of energy इसे बिलकुल मना करता है। तो हमारी assumption ग़लत थी, और अब सिर्फ़ एक ही विकल्प बचा। Induced current को उस change का विरोध करना ही होगा जिसने उसे पैदा किया। Lenz's law चुना नहीं गया, वो मजबूरी है।
अब इसे पलटिए और ईमानदार सवाल पूछिए: electrical energy असल में आती कहाँ से है? क्योंकि वो असली energy है, जो resistance में heat बनकर निकलती है।

जवाब ये है। ठीक इसीलिए कि coil आपका विरोध करती है, आपको उस विरोध के ख़िलाफ़ magnet को धकेलने में काम करना पड़ता है। आपके हाथ का वही mechanical work, circuit में आने वाली electrical energy का असली स्रोत है। कुछ भी मुफ़्त नहीं। Lenz's law, Faraday's law पर चिपकाया हुआ अलग नियम नहीं है। ये minus sign में लिखा energy conservation है।

board_events.text: Find (a) the initial flux through one turn, and (b) the magnitude of the induced emf.
Given: N = 200, r = 0.050 m, B = 0.40 T, theta = 0 degrees, and a time interval of 0.20 s.

segments.text: Let us put Faraday's law to work on a clean C B S E level numerical, and I want you to watch the presentation as much as the physics, because presentation is where these marks are won.

A circular coil of two hundred turns, radius five point zero centimetres. Its plane sits perpendicular to a uniform field of zero point four zero tesla, and we are told the field points along the area vector.

Look at the figure. Field lines threading straight through the coil on the left, and on the right the field has gone, dashed outline, nothing left. The field is steadily reduced to zero in zero point two zero seconds.
Two parts. Find the initial flux through one turn, and find the magnitude of the induced emf. Notice the phrase through one turn, that is deliberate, and it separates flux from flux linkage.

Write your given values first. Two hundred turns. Radius zero point zero five zero metres, converted from centimetres immediately. Field zero point four zero tesla. Theta is zero degrees, because the field lies along the area vector. Time interval zero point two zero seconds. Stating theta explicitly is worth a mark on its own.
Part a, and start with the area. Area equals pi r squared, which is pi times zero point zero five zero squared, giving seven point eight five times ten to the minus three square metres.

Now the flux. B A cos of zero degrees, and cos zero is one, so it is just zero point four zero times seven point eight five times ten to the minus three. That gives three point one four times ten to the minus three weber.

Part b, and here is the key reading. The flux falls from that value all the way to zero, so the magnitude of the change equals the whole initial flux. Emf is N times that change divided by the time: two hundred times three point one four times ten to the minus three, divided by zero point two zero, giving three point one four volts. Stating the angle, substituting cleanly, and tracking units is what carries the marks here.
अब Faraday's law को एक साफ़-सुथरे C B S E level numerical पर लगाते हैं, और मैं चाहती हूँ आप physics जितना ही ध्यान presentation पर दें, क्योंकि marks वहीं बनते हैं।
एक circular coil, two hundred turns, radius five point zero centimetres. इसका plane zero point four zero tesla की uniform field के perpendicular है, और बताया गया है कि field, area vector के साथ है।
Figure देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ field lines सीधी coil से गुज़र रही हैं, और दाईं तरफ़ field जा चुकी है, dashed outline, कुछ नहीं बचा। Field को zero point two zero seconds में steadily zero कर दिया जाता है।
दो parts. एक turn से गुज़रती initial flux निकालिए, और induced emf का magnitude निकालिए। ग़ौर कीजिए ये जो कहा गया है through one turn, ये जानबूझकर है, और यही flux को flux linkage से अलग करता है।

पहले अपनी given values लिखिए। Two hundred turns. Radius zero point zero five zero metres, centimetre से तुरंत convert किया हुआ। Field zero point four zero tesla. Theta है zero degrees, क्योंकि field area vector के साथ है। Time interval zero point two zero seconds. Theta को explicitly लिखना अपने आप में एक mark का है।
Part a, और शुरुआत area से। Area equals pi r squared, यानी pi times zero point zero five zero squared, जो देता है seven point eight five times ten to the minus three square metres.

अब flux. B A cos zero degrees, और cos zero होता है one, तो बस zero point four zero times seven point eight five times ten to the minus three. मिलता है three point one four times ten to the minus three weber.

Part b, और यहाँ असली पढ़ाई है। Flux उस value से गिरकर पूरी zero हो जाती है, तो change का magnitude पूरी initial flux के बराबर है। Emf है N times वो change बटा time: two hundred times three point one four times ten to the minus three, बटा zero point two zero, यानी three point one four volts. Angle लिखना, साफ़ substitution करना, और units track करना, यही यहाँ marks दिलाता है।

board_events.text: The trap: students see loop moving in a magnetic field and instantly write emf = Blv = 0.50 times 0.10 times 2.0 = 0.10 V.
The fast, correct read
Ask ONE question: does the flux change? The loop is always fully inside a uniform field, so the number of lines threading it is constant.
Motional emf appears only at a BOUNDARY, where the loop's area inside the field is changing. Speed rule: never compute. First check whether the flux actually changes.

segments.text: Now a N E E T style question, and this one is a pure trap. It is designed so that the student who knows more formulas gets it wrong faster.

A square conducting loop of area one hundred square centimetres lies entirely inside a large region of uniform magnetic field of zero point five zero tesla. The loop is pushed across the region at a steady two point zero metres per second, and crucially, it never crosses the boundary.
Look at the diagram. Field crosses everywhere, uniform, filling the whole region. The loop starts on the left, ends up on the right, and at every moment it is completely surrounded by field.

<curious> Here is the trap, and it is beautifully set. A student sees the words loop moving in a magnetic field, and their hand writes emf equals B l v before their brain engages. Zero point five zero times zero point one zero times two point zero, giving zero point one zero volts. Confident, fast, and completely wrong.
So let me give you the correct reading, and it takes about three seconds once you have the habit.
Ask one question and one question only. Does the flux change? Not is something moving. Not is there a field. Does the flux change.

The loop is always fully inside a uniform field. So the number of field lines threading it is exactly the same at every instant. Flux equals B A, and both B and A are constant, so the rate of change of flux is zero, and therefore the emf is zero. That is the entire solution.

<whisper> And now the general lesson, which is worth far more than this one question. Motional emf appears only at a boundary, where the loop's area inside the field is changing. Inside a uniform field, motion at any speed whatsoever induces nothing. So your speed rule is: never compute first. First check whether B A cos theta actually changes.
अब एक N E E T style question, और ये शुद्ध trap है। ये इस तरह बना है कि जिस student को ज़्यादा formulas आते हैं, वो और तेज़ी से ग़लत करता है।

एक square conducting loop जिसका area one hundred square centimetres है, वो zero point five zero tesla की uniform field के बड़े region के पूरी तरह अंदर पड़ा है। Loop को steady two point zero metres per second से region के आर-पार धकेला जाता है, और अहम बात, वो boundary कभी पार नहीं करता।
Diagram देखिए। हर जगह field के cross, uniform, पूरे region में भरे हुए। Loop बाईं तरफ़ से शुरू होकर दाईं तरफ़ पहुँचता है, और हर पल पूरी तरह field से घिरा रहता है।

<curious> अब trap देखिए, बड़ी सफ़ाई से बिछाया गया है। Student शब्द पढ़ता है loop moving in a magnetic field, और दिमाग़ चलने से पहले हाथ लिख देता है emf equals B l v. Zero point five zero times zero point one zero times two point zero, यानी zero point one zero volts. Confident, तेज़, और बिलकुल ग़लत।
तो मैं आपको सही पढ़ाई बताती हूँ, और आदत पड़ जाए तो इसमें तीन second लगते हैं।
एक सवाल पूछिए, बस एक। क्या flux बदल रही है? ये नहीं कि कुछ हिल रहा है क्या। ये नहीं कि field है क्या। बस, क्या flux बदल रही है।

Loop हमेशा uniform field के पूरी तरह अंदर है। तो उसे भेदने वाली field lines की संख्या हर पल बिलकुल वही है। Flux equals B A, और B तथा A दोनों constant हैं, तो flux के बदलने की rate zero है, इसलिए emf zero है। बस, यही पूरा solution है।

<whisper> और अब असली सबक़, जो इस एक question से कहीं ज़्यादा क़ीमती है। Motional emf सिर्फ़ boundary पर आती है, जहाँ field के अंदर loop का area बदल रहा हो। Uniform field के अंदर, किसी भी speed पर motion कुछ भी induce नहीं करती। तो आपका speed rule ये है: पहले calculate मत कीजिए। पहले check कीजिए कि B A cos theta सचमुच बदल रही है या नहीं।

sections.title: JEE Main level: a decaying field, and the heat it generates

board_events.text: N = 50 turns, area A = 200 cm squared, total resistance R = 10 ohm
The coil's plane is perpendicular to a field that decreases uniformly as B of t equals 0.60 minus 0.20 t tesla, with t in seconds.
Find (a) the induced emf, (b) the induced current, and (c) the total heat dissipated by the time the field reaches zero.
Convert first: A = 200 cm squared = 0.020 m squared. And the rate of change dB/dt = minus 0.20 T per second, read straight off the coefficient of t.
For part (c) you need the DURATION. The field goes from 0.60 T to zero at 0.20 T per second, so t = 3.0 s.

segments.text: This problem links Faraday's law with Joule heating, which is a very common J E E Main fusion. Two topics, one question.

A coil of fifty turns, area two hundred square centimetres, total resistance ten ohms. Its plane is perpendicular to a field that decreases uniformly, given as B of t equals zero point six zero minus zero point two zero t tesla, with t in seconds.
Three parts: the induced emf, the induced current, and the total heat dissipated by the time the field reaches zero.

Do your conversions before anything else. Two hundred square centimetres is zero point zero two zero square metres. And read the rate of change straight off the expression: the coefficient of t is minus zero point two zero, so d B by d t is minus zero point two zero tesla per second. It is constant, which makes everything after this easy.

Now the emf. Flux per turn is B A, and A is fixed, so the rate of change of flux is A times d B by d t. Multiply by N: fifty times zero point zero two zero times zero point two zero, giving zero point two zero volts.
Current follows immediately from Ohm's law. Zero point two zero divided by ten equals zero point zero two zero amperes, which is twenty milliamperes.
<curious> Now part c, and this is where the problem actually bites. Heat needs power multiplied by time, and nobody has given you the time. You have to find it from the physics.

The field starts at zero point six zero tesla and falls at zero point two zero tesla per second, so it takes zero point six zero divided by zero point two zero, which is three point zero seconds, to reach zero. And because the emf and current are constant throughout, heat is simply I squared R t: zero point zero two zero squared times ten times three point zero, giving zero point zero one two joules, or twelve millijoules.
ये problem Faraday's law को Joule heating से जोड़ती है, जो J E E Main का बहुत common fusion है। दो topics, एक question.

एक coil, fifty turns, area two hundred square centimetres, total resistance ten ohms. इसका plane उस field के perpendicular है जो uniformly घट रही है, दी गई है B of t equals zero point six zero minus zero point two zero t tesla, जहाँ t seconds में है।
तीन parts: induced emf, induced current, और field के zero तक पहुँचने तक dissipate होने वाली total heat.

सबसे पहले conversions कर लीजिए। Two hundred square centimetres यानी zero point zero two zero square metres. और rate of change सीधे expression से पढ़ लीजिए: t का coefficient है minus zero point two zero, तो d B by d t है minus zero point two zero tesla per second. ये constant है, जिससे आगे सब आसान हो जाता है।

अब emf. एक turn की flux है B A, और A fixed है, तो flux के बदलने की rate है A times d B by d t. N से multiply कीजिए: fifty times zero point zero two zero times zero point two zero, यानी zero point two zero volts.
Current तुरंत Ohm's law से मिलता है। Zero point two zero बटा ten equals zero point zero two zero amperes, यानी twenty milliamperes.
<curious> अब part c, और असली पेच यहीं है। Heat के लिए power into time चाहिए, और time किसी ने दिया ही नहीं। वो आपको physics से निकालना है।

Field शुरू होती है zero point six zero tesla से और zero point two zero tesla per second की दर से गिरती है, तो zero तक पहुँचने में लगते हैं zero point six zero बटा zero point two zero, यानी three point zero seconds. और चूँकि emf और current पूरे वक़्त constant हैं, heat बस I squared R t है: zero point zero two zero squared times ten times three point zero, यानी zero point zero one two joules, या twelve millijoules.

board_events.text: Why integration is unavoidable: the wire's field, mu-nought I over 2 pi r, is NON-uniform. So B A cos theta does not apply.
Take a thin vertical strip of width dr at distance r from the wire. Its area is L dr, and the field is essentially uniform across it.

segments.text: This is the J E E Advanced flavour of flux, and it is where that integral form finally earns its place. Look at the figure before we start, because the geometry is the whole problem.

A long straight wire carries current upward. To its right, in the same plane, sits a rectangular loop. Its long side, length zero point three zero metres, runs parallel to the wire. The near edge is at distance zero point zero two zero metres from the wire, and the loop is zero point zero eight zero metres wide, measured away from the wire.

Now, why can we not just use B A cos theta? Because the wire's field is mu nought I over two pi r. It falls off with distance. It is strong at the near edge and noticeably weaker at the far edge, so there is no single value of B to multiply by the area. That is what forces the integral.

So we choose our element the way the geometry suggests. Take a thin vertical strip of width d r, at distance r from the wire, running the full length L. Its area is L d r, and because the strip is thin, the field is essentially uniform across it.

The flux through that one strip is B of r times L d r. Now integrate r from the near edge at c out to the far edge at c plus a. The one over r integrates to a natural logarithm, which is why log appears in the answer.

Substituting, mu nought I nought L over two pi comes out to six point zero times ten to the minus seven. And the logarithm is of zero point one zero zero over zero point zero two zero, which is log of five, equal to one point six zero nine. Multiplying gives nine point six six times ten to the minus seven weber, roughly zero point nine seven microweber.

For part b the current now increases at twenty five amperes per second. And here is the shortcut worth seeing. Flux is directly proportional to current, so you simply replace I nought by d I by d t in the same expression. That gives six point zero times ten to the minus eight, times one point six zero nine, times twenty five, which is about two point four microvolts.

<whisper> Two closing points. On direction, the current in the wire is increasing, so the flux through the loop is increasing, and by Lenz's law the induced current flows so as to oppose that, creating a field inside the loop that pushes the flux back down. And notice the quantity we factored out, flux divided by current. That is precisely the mutual inductance between the wire and the loop, which is exactly where subtopic three of this chapter is heading.
ये flux का J E E Advanced वाला रूप है, और यहीं वो integral form अपनी जगह बनाता है। शुरू करने से पहले figure देख लीजिए, क्योंकि geometry ही पूरी problem है।

एक लंबी straight wire में ऊपर की तरफ़ current बह रहा है। उसके दाईं तरफ़, उसी plane में, एक rectangular loop रखा है। उसकी लंबी side, length zero point three zero metres, wire के parallel है। पास वाला किनारा wire से zero point zero two zero metres दूर है, और loop की चौड़ाई zero point zero eight zero metres है, wire से दूर की तरफ़ नापी हुई।

अब, हम सीधे B A cos theta क्यों नहीं लगा सकते? क्योंकि wire की field है mu nought I बटा two pi r. वो दूरी के साथ घटती है। पास वाले किनारे पर strong है और दूर वाले किनारे पर साफ़ तौर पर कमज़ोर, तो B की कोई एक value है ही नहीं जिसे area से multiply करें। यही integral को मजबूरी बनाता है।

तो हम अपना element वैसे चुनते हैं जैसा geometry कहती है। एक पतली vertical strip लीजिए, चौड़ाई d r, wire से r दूरी पर, पूरी length L तक फैली हुई। उसका area है L d r, और strip पतली होने की वजह से field उस पर practically uniform है।

उस एक strip से गुज़रती flux है B of r times L d r. अब r को integrate कीजिए, पास वाले किनारे c से दूर वाले किनारे c plus a तक। One over r का integral natural logarithm देता है, इसीलिए answer में log आता है।

Substitute करने पर, mu nought I nought L बटा two pi निकलता है six point zero times ten to the minus seven. और logarithm है zero point one zero zero बटा zero point zero two zero का, यानी log of five, जो है one point six zero nine. Multiply करने पर मिलता है nine point six six times ten to the minus seven weber, लगभग zero point nine seven microweber.

Part b में current अब twenty five amperes per second की दर से बढ़ रहा है। और यहाँ वो shortcut है जो देखने लायक़ है। Flux सीधे current के proportional है, तो उसी expression में I nought की जगह d I by d t रख दीजिए। मिलता है six point zero times ten to the minus eight, times one point six zero nine, times twenty five, यानी लगभग two point four microvolts.

<whisper> दो आख़िरी बातें। Direction की बात करें तो wire में current बढ़ रहा है, इसलिए loop से गुज़रती flux बढ़ रही है, और Lenz's law के मुताबिक़ induced current इस तरह बहेगा कि उसका विरोध करे, loop के अंदर ऐसी field बनाकर जो flux को वापस नीचे धकेले। और ग़ौर कीजिए जो quantity हमने बाहर निकाली, flux बटा current. वो ठीक-ठीक wire और loop के बीच की mutual inductance है, और chapter का subtopic तीन वहीं जा रहा है।

sections.subtopic: Magnetic Flux, Faraday's and Lenz's Laws
sections.title: The four pitfalls, and two shortcuts that save 30 seconds each

board_events.text: Pitfall 1: mistaking flux for emf
A large flux does NOT mean a large emf. Only a CHANGING flux induces emf. See a flux value, immediately ask: is it changing?
Pitfall 2: the angle confusion

Theta in $\Phi = BA\cos\theta$ is between $B$ and the area vector, not the plane. If a problem says the field makes angle alpha with the PLANE, then theta = 90 degrees minus alpha, and $\Phi = BA\sin\alpha$.
Pitfall 3: dropping the number of turns
For an N-turn coil the emf is N times bigger. Forgetting the N is a guaranteed mark loss in numericals.
Pitfall 4: misreading the minus sign
The negative sign in Faraday's law is not a number you carry into arithmetic. It is a direction rule. Compute the magnitude, then assign direction separately.

Pro-tip: for any charge-that-flows question, skip emf and current entirely. Go straight to q = N delta-phi over R. And for field at angle alpha to the plane, reach for sin alpha directly. Both save 30 to 40 seconds in NEET and JEE Main.

segments.text: Let me consolidate the four ways students lose marks in this subtopic, then hand you two shortcuts that genuinely buy back time in the exam.

Pitfall one, and it is the biggest in the chapter. Mistaking flux for emf. A large flux does not mean a large emf. Only a changing flux induces emf at all. So build this habit: whenever you see a flux value written in a problem, immediately ask whether it is changing, before you do anything else.
Pitfall two, the angle confusion, which we have met before and which keeps claiming victims.

Theta in the flux formula is the angle between the field and the area vector, the normal. Not the plane of the loop. So if a problem says the field makes an angle alpha with the plane, then theta is ninety degrees minus alpha, and the flux becomes B A sin alpha. Read the wording, decide which angle you have been handed, then write the formula.
Pitfall three, and this one is pure carelessness rather than misunderstanding. Dropping the number of turns.

For an N turn coil the emf is N times bigger. If a problem hands you two hundred turns and your answer does not contain a factor of two hundred, you have lost the mark. Circle the N in the question before you start.
Pitfall four, misreading the minus sign, and this one is about method rather than memory.

The negative sign in Faraday's law is not a number you carry into arithmetic. It is a direction rule, and it is Lenz's law in disguise. Compute the magnitude first, then assign the direction separately by asking what the induced current must oppose.

<whisper> Now the two shortcuts, and both are worth real seconds. First: for any question asking what charge flows, skip emf and skip current entirely. Go straight to q equals N delta phi over R. Second: when a field is given at angle alpha to the plane, reach for sin alpha directly instead of converting to the normal angle every time. Each of those saves thirty to forty seconds under N E E T and J E E Main pressure, and in those exams seconds are marks.
अब इस subtopic में marks गँवाने के चार तरीक़े एक साथ रख देती हूँ, फिर दो shortcuts दूँगी जो exam में सचमुच time वापस दिलाते हैं।

Pitfall एक, और यही chapter की सबसे बड़ी है। Flux को emf समझ लेना। बड़ी flux का मतलब बड़ी emf नहीं है। सिर्फ़ बदलती हुई flux ही emf induce करती है। तो ये आदत बनाइए: problem में जब भी flux की कोई value दिखे, सबसे पहले पूछिए कि वो बदल रही है या नहीं, बाक़ी सब बाद में।
Pitfall दो, angle की उलझन, जो हम पहले भी मिल चुके हैं और जो लगातार शिकार लेती रहती है।

Flux formula में theta है field और area vector यानी normal के बीच का angle. Loop के plane के साथ नहीं। तो अगर problem कहे कि field, plane के साथ alpha angle बनाती है, तो theta होगा ninety degrees minus alpha, और flux बनेगी B A sin alpha. Wording पढ़िए, तय कीजिए कौन सा angle दिया गया है, फिर formula लिखिए।
Pitfall तीन, और ये नासमझी नहीं, शुद्ध लापरवाही है। Turns की संख्या छोड़ देना।
N turn coil के लिए emf N गुना बड़ी होती है। अगर problem two hundred turns देती है और आपके answer में two hundred का factor नहीं है, तो mark गया। शुरू करने से पहले question में N पर गोला लगा दीजिए।
Pitfall चार, minus sign को ग़लत पढ़ना, और ये याददाश्त से ज़्यादा तरीक़े की बात है।

Faraday's law का negative sign कोई number नहीं है जिसे आप arithmetic में ले जाएँ। वो direction का नियम है, और भेस बदले हुए Lenz's law है। पहले magnitude निकालिए, फिर अलग से direction तय कीजिए ये पूछकर कि induced current किस चीज़ का विरोध करेगा।

<whisper> अब दो shortcuts, और दोनों असली seconds की क़ीमत रखते हैं। पहला: जो भी question पूछे कि कितना charge बहा, emf और current दोनों छोड़ दीजिए। सीधे q equals N delta phi बटा R पर जाइए। दूसरा: जब field, plane से alpha angle पर दी हो, हर बार normal angle में बदलने की जगह सीधे sin alpha उठाइए। इनमें से हर एक N E E T और J E E Main के दबाव में तीस से चालीस seconds बचाता है, और उन exams में seconds ही marks हैं।

sections.title: Move the conductor instead: the rod that becomes a battery

board_events.text: Last subtopic we changed the flux by changing the FIELD
Now we keep the field steady and move the CONDUCTOR instead. The same magic happens: an emf appears.
Forget loops for a moment. Look at a single metal rod sliding through a magnetic field.

board_events.text: A metal rod is packed with free electrons. Picture them as passengers standing in a moving local train.
The instant the train moves sideways through a field, every passenger feels an invisible shove along the length of the carriage: the Lorentz force, $F = q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$.
Electrons pile up at one end, leaving the other end positive. The rod has spontaneously turned into a tiny battery.
This voltage across its ends is the MOTIONAL EMF: emf generated by motion rather than by a time-varying field.

segments.text: In the last subtopic we changed the flux by changing the field. The magnet moved, the current switched, the field itself varied. Now we do something different.
We keep the field completely steady, and we move the conductor instead. And the same magic happens. An emf appears. Same law underneath, different variable being changed.
To see why, forget loops and circuits for a moment. Look at just a single metal rod sliding through a magnetic field. No wires attached, nothing else in the picture.
Study the diagram. A rod sitting in a field that points into the page, and the rod is moving to the right with velocity v. That is the whole setup.
Now, a metal rod is packed with free electrons, which is what makes it a conductor at all. Picture those electrons as passengers standing inside a moving local train, and the rod is the train.

<excited> The instant that train moves sideways through a magnetic field, every single passenger feels an invisible shove along the length of the carriage. That shove is the magnetic force, q v cross B, the Lorentz force you already know from the previous chapter.

So all the electrons get pushed toward one end of the rod and pile up there, which leaves the other end short of electrons, and therefore positive. Look at the plus signs at the top of the rod and the minus signs at the bottom.

And now look at what you have. Positive at one end, negative at the other, with a voltage between them. The rod has spontaneously turned into a tiny battery, with no chemistry and no external source. That voltage across its ends is the motional emf, emf generated by motion rather than by a time-varying field.
पिछले subtopic में हमने field बदलकर flux बदली थी। Magnet हिला, current switch हुआ, field ख़ुद बदली। अब हम कुछ अलग करते हैं।
हम field को पूरी तरह steady रखेंगे, और conductor को हिलाएँगे। और वही जादू होता है। Emf आ जाती है। नीचे law वही है, बस बदलने वाला variable अलग है।
समझने के लिए, थोड़ी देर के लिए loops और circuits भूल जाइए। सिर्फ़ एक metal rod देखिए जो magnetic field में सरक रहा है। कोई तार जुड़ा नहीं, तस्वीर में और कुछ नहीं।
Diagram देखिए। एक rod उस field में रखा है जो page के अंदर जा रही है, और rod दाईं तरफ़ velocity v से चल रहा है। बस, यही पूरा setup है।
अब, metal rod free electrons से भरा होता है, इसी वजह से वो conductor है। उन electrons को चलती हुई local train में खड़े passengers की तरह सोचिए, और rod वो train है।

<excited> जिस पल वो train magnetic field में बग़ल की तरफ़ चलती है, हर एक passenger को carriage की लंबाई के साथ एक अदृश्य धक्का महसूस होता है। वो धक्का है magnetic force, q v cross B, वही Lorentz force जो आप पिछले chapter से जानते हैं।

तो सारे electrons rod के एक सिरे की तरफ़ धकेल दिए जाते हैं और वहाँ जमा हो जाते हैं, जिससे दूसरा सिरा electrons की कमी में आ जाता है, यानी positive. Rod के ऊपर plus के निशान और नीचे minus के निशान देखिए।

और अब देखिए आपके पास क्या है। एक सिरा positive, दूसरा negative, और बीच में voltage. Rod अपने आप एक छोटी battery बन गया है, बिना किसी chemistry के, बिना किसी बाहरी source के। सिरों के बीच का वही voltage है motional emf, यानी motion से पैदा हुई emf, न कि समय के साथ बदलती field से।
