board_events.text: The rod's battery action drives a current around the loop, and the bulb glows. You have built the simplest possible electric generator.
The moment you stop pushing, the current dies.
And while you push, you can FEEL a resistance fighting you. That is Lenz's law again: the induced current creates a force opposing your push.
Follow the energy
The mechanical work of your hand is converted, rail by rail, into electrical energy and finally into heat in the resistor. No work, no electricity. Energy is strictly conserved.

segments.text: A single rod with a voltage across its ends is interesting, but it does not yet do anything useful. Let us close a circuit and turn it into a machine.

Lay two parallel conducting rails on a table. Bridge them with our sliding rod, and close the circuit at the far end with a resistor. Now push the rod along the rails, through a magnetic field pointing into the page.
Look at the picture. Two rails, the rod sitting across them in red, the resistor closing the loop on the left, and the whole thing sitting in a field.

The rod's battery action now has somewhere to send its current. Charge flows around the complete loop, through the rails, through the resistor, and back. Put a bulb there and it glows. You have built the simplest possible electric generator, and it has almost no parts.
Now here are two things you would notice immediately if you actually did this on a bench. First, the moment you stop pushing, the current dies. Not fades slowly, dies. No motion, no emf, no current.

<curious> Second, and this is the interesting one. While you push, you can physically feel a resistance fighting you. The rod is harder to move than it would be with the field switched off. Where is that coming from?

It is Lenz's law again, showing up as a force this time. The induced current in the rod sits in a magnetic field, so it experiences a force, and that force points backwards, opposing your push. The generator resists being driven.

So follow the energy all the way through, because this is the honest accounting. The mechanical work of your hand is converted, rail by rail, into electrical energy in the circuit, and finally into heat in the resistor. No work, no electricity. Energy is strictly conserved, and we will prove that quantitatively in a few sections.
एक rod जिसके सिरों पर voltage है, दिलचस्प तो है, लेकिन अभी कुछ काम का नहीं। चलिए circuit पूरा करके इसे एक machine बनाते हैं।

Table पर दो parallel conducting rails बिछा दीजिए। उन पर हमारा sliding rod रख दीजिए, और दूसरे सिरे पर एक resistor लगाकर circuit पूरा कर दीजिए। अब rod को rails पर धकेलिए, उस magnetic field में जो page के अंदर जा रही है।
तस्वीर देखिए। दो rails, उन पर आड़ा रखा लाल rod, बाईं तरफ़ loop बंद करता resistor, और पूरा setup field के अंदर।

अब rod की battery वाली हरकत के पास current भेजने की जगह है। Charge पूरे loop में बहता है, rails से होकर, resistor से होकर, और वापस। वहाँ bulb लगा दीजिए तो जल उठेगा। आपने सबसे simple electric generator बना लिया है, और इसमें लगभग कोई part है ही नहीं।
अब दो बातें जो bench पर सचमुच करने से आपको तुरंत दिखेंगी। पहली, जिस पल आप धकेलना बंद करते हैं, current मर जाता है। धीरे-धीरे कम नहीं होता, मर जाता है। न motion, न emf, न current.
<curious> दूसरी, और ये दिलचस्प है। धकेलते वक़्त आपको साफ़ महसूस होता है कि कोई चीज़ आपसे लड़ रही है। Field बंद होने के मुक़ाबले rod को हिलाना मुश्किल लगता है। ये कहाँ से आ रहा है?

ये फिर से Lenz's law है, इस बार force के रूप में। Rod का induced current magnetic field में है, तो उस पर force लगता है, और वो force पीछे की तरफ़ है, आपके धक्के के विरुद्ध। Generator चलाए जाने का विरोध करता है।

तो energy को पूरे रास्ते follow कीजिए, क्योंकि यही ईमानदार हिसाब है। आपके हाथ का mechanical work, rail दर rail, circuit की electrical energy में बदलता है, और आख़िर में resistor की heat में। न काम, न बिजली। Energy पूरी तरह conserved है, और कुछ sections बाद हम इसे गणित से prove करेंगे।

sections.title: Eddy currents: whirlpools in a solid block of metal

board_events.text: Everything so far assumed charges flow along a neat thin wire
But what if the conductor is a solid SLAB of metal, moving through or sitting in a changing field?
The induced charges still want to circulate. But now they have a whole three-dimensional block to swirl around in.

board_events.text: They form closed whirlpools of current throughout the bulk of the metal, exactly like eddies behind a rock in a flowing river. These are EDDY CURRENTS, also called Foucault currents.
Like all induced currents, they obey Lenz's law. Drop a strong magnet down a copper pipe and it floats down in slow motion, as if falling through honey.
Swing a solid copper plate between the poles of a magnet and it screeches to a halt almost instantly. That is electromagnetic damping.
These swirling currents also dump energy as heat. Sometimes a nuisance, as in transformer cores. Sometimes the whole point, as in induction furnaces and cooktops.

segments.text: Everything we have done so far quietly assumed that the induced charges flow along a neat, thin wire. The wire tells them where to go. Now let us drop that assumption.
What if the conductor is not a wire at all? What if it is a solid slab of metal, moving through a field, or just sitting in a field that is changing?

The physics does not change. The induced charges still want to circulate, because a changing flux still drives them. But now they are not confined to a thin path. They have a whole three-dimensional block to swirl around in.
Look at the two pipes on the board. Same magnet dropped down each. On the left, copper. On the right, P V C plastic. Watch what happens.

In the copper, the charges form closed whirlpools of current throughout the bulk of the metal. They look exactly like the little eddies you see swirling behind a rock in a flowing river, which is where the name comes from. These are eddy currents, also called Foucault currents.

<excited> And like every induced current in this chapter, they obey Lenz's law. They oppose the change that creates them. So drop a strong magnet down a copper pipe and it does not fall. It floats down in slow motion, as if it were falling through honey. The eddy currents in the pipe wall are fighting its motion the whole way.

Same idea in a different geometry: swing a solid copper plate between the poles of a magnet and it screeches to a halt almost instantly, instead of swinging freely. That is electromagnetic damping, and it is how some brakes and analogue meters work.

And there is a second consequence. These swirling currents also dump energy as heat, through I squared R. Sometimes that is pure nuisance, as in transformer cores where it wastes power. Sometimes it is the entire point, as in an induction furnace or the induction cooktop heating a pan in your kitchen.
अब तक हमने चुपचाप ये मान रखा था कि induced charges एक पतले, साफ़ wire में बहते हैं। Wire उन्हें रास्ता बता देता है। अब ये assumption हटा देते हैं।
अगर conductor wire है ही नहीं तो? अगर वो metal का एक ठोस slab हो, जो field में चल रहा हो, या बस ऐसी field में रखा हो जो बदल रही है?
Physics नहीं बदलती। Induced charges अब भी घूमना चाहते हैं, क्योंकि बदलती flux अब भी उन्हें धकेलती है। लेकिन अब वो किसी पतले रास्ते में क़ैद नहीं हैं। उनके पास घूमने के लिए पूरा तीन-आयामी block है।
Board पर दोनों pipes देखिए। दोनों में वही magnet गिराया गया है। बाईं तरफ़ copper. दाईं तरफ़ P V C plastic. देखिए क्या होता है।

Copper में, charges पूरे metal के भीतर current के बंद भँवर बना लेते हैं। वो बिलकुल वैसे दिखते हैं जैसे बहती नदी में पत्थर के पीछे बनने वाले छोटे भँवर, और नाम वहीं से आया है। ये हैं eddy currents, जिन्हें Foucault currents भी कहते हैं।

<excited> और इस chapter के हर induced current की तरह, ये भी Lenz's law मानते हैं। ये उसी change का विरोध करते हैं जिसने इन्हें पैदा किया। तो copper pipe में strong magnet गिराइए और वो गिरता नहीं है। वो slow motion में तैरता हुआ उतरता है, जैसे शहद में गिर रहा हो। Pipe की दीवार के eddy currents पूरे रास्ते उसकी motion से लड़ते रहते हैं।

वही बात दूसरी geometry में: magnet के poles के बीच ठोस copper plate झुलाइए और वो आज़ादी से झूलने की जगह लगभग तुरंत रुक जाती है। यही electromagnetic damping है, और कुछ brakes तथा analogue meters इसी पर चलते हैं।

और एक दूसरा नतीजा भी है। ये भँवर वाले currents I squared R के ज़रिए energy को heat के रूप में भी बहा देते हैं। कभी ये शुद्ध मुसीबत है, जैसे transformer cores में जहाँ power बर्बाद होती है। और कभी यही पूरा मक़सद है, जैसे induction furnace में या आपकी रसोई के induction cooktop में जो कड़ाही गरम करता है।

sections.title: Four conditions that decide whether these formulas apply

board_events.text: Condition 1: the geometry behind the clean formula
The simple result $\varepsilon = Bvl$ holds only when the velocity, the field, and the rod are MUTUALLY perpendicular.
Otherwise only the perpendicular components count, and you must fall back on the general form with the cross product.
Condition 2: an emf is not automatically a current
A single rod moving in a uniform field has an emf across its ends, but drives NO steady current unless it is part of a circuit whose enclosed flux is actually changing.
Condition 3: this is not new physics
Motional emf is Faraday's law seen from the moving conductor's side. Both routes give the identical answer, and we will show that explicitly.
Condition 4: eddy currents need a conductor
Eddy currents require a conductor AND a changing flux. An insulator such as PVC or glass shows none, however strong the field.

segments.text: Before the formulas arrive, let me fence off exactly when they are valid. Four conditions, and each one corresponds to a specific exam trap.

Condition one is geometric. The clean formula, emf equals B v l, holds only when three things are mutually perpendicular: the velocity, the field, and the rod itself. All three at right angles to one another.

If the velocity is at some angle instead, that formula overestimates the answer. Only the perpendicular components generate emf, and you must fall back on the general form with the cross product, v cross B, dotted with the length element.
Condition two is one students find genuinely surprising, so read it carefully.

A single rod moving in a uniform field has a real emf across its ends. You could measure it. But it drives no steady current at all, unless it is part of a circuit whose enclosed flux is actually changing. An emf is a potential difference. A current needs a closed path with a changing flux around it. Those are different requirements.
Condition three is conceptual rather than restrictive, and it prevents a nasty double-counting error. Motional emf is not new physics. It is Faraday's law seen from the moving conductor's side.

Both routes, the Lorentz force route and the flux route, give the identical answer, and we are going to show that explicitly in two sections' time. So never add a motional emf and a flux-change emf for the same single effect. That is one effect, not two.
Condition four is about eddy currents, and it is the simplest of the four to apply.

They require two things together: a conductor, and a changing flux. Take away either one and you get nothing at all. So an insulator like P V C or glass shows no eddy currents whatsoever, however strong the field you apply.
Formulas आने से पहले, मैं ठीक-ठीक बता देती हूँ कि वो कब valid हैं। चार conditions, और हर एक किसी ख़ास exam trap से जुड़ी है।
पहली condition geometric है। साफ़ formula, emf equals B v l, तभी चलता है जब तीन चीज़ें आपस में perpendicular हों: velocity, field, और ख़ुद rod. तीनों एक दूसरे से समकोण पर।

अगर velocity किसी और angle पर है, तो वो formula answer को बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर देता है। सिर्फ़ perpendicular components emf बनाते हैं, और आपको general form पर लौटना पड़ता है, v cross B, जिसका length element से dot लिया जाता है।
दूसरी condition वो है जो students को सचमुच चौंकाती है, तो ध्यान से पढ़िए।

Uniform field में चलते हुए अकेले rod के सिरों पर असली emf होती है। आप उसे नाप सकते हैं। लेकिन वो कोई steady current नहीं चलाता, जब तक वो ऐसे circuit का हिस्सा न हो जिसकी enclosed flux सचमुच बदल रही हो। Emf एक potential difference है। Current के लिए बंद रास्ता चाहिए जिसके भीतर flux बदल रही हो। ये दोनों अलग शर्तें हैं।

तीसरी condition restriction से ज़्यादा conceptual है, और ये double-counting की एक ख़तरनाक ग़लती से बचाती है। Motional emf कोई नई physics नहीं है। ये Faraday's law ही है, बस चलते हुए conductor की तरफ़ से देखा गया।

दोनों रास्ते, Lorentz force वाला और flux वाला, बिलकुल एक ही answer देते हैं, और हम दो sections बाद यही explicitly दिखाएँगे। तो एक ही effect के लिए motional emf और flux-change emf को कभी मत जोड़िए। वो एक effect है, दो नहीं।
चौथी condition eddy currents के बारे में है, और चारों में सबसे आसान यही है।

इनके लिए दो चीज़ें एक साथ चाहिए: conductor, और बदलती flux. इनमें से कोई एक हटा दीजिए तो कुछ नहीं मिलेगा। तो P V C या glass जैसा insulator कोई eddy current नहीं दिखाता, चाहे आप कितनी भी strong field लगा दें।

sections.title: The motional emf formulas and the rod-on-rails chain

board_events.text: Motional emf, with velocity, field and rod mutually perpendicular
General motional emf, when they are not
The rod-on-rails generator: rod length l, speed v, circuit resistance R

board_events.latex: P = Fv = \frac{B^2 l^2 v^2}{R} = I^2 R

board_events.text: Anchor everything to one quantity, emf = Bvl, and let the chain cascade. Learn the chain, not four separate formulas.

segments.text: Here is the core formula set for motional emf. And I want you to notice the structure, because these are not four independent things to memorise. They are one thing, followed three steps downstream.
The headline result: emf equals B v l. Field, times speed, times the length of the rod. That holds when velocity, field, and rod are mutually perpendicular, which is the standard setup.
When those three are not mutually perpendicular, that clean formula stops being valid and you need the general form instead.

It is the integral of v cross B, dotted with the length element d l, and for a closed loop it becomes a closed-loop integral. In practice you meet the clean version far more often, but you should recognise the general one the moment a problem tilts the geometry.
Now the rod-on-rails chain, and watch how each line feeds the next.
Start with the emf we already have and apply Ohm's law. Current equals B v l over R. That is step one, and it is just the emf divided by resistance.

Now that current sits in a magnetic field, so it feels a force, F equals B I l. Substitute the current we just found and you get B squared l squared v over R. That is the retarding force, the thing you physically feel resisting your push.

One more step. Power is force times velocity, so multiply by v again and you get B squared l squared v squared over R. And notice, satisfyingly, that this equals I squared R exactly, the Joule heating in the resistor. Mechanical power in equals electrical power out.

<whisper> So here is how to hold this in your head under exam pressure. Do not memorise four formulas. Anchor everything to emf equals B v l, then let the chain cascade: divide by R for current, multiply by B l for force, multiply by v for power. Three moves, and you can rebuild the whole set in about ten seconds.
ये रहा motional emf का मुख्य formula set. और मैं चाहती हूँ आप इसकी बनावट देखें, क्योंकि ये चार अलग-अलग रटने वाली चीज़ें नहीं हैं। ये एक ही चीज़ है, जिसके तीन क़दम आगे के नतीजे हैं।
मुख्य result: emf equals B v l. Field, into speed, into rod की length. ये तब चलता है जब velocity, field, और rod आपस में perpendicular हों, जो कि standard setup है।
जब ये तीनों आपस में perpendicular न हों, तो वो साफ़ formula valid नहीं रहता और general form चाहिए।

वो है v cross B का integral, जिसका length element d l से dot लिया गया हो, और बंद loop के लिए ये closed-loop integral बन जाता है। Practically साफ़ वाला version कहीं ज़्यादा मिलता है, लेकिन जैसे ही problem geometry टेढ़ी करे, general वाला पहचान लेना चाहिए।
अब rod-on-rails की chain, और देखिए हर line अगली को कैसे खिलाती है।
जो emf हमारे पास है वहीं से शुरू कीजिए और Ohm's law लगाइए। Current equals B v l बटा R. यही पहला क़दम है, और ये बस emf बटा resistance है।

अब वो current magnetic field में है, तो उस पर force लगता है, F equals B I l. अभी निकाला हुआ current रख दीजिए और मिलता है B squared l squared v बटा R. यही retarding force है, वही चीज़ जो आपको अपने धक्के का विरोध करती महसूस होती है।

एक और क़दम। Power होती है force into velocity, तो एक बार और v से multiply कीजिए और मिलता है B squared l squared v squared बटा R. और ग़ौर कीजिए, बड़ी संतोषजनक बात है, ये बिलकुल I squared R के बराबर है, यानी resistor की Joule heating. अंदर जाती mechanical power बराबर बाहर आती electrical power.

<whisper> तो exam के दबाव में इसे दिमाग़ में ऐसे रखिए। चार formulas मत रटिए। सब कुछ emf equals B v l पर टिकाइए, फिर chain चलने दीजिए: current के लिए R से भाग, force के लिए B l से गुणा, power के लिए v से गुणा। तीन चालें, और आप पूरा set दस second में दोबारा बना सकते हैं।

sections.title: Rotating rod, terminal velocity, and the units

board_events.text: Rod rotating about one end
Rod of length l, angular velocity omega, field perpendicular to the plane of rotation.
Note the l SQUARED. This is where exam questions about doubling the length live.
Terminal velocity: a rod of mass m falling under gravity on vertical rails
Induced charge, carried over from Subtopic 01

Units: motional emf in volt, dimension $[ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}]$, same as any emf. The retarding force is genuinely a force: newton, $[MLT^{-2}]$. Eddy-current power loss scales with $B^2$ and with the square of the frequency of flux change, which is why it is fought by raising the resistance of the current paths, not by changing the field.

segments.text: Three more results to add to the set, and then the units. These are the ones that show up in the harder numericals.
First, the rotating rod. A rod of length l spins about one fixed end, with angular velocity omega, in a field perpendicular to the plane of rotation.
The emf is one half B omega l squared. We will derive this properly in a few sections, but for now, look hard at the structure of it.

Notice the l squared. That is not decoration, and it is where exam questions live. A very standard question doubles the length while halving the angular velocity and asks what happens. Halving omega gives a factor of one half. Doubling l gives a factor of four, because it is squared. Net effect, the emf doubles. Students who miss the square get that badly wrong.
Second, terminal velocity. A rod of mass m falls under gravity on vertical rails, and the answer is m g R over B squared l squared.

And I want you to see where this comes from conceptually, not just as a formula. As the rod falls faster, the emf grows, so the current grows, so the retarding force grows. Eventually that force equals gravity, the acceleration goes to zero, and the speed stops changing. It is a force balance, nothing more.
Third, the induced charge result carries straight over from subtopic one, completely unchanged.
It is q equals N delta phi over R. Nothing about motional emf touches it, so if a motional-emf problem asks how much charge flowed, you still go straight to this formula and skip the emf entirely.

Now the units. Motional emf is measured in volts, dimension M L squared T to the minus three A to the minus one, exactly the same as any other emf. The retarding force is a genuine force, newtons, M L T to the minus two. And eddy-current power loss scales with B squared and with the square of the frequency of flux change, which is precisely why engineers fight it by raising the resistance of the current paths, and not by weakening the field they actually want.
Set में तीन और results जोड़ते हैं, फिर units. ये वही हैं जो मुश्किल numericals में आते हैं।
पहला, rotating rod. एक rod जिसकी length l है, वो एक स्थिर सिरे के गिर्द angular velocity omega से घूम रहा है, उस field में जो plane of rotation के perpendicular है।
Emf है one half B omega l squared. इसे हम कुछ sections बाद ठीक से derive करेंगे, लेकिन फ़िलहाल इसकी बनावट ग़ौर से देखिए।

वो l squared देखिए। ये सजावट नहीं है, और यहीं exam के questions रहते हैं। एक बहुत standard question length दोगुनी कर देता है और angular velocity आधी, फिर पूछता है क्या होगा। Omega आधी करने से one half का factor. L दोगुनी करने से चार का factor, क्योंकि वो squared है। कुल असर, emf दोगुनी। जो students square छोड़ देते हैं वो बुरी तरह ग़लत करते हैं।
दूसरा, terminal velocity. Mass m का rod vertical rails पर gravity से गिरता है, और answer है m g R बटा B squared l squared.

और मैं चाहती हूँ आप conceptually देखें ये कहाँ से आया, सिर्फ़ formula की तरह नहीं। जैसे-जैसे rod तेज़ गिरता है, emf बढ़ती है, तो current बढ़ता है, तो retarding force बढ़ता है। आख़िरकार वो force gravity के बराबर हो जाता है, acceleration zero हो जाता है, और speed बदलना बंद कर देती है। ये बस एक force balance है, और कुछ नहीं।
तीसरा, induced charge का result subtopic एक से बिलकुल बिना बदले सीधे चला आता है।
वो है q equals N delta phi बटा R. Motional emf उसमें कुछ नहीं बदलती, तो अगर motional-emf वाली problem पूछे कि कितना charge बहा, आप सीधे इसी formula पर जाइए और emf बीच में लाइए ही मत।

अब units. Motional emf volts में नापी जाती है, dimension M L squared T to the minus three A to the minus one, बिलकुल किसी भी दूसरी emf जैसी। Retarding force असली force है, newtons में, M L T to the minus two. और eddy-current की power loss B squared के साथ और flux बदलने की frequency के square के साथ बढ़ती है, और ठीक इसीलिए engineers इससे current paths की resistance बढ़ाकर लड़ते हैं, उस field को कमज़ोर करके नहीं जो उन्हें चाहिए ही चाहिए।

sections.title: Board derivation: the same emf by two completely different routes

board_events.text: Route A: from the Lorentz force, first principles
Each free charge q inside the rod moves with the rod, so it feels a magnetic force of magnitude $F = qvB$, directed ALONG the rod.
This shovels positive charge to one end. The separated charge sets up an electric field E inside the rod, pushing back. Charge piles up until the two forces balance:

board_events.latex: qE = qvB \;\Rightarrow\; E = vB \;\Rightarrow\; V = El = Bvl \;\Rightarrow\; \varepsilon = Bvl

board_events.text: Route B: from Faraday's law, the flux view
Put the rod on two rails separated by l. As the rod slides a distance $dx = v\,dt$, the loop area grows by $dA = l\,dx = lv\,dt$.
Identical. The Lorentz view is LOCAL, about charges in the rod. The flux view is GLOBAL, about area swept by the circuit. One law, two viewpoints.
This is why you must never add a motional emf and a flux-change emf for the same effect. You would be counting one thing twice.

segments.text: This is a C B S E favourite derivation, and it is worth doing carefully because the punchline matters more than either calculation.
Route A starts from the Lorentz force, from first principles. Take a straight rod of length l moving with constant velocity v perpendicular to a uniform field B, everything mutually perpendicular.

Each free charge q inside the rod moves along with the rod, so it feels a magnetic force of magnitude q v B, and that force is directed along the length of the rod. So it shovels positive charge toward one end and electrons toward the other.

But that separated charge immediately sets up an electric field E inside the rod, pointing back the other way, pushing the charges back. Charge keeps piling up until those two forces exactly balance. Setting q E equal to q v B gives E equals v B. The potential difference across the rod is E times l, which is B v l. And that is the motional emf.
Now route B, which throws away all of that and starts from Faraday's law instead.
Put the rod on two rails separated by distance l, closing a circuit. As the rod slides a distance d x, which is v d t, the area of the loop grows by d A equals l d x, which is l v d t.
So the flux changes by B times that area, which is B l v d t. Divide by d t as Faraday's law demands, the d t cancels, and the induced emf is B v l.

<excited> Identical. Two completely different starting points, no shared steps, and the same answer. And here is the key conceptual takeaway. The Lorentz view is local, it is about individual charges being shoved inside the rod. The flux view is global, it is about the area being swept by the whole circuit.

They are two views of one law. And that is exactly why you must never add a motional emf and a flux-change emf for the same single effect. You would be counting one thing twice, and the answer would come out double.
ये C B S E की favourite derivation है, और इसे ध्यान से करना ज़रूरी है क्योंकि आख़िरी बात दोनों calculations से ज़्यादा अहम है।
Route A शुरू होता है Lorentz force से, first principles से। एक सीधा rod लीजिए, length l, जो uniform field B के perpendicular constant velocity v से चल रहा है, सब कुछ आपस में perpendicular.

Rod के अंदर हर free charge q, rod के साथ चलता है, तो उसे q v B magnitude का magnetic force महसूस होता है, और वो force rod की लंबाई के साथ है। तो वो positive charge को एक सिरे और electrons को दूसरे सिरे धकेल देता है।

लेकिन वो अलग हुआ charge फ़ौरन rod के अंदर एक electric field E बना देता है, जो उल्टी तरफ़ है और charges को वापस धकेलता है। Charge तब तक जमा होता रहता है जब तक ये दोनों forces ठीक बराबर न हो जाएँ। q E को q v B के बराबर रखने पर मिलता है E equals v B. Rod के आर-पार potential difference है E into l, यानी B v l. और यही motional emf है।
अब route B, जो ये सब छोड़कर Faraday's law से शुरू करता है।
Rod को l दूरी पर रखी दो rails पर रख दीजिए, circuit पूरा हो गया। जैसे ही rod d x दूरी सरकता है, जो कि v d t है, loop का area बढ़ता है d A equals l d x, यानी l v d t.
तो flux बदलती है B times वो area, यानी B l v d t. Faraday's law के मुताबिक़ d t से भाग दीजिए, d t cancel हो जाता है, और induced emf निकलती है B v l.

<excited> बिलकुल वही। दो बिलकुल अलग शुरुआतें, कोई साझा क़दम नहीं, और वही answer. और अब असली conceptual बात। Lorentz वाला नज़रिया local है, वो rod के अंदर अलग-अलग charges के धक्के की बात करता है। Flux वाला नज़रिया global है, वो पूरे circuit द्वारा बुहारे गए area की बात करता है।
ये एक ही law के दो नज़रिए हैं। और ठीक इसीलिए एक ही effect के लिए motional emf और flux-change emf को कभी मत जोड़िए। वो एक ही चीज़ को दो बार गिनना होगा, और answer दोगुना आ जाएगा।

sections.title: Board derivation: the energy books balance exactly

board_events.text: The slidewire generator, driven at constant speed
The induced current is $I = Bvl/R$. The field exerts a force $F = BIl$ on the current-carrying rod, opposing its motion. That is Lenz.
To keep v constant, an external agent must supply an equal forward force, doing work at the rate:
Now compute the electrical power independently

board_events.latex: P_{\text{elec}} = I^2 R = \left(\frac{Bvl}{R}\right)^2 R = \frac{B^2 l^2 v^2}{R}

board_events.text: Exactly equal. Every joule of mechanical work becomes a joule of electrical heat. This is Lenz's law as bookkeeping for energy conservation.
Note what makes this work: the rod moves at CONSTANT speed, so its kinetic energy is not changing. All the external work goes to the circuit.

segments.text: Earlier I claimed that the mechanical work you do turns into electrical heat, exactly, with nothing left over. Let us now prove that, because it is a very satisfying calculation and C B S E asks for it.
Take the slidewire generator, driven at constant speed. The induced current is B v l over R, which we established from the chain.

That current sits in a magnetic field, so the field exerts a force on the current-carrying rod, F equals B I l. And by Lenz's law that force opposes the rod's motion. Substituting for the current gives B squared l squared v over R.
Now, the rod is moving at constant speed, which means the net force on it is zero. So an external agent, your hand, must be supplying an equal and opposite forward force.
The rate at which your hand does work is force times velocity, giving mechanical power equal to B squared l squared v squared over R. Hold onto that expression.

Now compute the electrical power completely independently, without looking at the mechanics at all. Power dissipated in a resistance is I squared R. Substitute I equals B v l over R, square it, multiply by R.
<excited> And out comes B squared l squared v squared over R.
Exactly the same expression. Not approximately, not to within some factor. Identical. Every single joule of mechanical work becomes a joule of electrical heat in the resistor.

One condition makes this clean, and it is worth stating in your answer. The rod moves at constant speed, so its kinetic energy is not changing, and none of your work is going into speeding it up. All of it goes to the circuit. This is Lenz's law functioning as bookkeeping for conservation of energy, and it is the reason the minus sign has to be there.
पहले मैंने दावा किया था कि आपका किया हुआ mechanical work पूरा का पूरा electrical heat बन जाता है, बिना कुछ बचे। अब उसे prove करते हैं, क्योंकि ये बड़ी संतोषजनक calculation है और C B S E इसे पूछता है।
Slidewire generator लीजिए, constant speed पर चलाया हुआ। Induced current है B v l बटा R, जो हमने chain से निकाला था।

वो current magnetic field में है, तो field उस current-carrying rod पर force लगाती है, F equals B I l. और Lenz's law के मुताबिक़ वो force rod की motion का विरोध करता है। Current रखने पर मिलता है B squared l squared v बटा R.
अब, rod constant speed पर चल रहा है, यानी उस पर net force zero है। तो कोई बाहरी agent, आपका हाथ, बराबर और उल्टा आगे की तरफ़ force लगा रहा होगा।
आपका हाथ जिस दर से काम करता है वो है force into velocity, यानी mechanical power equals B squared l squared v squared बटा R. इस expression को पकड़े रखिए।
अब electrical power बिलकुल अलग से निकालिए, mechanics की तरफ़ देखे बिना। Resistance में dissipate होने वाली power है I squared R. उसमें I equals B v l बटा R रखिए, square कीजिए, R से multiply कीजिए।
<excited> और निकलता है B squared l squared v squared बटा R.
बिलकुल वही expression. लगभग नहीं, किसी factor के अंतर से नहीं। एकदम वही। Mechanical work का हर एक joule, resistor में electrical heat का एक joule बन जाता है।

एक condition इसे साफ़ बनाती है, और उसे अपने answer में लिखना चाहिए। Rod constant speed पर चल रहा है, तो उसकी kinetic energy बदल नहीं रही, और आपका कोई काम उसे तेज़ करने में नहीं जा रहा। सब कुछ circuit में जाता है। यही Lenz's law है conservation of energy का हिसाब रखते हुए, और यही वजह है कि minus sign वहाँ होना ही था।

board_events.text: Why we cannot just write Bvl: every part of the rod moves at a DIFFERENT speed. The pivot end is stationary, the far end is fastest.
So take a small element of length dx at distance x from the pivot. It moves with speed $v = \omega x$.
Now sum along the whole rod, from the pivot at x = 0 to the tip at x = l:

segments.text: Now the rotating rod, and this derivation is short but it teaches a habit you will use everywhere: when a formula breaks, find the piece where it still works.

A rod of length l rotates with angular velocity omega about one fixed end, sitting in a field B perpendicular to the plane of rotation. Look at the diagram: pivot at O, the tip sweeping out the dashed circle.

Now, why can we not simply write emf equals B v l and be done? Because there is no single v. Every part of the rod moves at a different speed. The end at the pivot is stationary. The far tip is moving fastest. Which v would you even substitute?
So we do what we did with the non-uniform field earlier. We find the piece small enough that the simple formula is valid again.

Take a small element of length d x, sitting at distance x from the pivot. Look at the shaded green element on the diagram. Because it is small, every point in it moves at essentially the same speed, and that speed is omega times x.
So this one element behaves exactly like a tiny straight rod moving at speed omega x, and it contributes an emf of B times omega x times d x.
Now add up every element along the rod, from the pivot at x equals zero to the tip at x equals l. The integral of x d x is x squared over two, evaluated at l, giving l squared over two.

So the emf is one half B omega l squared. And notice where the one half and the square came from: they fell out of integrating x, they were not memorised. That is why the length is squared, and it is why doubling the rod length quadruples the emf rather than doubling it.
अब rotating rod, और ये derivation छोटी है लेकिन एक आदत सिखाती है जो आप हर जगह इस्तेमाल करेंगे: जब formula टूट जाए, तो वो टुकड़ा ढूँढिए जहाँ वो अब भी चलता है।
Length l का rod, angular velocity omega से एक स्थिर सिरे के गिर्द घूम रहा है, उस field B में जो plane of rotation के perpendicular है। Diagram देखिए: pivot O पर, और सिरा dashed circle बनाता हुआ।

अब, हम सीधे emf equals B v l लिखकर काम ख़त्म क्यों नहीं कर सकते? क्योंकि कोई एक v है ही नहीं। Rod का हर हिस्सा अलग speed से चल रहा है। Pivot वाला सिरा स्थिर है। दूर वाला सिरा सबसे तेज़। आप कौन सी v रखेंगे?
तो हम वही करते हैं जो पहले non-uniform field के साथ किया था। हम वो टुकड़ा ढूँढते हैं जो इतना छोटा हो कि simple formula फिर से valid हो जाए।

Length d x का एक छोटा element लीजिए, जो pivot से x दूरी पर है। Diagram पर वो हरा shaded element देखिए। छोटा होने की वजह से उसका हर point practically एक ही speed से चलता है, और वो speed है omega into x.
तो ये एक element बिलकुल एक छोटे सीधे rod की तरह बर्ताव करता है जो omega x speed से चल रहा है, और वो B times omega x times d x की emf देता है।
अब rod के हर element को जोड़िए, pivot पर x equals zero से लेकर सिरे पर x equals l तक। x d x का integral है x squared बटा two, जिसे l पर evaluate करने पर मिलता है l squared बटा two.

तो emf है one half B omega l squared. और ग़ौर कीजिए वो one half और वो square आए कहाँ से: वो x को integrate करने से निकले, रटे नहीं गए। इसीलिए length squared है, और इसीलिए rod की length दोगुनी करने पर emf दोगुनी नहीं, चार गुनी होती है।

board_events.text: Find (a) the motional emf, (b) the induced current, (c) the force needed to keep the rod moving steadily, and (d) the power delivered.
Check three ways: P = Fv = 0.18 W. Also eps times I = 0.18 W. Also I squared R = 0.18 W. All agree.

segments.text: This is the standard C B S E rod-on-rails question, and it exists to test whether you can run the chain cleanly from end to end. Four parts, and each one feeds the next.

A conducting rod of length zero point five zero metres slides at constant speed three point zero metres per second along two horizontal frictionless rails, in a uniform vertical field of zero point four zero tesla. The rails are joined by a resistor, total circuit resistance two point zero ohms.
The figure is exactly our slidewire generator. Rod bridging the rails, resistor closing the loop, field into the page.
Four parts to find: the motional emf, the induced current, the force needed to keep the rod moving steadily, and the power delivered.

Part a, and start at the anchor. Emf equals B v l, which is zero point four zero times three point zero times zero point five zero, giving zero point six zero volts. Everything else in this problem descends from this number.
Part b, divide by resistance. Zero point six zero over two point zero gives zero point three zero amperes.

Part c, and read the wording carefully because it decides the physics. The rod moves steadily, at constant speed, so net force is zero. Therefore the applied force exactly balances the magnetic retarding force. F equals B I l, which is zero point four zero times zero point three zero times zero point five zero, giving zero point zero six zero newtons.

<whisper> Part d, and here is where you can buy yourself certainty for free. Power equals F v equals zero point zero six zero times three point zero, which is zero point one eight watts. Now check it two other ways. Emf times current is zero point six zero times zero point three zero, also zero point one eight. And I squared R is zero point three zero squared times two point zero, again zero point one eight. Three independent routes agreeing means your whole chain is right. Do that check whenever the numbers are easy.
ये standard C B S E rod-on-rails question है, और ये देखने के लिए है कि आप chain को साफ़-साफ़ शुरू से आख़िर तक चला सकते हैं या नहीं। चार parts, और हर एक अगले को खिलाता है।

एक conducting rod, length zero point five zero metres, दो horizontal frictionless rails पर constant speed three point zero metres per second से सरक रहा है, zero point four zero tesla की uniform vertical field में। Rails एक resistor से जुड़ी हैं, total circuit resistance two point zero ohms.
Figure बिलकुल हमारा slidewire generator है। Rod rails के आर-पार, resistor loop बंद करता हुआ, field page के अंदर।
चार parts निकालने हैं: motional emf, induced current, rod को steadily चलाने के लिए ज़रूरी force, और delivered power.

Part a, और शुरुआत anchor से। Emf equals B v l, यानी zero point four zero times three point zero times zero point five zero, जो देता है zero point six zero volts. इस problem की बाक़ी हर चीज़ इसी number से निकलती है।
Part b, resistance से भाग दीजिए। Zero point six zero बटा two point zero देता है zero point three zero amperes.

Part c, और wording ध्यान से पढ़िए क्योंकि वही physics तय करती है। Rod steadily चल रहा है, constant speed पर, तो net force zero है। इसलिए लगाया गया force ठीक magnetic retarding force को balance करता है। F equals B I l, यानी zero point four zero times zero point three zero times zero point five zero, जो देता है zero point zero six zero newtons.

<whisper> Part d, और यहाँ आप मुफ़्त में यक़ीन ख़रीद सकते हैं। Power equals F v equals zero point zero six zero times three point zero, यानी zero point one eight watts. अब इसे दो और तरीक़ों से check कीजिए। Emf into current है zero point six zero times zero point three zero, यानी वही zero point one eight. और I squared R है zero point three zero squared times two point zero, फिर वही zero point one eight. तीन अलग रास्तों का एक जगह मिलना बताता है कि आपकी पूरी chain सही है। जब numbers आसान हों, ये check ज़रूर कीजिए।

board_events.text: The trap: both tubes are hollow and the magnet touches neither, so gravity is the only force, so it takes the same time in both. Tempting, but wrong.
The fast, correct read
As the magnet falls through the COPPER tube, the flux through each ring-like cross-section of the tube changes, inducing eddy currents in the copper wall.
By Lenz's law those currents oppose the change. They exert an upward retarding force on the falling magnet, so it descends slowly.
PVC is an insulator, so no eddy currents form, and the magnet falls in free-fall time. Answer: much longer in the copper tube.

segments.text: This is a N E E T conceptual question, and it is a very good one, because the wrong answer is genuinely reasonable-sounding.

A strong cylindrical magnet is dropped from the top of two identical vertical tubes of the same length. One tube is made of copper, the other of P V C plastic. Through which tube does the magnet take longer to fall, and why?
Look at the two tubes on the board. Copper on the left, P V C on the right, same magnet dropped down each.

<curious> Now the trap, and notice how sensible it sounds. Both tubes are hollow. The magnet touches neither wall. It is in free space inside both. So gravity is the only force acting, and it must take exactly the same time in both. Tempting, and completely wrong.
Here is the correct read, and it takes seconds once you spot the keyword copper.

As the magnet falls through the copper tube, think about any horizontal ring-shaped cross-section of that tube. As the magnet approaches and passes, the flux through that ring changes. Changing flux in a conductor means induced currents, and since the tube wall is a bulk conductor, those are eddy currents.

And by Lenz's law, those eddy currents oppose the change that created them. In practice that means they exert an upward retarding force on the falling magnet. So it does not free-fall. It descends slowly, as though falling through honey.

<whisper> P V C, on the other hand, is an insulator. No free charges to circulate, so no eddy currents form at all, however strong the magnet. It falls in ordinary free-fall time. So the answer is that the magnet takes much longer in the copper tube. And here is your one-line elimination for the exam hall: eddy currents need a conductor. P V C has none. Cross it out immediately and move on.
ये N E E T का conceptual question है, और बहुत अच्छा है, क्योंकि ग़लत answer सचमुच समझदारी भरा लगता है।

एक strong cylindrical magnet दो एक जैसी vertical tubes के ऊपर से गिराया जाता है, दोनों की length बराबर। एक tube copper की है, दूसरी P V C plastic की। किस tube से गिरने में magnet को ज़्यादा time लगेगा, और क्यों?
Board पर दोनों tubes देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ copper, दाईं तरफ़ P V C, दोनों में वही magnet गिराया गया।

<curious> अब trap देखिए, और ग़ौर कीजिए कितना समझदार लगता है। दोनों tubes खोखली हैं। Magnet किसी दीवार को छूता नहीं। दोनों के अंदर वो खुली जगह में है। तो सिर्फ़ gravity काम कर रही है, और दोनों में बिलकुल बराबर time लगना चाहिए। लुभावना, और बिलकुल ग़लत।
ये रही सही पढ़ाई, और copper शब्द दिखते ही इसमें seconds लगते हैं।

जब magnet copper tube से गिरता है, उस tube के किसी भी horizontal ring जैसे cross-section के बारे में सोचिए। जैसे-जैसे magnet पास आता है और गुज़रता है, उस ring से गुज़रती flux बदलती है। Conductor में बदलती flux यानी induced currents, और चूँकि tube की दीवार bulk conductor है, वो eddy currents हैं।

और Lenz's law के मुताबिक़, वो eddy currents उसी change का विरोध करते हैं जिसने उन्हें पैदा किया। व्यवहार में इसका मतलब है कि वो गिरते हुए magnet पर ऊपर की तरफ़ retarding force लगाते हैं। तो वो free-fall नहीं करता। वो धीरे-धीरे उतरता है, जैसे शहद में गिर रहा हो।

<whisper> दूसरी तरफ़ P V C एक insulator है। घूमने के लिए free charges ही नहीं, तो कोई eddy current बनता ही नहीं, चाहे magnet कितना भी strong हो। वो सामान्य free-fall time में गिरता है। तो answer ये है कि copper tube में magnet को कहीं ज़्यादा time लगता है। और exam hall के लिए आपकी एक-line elimination: eddy currents के लिए conductor चाहिए। P V C में है ही नहीं। तुरंत काटिए और आगे बढ़िए।

board_events.text: This couples Newton's second law with electromagnetic induction. Do NOT solve a differential equation. Just balance forces.
As the rod falls and speeds up, the induced current grows, and so does the upward retarding force. Terminal velocity is reached when that force balances gravity:

segments.text: This problem couples Newton's second law with electromagnetic induction, which is exactly the kind of fusion J E E Main likes. And there is a trap of method here, not of physics.

A conducting rod of mass forty grams and length zero point four zero metres slides without friction down two vertical conducting rails, connected at the bottom by a resistor, giving total circuit resistance zero point two zero ohms. A uniform horizontal field of zero point five zero tesla is perpendicular to the plane of the rails. The rod is released from rest. Take g as ten metres per second squared.
Look at the diagram before you write anything. The rod falls, gravity pulls down, and the magnetic drag pushes up. Those are the only two forces that matter.

<whisper> Now the method trap. Some students see released from rest, realise the speed is changing, and start setting up a differential equation for the motion. Under exam pressure that is a disaster. You do not need it. Terminal velocity is a statement about the final steady state, and the final steady state is just a force balance.

Here is the physical story. As the rod falls and speeds up, the emf grows, so the induced current grows, so the upward retarding force B squared l squared v over R grows. Terminal velocity is reached at the moment that force equals gravity, because then the acceleration is zero and the speed stops changing.
So set m g equal to B squared l squared v over R and rearrange. Terminal velocity equals m g R over B squared l squared.

Substitute, watching the units. Mass is zero point zero four zero kilograms, converted from forty grams. Numerator is zero point zero four zero times ten times zero point two zero, giving zero point zero eight zero. Denominator is zero point five zero squared times zero point four zero squared, which is zero point two five times zero point one six, giving zero point zero four zero. So terminal velocity is two point zero metres per second.

The current at that instant is B v l over R, which is zero point five zero times two point zero times zero point four zero, over zero point two zero, giving two point zero amperes. And now verify with energy. Gravitational power input is m g v, which is zero point eight zero watts. Electrical dissipation is I squared R, which is four times zero point two zero, also zero point eight zero watts. They match, which confirms the physical picture: at terminal velocity, all the gravitational power is going straight into heat.
ये problem Newton's second law को electromagnetic induction से जोड़ती है, और ठीक यही fusion J E E Main को पसंद है। और यहाँ trap method का है, physics का नहीं।

एक conducting rod, mass forty grams, length zero point four zero metres, दो vertical conducting rails पर बिना घर्षण के नीचे सरकता है, नीचे एक resistor से जुड़ी हुई, जिससे total circuit resistance zero point two zero ohms है। Rails के plane के perpendicular zero point five zero tesla की uniform horizontal field है। Rod को rest से छोड़ा जाता है। g को ten metres per second squared लीजिए।
कुछ भी लिखने से पहले diagram देखिए। Rod गिर रहा है, gravity नीचे खींच रही है, और magnetic drag ऊपर धकेल रहा है। बस यही दो forces मायने रखती हैं।

<whisper> अब method वाला trap. कुछ students released from rest पढ़ते हैं, समझते हैं कि speed बदल रही है, और motion के लिए differential equation बनाने लगते हैं। Exam के दबाव में ये आफ़त है। इसकी ज़रूरत ही नहीं। Terminal velocity आख़िरी steady state की बात है, और वो steady state सिर्फ़ एक force balance है।

Physical कहानी ये है। जैसे-जैसे rod गिरता और तेज़ होता है, emf बढ़ती है, तो induced current बढ़ता है, तो ऊपर की तरफ़ retarding force B squared l squared v बटा R बढ़ता है। Terminal velocity उस पल आती है जब वो force gravity के बराबर हो जाए, क्योंकि तब acceleration zero है और speed बदलना बंद।
तो m g को B squared l squared v बटा R के बराबर रखिए और rearrange कीजिए। Terminal velocity equals m g R बटा B squared l squared.

Substitute कीजिए, units पर नज़र रखते हुए। Mass है zero point zero four zero kilograms, forty grams से बदला हुआ। ऊपर है zero point zero four zero times ten times zero point two zero, यानी zero point zero eight zero. नीचे है zero point five zero squared times zero point four zero squared, यानी zero point two five times zero point one six, यानी zero point zero four zero. तो terminal velocity है two point zero metres per second.

उस पल current है B v l बटा R, यानी zero point five zero times two point zero times zero point four zero, बटा zero point two zero, यानी two point zero amperes. और अब energy से verify कीजिए। Gravitational power input है m g v, यानी zero point eight zero watts. Electrical dissipation है I squared R, यानी four times zero point two zero, वही zero point eight zero watts. दोनों मिल गए, जो physical तस्वीर की पुष्टि करता है: terminal velocity पर सारी gravitational power सीधे heat में जा रही है।

board_events.text: Find (a) the emf, (b) the current, (c) the external torque needed to maintain rotation, and (d) the power supplied.
For torque, do not hunt for a force and a lever arm. Go through POWER: the electrical power drawn must equal the mechanical power supplied, and mechanical power is torque times omega.

segments.text: Now the rotating rod as a working circuit, which is the J E E Advanced version. The physics is the same as our derivation, but part c asks something new and there is a slick way to get it.

A conducting rod of length zero point six zero metres rotates with constant angular velocity fifty radians per second about a fixed axis through one end, in a uniform field of zero point three zero tesla perpendicular to the plane of rotation.

Look at the circuit. The far end of the rod slides on a circular conducting track. A wire from that track and a wire from the pivot run out through an external resistance of nine point zero ohms. The rod and contacts are treated as resistanceless, so all the resistance is in R.
Four parts: the emf, the current, the external torque needed to maintain rotation, and the power supplied.

Part a uses our derived result directly. Emf equals one half B omega l squared, which is one half times zero point three zero times fifty times zero point three six. Note that l squared is zero point six zero squared, which is zero point three six. That gives two point seven volts.
Part b is Ohm's law. Two point seven over nine point zero gives zero point three zero amperes.

<curious> Part c is the interesting one. You need the external torque. Now, you could try to find the magnetic force on the rod, work out where it effectively acts, and take a moment about the pivot. That is honest work, and it is slow, and it is easy to get wrong.

Go through power instead. The electrical power being drawn is emf times current, two point seven times zero point three zero, giving zero point eight one watts. Check it against I squared R: zero point three zero squared times nine point zero, also zero point eight one. That power is being supplied mechanically, and mechanical power for a rotation is torque times omega. So torque is power over omega, zero point eight one over fifty, which is one point six two times ten to the minus two newton metres. And part d is that same zero point eight one watts, the mechanical power the agent must supply against the magnetic braking torque. Every watt of it ends up as heat in R.
अब rotating rod को एक चलते हुए circuit की तरह देखते हैं, यही J E E Advanced वाला रूप है। Physics हमारी derivation जैसी ही है, लेकिन part c कुछ नया माँगता है और उसे निकालने का एक चालाक तरीक़ा है।

एक conducting rod, length zero point six zero metres, एक सिरे से गुज़रती स्थिर axis के गिर्द constant angular velocity fifty radians per second से घूम रहा है, zero point three zero tesla की uniform field में जो plane of rotation के perpendicular है।

Circuit देखिए। Rod का दूर वाला सिरा एक circular conducting track पर सरकता है। उस track से एक तार और pivot से एक तार निकलकर nine point zero ohms की external resistance से होकर जाते हैं। Rod और contacts को resistanceless माना गया है, तो सारी resistance R में है।
चार parts: emf, current, rotation बनाए रखने के लिए ज़रूरी external torque, और supplied power.

Part a सीधे हमारे derived result से। Emf equals one half B omega l squared, यानी one half times zero point three zero times fifty times zero point three six. ध्यान दीजिए l squared है zero point six zero squared, यानी zero point three six. इससे मिलता है two point seven volts.
Part b Ohm's law है। Two point seven बटा nine point zero देता है zero point three zero amperes.

<curious> Part c दिलचस्प है। आपको external torque चाहिए। अब, आप चाहें तो rod पर magnetic force निकालें, तय करें कि वो असरदार तौर पर कहाँ लगता है, और pivot के बारे में moment लें। ये ईमानदार मेहनत है, धीमी है, और ग़लत होने की गुंजाइश ज़्यादा है।

इसकी जगह power के रास्ते जाइए। खींची जा रही electrical power है emf into current, two point seven times zero point three zero, यानी zero point eight one watts. इसे I squared R से check कीजिए: zero point three zero squared times nine point zero, वही zero point eight one. वो power mechanically दी जा रही है, और rotation के लिए mechanical power होती है torque into omega. तो torque है power बटा omega, zero point eight one बटा fifty, यानी one point six two times ten to the minus two newton metres. और part d वही zero point eight one watts है, यानी वो mechanical power जो agent को magnetic braking torque के ख़िलाफ़ देनी पड़ती है। उसका हर watt आख़िर में R की heat बन जाता है।

sections.title: The four pitfalls of motional emf, and the pro-tip that saves the day

board_events.text: Pitfall 1: ignoring the geometry in Bvl

The clean formula needs velocity, field, and rod MUTUALLY perpendicular. If the velocity makes an angle, only the perpendicular component generates emf. Use $\varepsilon = Bvl\sin\theta$ with the right theta, or fall back on the cross-product form.
Pitfall 2: assuming a moving rod always carries current
An isolated rod develops a voltage across its ends but NO sustained current. Current needs a closed circuit whose enclosed flux changes.
Pitfall 3: treating motional emf as separate from Faraday's law

They are the same law. Never double-count by adding a motional emf and a flux-change emf for the same effect. The exception: setups where the field ALSO varies in time. Then you genuinely add the two contributions.
Pitfall 4: misunderstanding laminations
Laminations do not block magnetism. They raise the resistance of eddy-current loops. And remember, hysteresis loss and eddy-current loss are different problems with different fixes.

Pro-tip: anchor every rod-on-rails problem to emf = Bvl and let the chain cascade to current, force, then power. For terminal velocity, never solve a differential equation under exam pressure. Just set driving force equal to magnetic retarding force and solve algebraically.

segments.text: Let me gather the four ways this subtopic takes marks off you, and finish with the pro-tip that makes the whole thing mechanical.

Pitfall one, ignoring the geometry inside B v l. That clean formula needs three things mutually perpendicular: velocity, field, and rod. It is not a universal formula, it is the answer to one specific arrangement. If the velocity makes an angle instead, only the perpendicular component generates emf, so you use B v l sin theta with the correct theta, or you fall back on the cross-product form. Check the geometry before you reach for the formula, every single time.
Pitfall two, and this one is conceptually deep, so it is worth getting right rather than memorising. Assuming a moving rod always carries a current.

An isolated rod develops a real voltage across its ends, but no sustained current at all. Current needs a closed circuit whose enclosed flux is changing. Emf is one thing, current is another, and this chapter tests the difference repeatedly.
Pitfall three, treating motional emf as separate physics from Faraday's law.

We derived the same B v l by both routes precisely to kill this idea. Never double-count by adding a motional emf and a flux-change emf for one single effect. The one genuine exception is a setup where the field also varies in time on top of the motion. Then there really are two contributions, and you do add them.
Pitfall four, misunderstanding what laminations are for.

Students write that laminations block magnetism. They do not, and they are specifically designed not to, because the flux is the useful part. What they do is raise the resistance of the eddy-current loops by breaking wide paths into many narrow insulated ones, which cuts the I squared R heat loss. And keep hysteresis loss separate in your head: that is fixed by choosing a soft magnetic material, an entirely different mechanism.

<whisper> Now the pro-tip. For any rod-on-rails problem, anchor everything to emf equals B v l and let the chain cascade: divide by R for current, multiply by B l for force, multiply by v again for power. And for terminal velocity, do not solve a differential equation under exam pressure. Just set the driving force equal to the magnetic retarding force and solve algebraically. That single habit turns a five minute problem into a one minute problem.
अब वो चार तरीक़े इकट्ठा करती हूँ जिनसे ये subtopic आपके marks काटता है, और आख़िर में वो pro-tip जो पूरी चीज़ को mechanical बना देती है।

Pitfall एक, B v l के अंदर की geometry नज़रअंदाज़ करना। उस साफ़ formula के लिए तीन चीज़ों का आपस में perpendicular होना ज़रूरी है: velocity, field, और rod. ये universal formula नहीं है, ये एक ख़ास arrangement का जवाब है। अगर velocity किसी angle पर है, तो सिर्फ़ perpendicular component emf बनाता है, तो आप सही theta के साथ B v l sin theta इस्तेमाल कीजिए, या cross-product form पर लौटिए। Formula उठाने से पहले हर बार geometry check कीजिए।
Pitfall दो, और ये conceptually गहरी है, तो इसे रटने की जगह समझना ज़रूरी है। ये मान लेना कि चलता हुआ rod हमेशा current देता है।

अकेले rod के सिरों पर असली voltage बनता है, लेकिन कोई लगातार current नहीं। Current के लिए बंद circuit चाहिए जिसकी enclosed flux बदल रही हो। Emf एक चीज़ है, current दूसरी, और ये chapter बार-बार यही फ़र्क़ जाँचता है।
Pitfall तीन, motional emf को Faraday's law से अलग physics समझना।

हमने वही B v l दोनों रास्तों से इसीलिए निकाला था कि ये सोच ख़त्म हो जाए। एक ही effect के लिए motional emf और flux-change emf जोड़कर दोहरी गिनती कभी मत कीजिए। एक असली exception है, वो setup जहाँ motion के साथ-साथ field भी समय के साथ बदल रही हो। तब सचमुच दो contributions होते हैं, और आप उन्हें जोड़ते हैं।
Pitfall चार, laminations किस लिए होती हैं ये ग़लत समझना।

Students लिख देते हैं कि laminations magnetism को रोकती हैं। वो नहीं रोकतीं, और उन्हें ख़ास तौर पर ऐसा बनाया जाता है कि न रोकें, क्योंकि flux तो काम की चीज़ है। वो करती ये हैं कि चौड़े रास्तों को कई पतले insulated रास्तों में तोड़कर eddy-current loops की resistance बढ़ा देती हैं, जिससे I squared R की heat loss घट जाती है। और hysteresis loss को दिमाग़ में अलग रखिए: वो soft magnetic material चुनकर ठीक होती है, बिलकुल अलग तरीक़ा।

<whisper> अब pro-tip. किसी भी rod-on-rails problem में सब कुछ emf equals B v l पर टिकाइए और chain चलने दीजिए: current के लिए R से भाग, force के लिए B l से गुणा, power के लिए फिर v से गुणा। और terminal velocity के लिए, exam के दबाव में differential equation मत हल कीजिए। बस driving force को magnetic retarding force के बराबर रखकर algebra से हल कीजिए। यही एक आदत पाँच मिनट की problem को एक मिनट की problem बना देती है।

sections.title: Self-induction: a coil that changes its own flux

board_events.text: So far the flux was changed by something EXTERNAL
A moving magnet, a moving rod, a neighbouring field. Now a subtle and beautiful twist.
A coil carrying a CHANGING current changes its OWN flux, and so induces an emf in itself. This is self-induction.
The cleanest way to feel this: inertia

board_events.text: A loaded bullock cart resists being set into motion, and once rolling, resists being stopped. That reluctance is mechanical inertia, which we call mass.
A coil behaves exactly like this toward current. Switch on, and it fights the rising current. Switch off, and it fights the collapse.
Notice: the coil does NOT oppose current itself. A steady current flows through freely. It opposes CHANGES in current.

segments.text: Everything in this chapter so far has had the flux changed by something external. A magnet moving in, a rod sliding along rails, a neighbouring coil switching on. Something outside our circuit did the work.
Now comes a subtle and rather beautiful twist, and it is the idea that makes this subtopic worth its weight in exam marks.

<curious> A coil carrying a changing current changes its own flux. Its own current makes its own field, that field threads its own turns, and if the current changes, that flux changes, and Faraday's law fires. The coil induces an emf in itself. This is self-induction.
The cleanest way to actually feel what this means is not a formula but an analogy, and it is one you already understand from mechanics: inertia.
Look at the two panels. On the left, mechanical inertia. On the right, its electrical cousin.

Think of a loaded bullock cart. It resists being set into motion, you have to push hard to get it rolling. And once it is rolling, it resists being stopped. That reluctance to change its state of motion is mechanical inertia, which we call mass.

A coil behaves exactly like this, but toward current instead of motion. Switch the circuit on, and the coil fights the rising current, slowing its climb. Switch it off, and the coil fights the collapse, trying to keep the current going. This is why inductance is nicknamed electrical inertia. It is the electrical cousin of mass.

And now the distinction that separates a student who understands this from one who has memorised a phrase. The coil does not oppose current. A steady current flows through an inductor perfectly freely, with no opposition at all. What it opposes is changes in current. Hold onto that, because it decides several exam questions on its own.
इस chapter में अब तक flux को हमेशा किसी बाहरी चीज़ ने बदला था। कोई magnet अंदर आया, कोई rod rails पर सरका, कोई पड़ोसी coil on हुई। हमारे circuit के बाहर की किसी चीज़ ने काम किया।
अब आता है एक subtle और बेहद ख़ूबसूरत मोड़, और यही वो idea है जो इस subtopic को exam marks में सोने के भाव बेचता है।

<curious> जिस coil में बदलता हुआ current बह रहा है, वो अपनी ही flux बदल देती है। उसका अपना current उसकी अपनी field बनाता है, वो field उसके अपने turns से गुज़रती है, और अगर current बदले तो वो flux बदलती है, और Faraday's law चल पड़ता है। Coil ख़ुद अपने अंदर emf induce कर लेती है। यही है self-induction.
इसका असली मतलब महसूस करने का सबसे साफ़ तरीक़ा कोई formula नहीं, एक analogy है, और वो आप mechanics से पहले से जानते हैं: inertia.
दोनों panels देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ mechanical inertia. दाईं तरफ़ उसका electrical भाई।

एक लदी हुई बैलगाड़ी सोचिए। वो चलना शुरू करने का विरोध करती है, चलाने के लिए ज़ोर लगाना पड़ता है। और एक बार चल पड़े तो रुकने का विरोध करती है। अपनी motion की हालत बदलने की यही अनिच्छा mechanical inertia है, जिसे हम mass कहते हैं।

Coil बिलकुल ऐसा ही बर्ताव करती है, बस motion की जगह current के प्रति। Circuit on कीजिए, coil बढ़ते current से लड़ती है, उसकी चढ़ाई धीमी करती है। Off कीजिए, coil गिरावट से लड़ती है, current को बनाए रखने की कोशिश करती है। इसीलिए inductance को electrical inertia कहा जाता है। ये mass का electrical भाई है।

और अब वो फ़र्क़ जो समझने वाले student को रटने वाले से अलग करता है। Coil current का विरोध नहीं करती। Inductor में steady current बिलकुल आज़ादी से बहता है, कोई विरोध नहीं। वो विरोध करती है current के बदलाव का। इसे पकड़े रखिए, क्योंकि अकेले यही बात कई exam questions तय कर देती है।

<text x="386" y="196" font-family="Helvetica" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#b3402f" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">dI/dt is enormous</text>
<text x="386" y="216" font-family="Helvetica" font-size="11" fill="#22303c" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">The coil answers with a</text>
<text x="386" y="232" font-family="Helvetica" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#b3402f" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">huge back-emf</text>

<text x="200" y="242" font-family="Helvetica" font-size="12" fill="#2f7d5a" text-anchor="middle" paint-order="stroke fill" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="2px">The bigger the inductance, the angrier the spark</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: As the switch breaks, the current is forced to drop to zero almost instantly.
So $dI/dt$ is enormous. And the induced emf is $-L\,dI/dt$, so the coil generates a large BACK-EMF.
That back-emf pushes the current across the opening gap, and the air itself conducts for an instant. That glowing bridge is the spark.
The bigger the inductance, the angrier the spark
This is why heavy inductive loads need switches designed for it. The coil is not being difficult. It is obeying Lenz's law: it opposes the collapse you are imposing.

segments.text: Let me connect this to something you have almost certainly seen with your own eyes, without knowing what you were looking at.
You unplug a fan, or you switch off an old tube-light with a choke in it, and a tiny blue spark jumps at the switch contact. That spark is self-induction, caught in the act.
Look at the circuit. Battery, coil, switch. Everything running happily with a steady current. And then the switch begins to open.
Here is what the coil experiences. As the switch breaks, the current is forced to drop from its full value to zero in almost no time at all. Not gradually. Practically instantly.

<excited> Now put that into the formula. The induced emf is minus L times d I by d t, and d I by d t is enormous, because a large change is happening in a tiny time. So the coil generates a large back-emf, far larger than the battery voltage that was driving it.

And that back-emf has to go somewhere. It pushes the current across the opening gap, and the voltage becomes high enough that the air itself briefly conducts. That glowing bridge of conducting air is the spark you see.

Which gives a nice qualitative rule: the bigger the inductance, the angrier the spark. A small coil gives a faint blue flicker. A large industrial inductor can produce a bright, damaging arc, which is exactly why heavy inductive loads need switches specifically designed to handle it.

And notice the coil is not being difficult here. It is doing precisely what Lenz's law says it must. You are imposing a collapse of current, so it opposes that collapse by trying to keep the current flowing. The spark is that opposition made visible.
अब इसे उस चीज़ से जोड़ती हूँ जो आपने लगभग ज़रूर अपनी आँखों से देखी है, बिना जाने कि आप क्या देख रहे थे।
आप fan का plug निकालते हैं, या choke वाली पुरानी tube-light बंद करते हैं, और switch के contact पर एक नन्हीं नीली चिंगारी कौंध जाती है। वो चिंगारी self-induction है, रंगे हाथों पकड़ी हुई।
Circuit देखिए। Battery, coil, switch. सब ख़ुशी-ख़ुशी steady current पर चल रहा है। और फिर switch खुलना शुरू होता है।
अब देखिए coil के साथ क्या गुज़रती है। जैसे ही switch टूटता है, current को अपनी पूरी value से zero तक गिरने पर मजबूर कर दिया जाता है, लगभग बिना किसी समय के। धीरे-धीरे नहीं। practically तुरंत।

<excited> अब इसे formula में डालिए। Induced emf है minus L times d I by d t, और d I by d t बहुत विशाल है, क्योंकि बहुत छोटे समय में बहुत बड़ा बदलाव हो रहा है। तो coil एक बड़ी back-emf पैदा कर देती है, उस battery voltage से कहीं बड़ी जो उसे चला रही थी।

और उस back-emf को कहीं तो जाना है। वो current को खुलते हुए gap के आर-पार धकेलती है, और voltage इतना ऊँचा हो जाता है कि हवा ख़ुद कुछ पल के लिए conduct करने लगती है। conducting हवा का वही चमकता पुल आपको चिंगारी के रूप में दिखता है।

इससे एक अच्छा qualitative नियम मिलता है: inductance जितनी बड़ी, चिंगारी उतनी ग़ुस्सैल। छोटी coil एक हल्की नीली झिलमिलाहट देती है। बड़ा industrial inductor एक तेज़, नुक़सानदेह arc बना सकता है, और ठीक इसीलिए भारी inductive loads के लिए ख़ास तौर पर बने switches चाहिए होते हैं।

और ग़ौर कीजिए, coil यहाँ ज़िद नहीं कर रही। वो ठीक वही कर रही है जो Lenz's law कहता है। आप current का ढहना थोप रहे हैं, तो वो उस ढहने का विरोध करती है, current को बहता रखने की कोशिश करके। चिंगारी उसी विरोध का दिखाई देने वाला रूप है।

sections.title: Mutual induction, and the reciprocity you should hold onto

board_events.text: Now bring a SECOND coil nearby
When the current in the first coil changes, its changing magnetic field threads the second coil too, inducing an emf there.
With no wire connecting them. This is mutual induction.

board_events.text: It is the principle behind transformers, the wireless charging pad for your phone, an induction cooktop heating a pan, and the metal detector at an airport.
The coupling quantity is the mutual inductance M. A big M means the two coils talk strongly. A small M means they barely notice each other.
A lovely fact worth holding onto
Mutual induction is perfectly RECIPROCAL. Coil 1 influences coil 2 exactly as strongly as coil 2 influences coil 1. There is a single number M for the pair.

segments.text: We have looked at a coil acting on itself. Now bring a second coil nearby and watch what happens between them.

When the current in the first coil changes, its magnetic field changes with it. And that changing field does not politely stay inside coil one. It threads coil two as well. So the flux through coil two changes, and by Faraday's law, an emf is induced there.

<excited> And here is the part worth pausing on. There is no wire connecting the two coils. Nothing joins them electrically. Energy crosses that gap purely through the magnetic field. This is mutual induction.

Look at the diagram. Coil one on the left with its changing current, field lines running across the gap, coil two on the right with an emf appearing in it, and no connection whatsoever between the two circuits.

This is not an exotic laboratory effect. It is the principle behind the transformer on your street pole, the wireless charging pad you drop your phone onto, the induction cooktop heating a pan, and the metal detector you walk through at an airport. All the same physics.

The quantity that measures the coupling is the mutual inductance, written M. A big M means the two coils talk to each other strongly, so a modest change in one produces a healthy emf in the other. A small M means they barely notice each other.
Now a lovely fact that you should hold onto, because it saves genuine work in problems. Mutual induction is perfectly reciprocal.

Coil one influences coil two exactly as strongly as coil two influences coil one. Not approximately, not usually. Exactly. So there is a single number M for the pair, and M one two equals M two one. We will prove it shortly, and then we will use it to dodge a very unpleasant integral.
हमने देखा कि coil अपने ऊपर कैसे असर डालती है। अब पास में एक दूसरी coil लाइए और देखिए उन दोनों के बीच क्या होता है।

जब पहली coil का current बदलता है, तो उसके साथ उसकी magnetic field भी बदलती है। और वो बदलती field शराफ़त से coil one के अंदर नहीं बैठी रहती। वो coil two से भी गुज़रती है। तो coil two की flux बदलती है, और Faraday's law के मुताबिक़ वहाँ emf induce हो जाती है।
<excited> और अब वो हिस्सा जिस पर रुकना चाहिए। दोनों coils के बीच कोई तार नहीं है। कोई electrical जोड़ नहीं। Energy उस खाली जगह को सिर्फ़ magnetic field के ज़रिए पार करती है। यही mutual induction है।
Diagram देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ coil one अपने बदलते current के साथ, बीच में field lines खाली जगह पार करती हुईं, दाईं तरफ़ coil two जिसमें emf आ रही है, और दोनों circuits के बीच कोई connection नहीं।
ये कोई अजीब laboratory वाला effect नहीं है। यही आपके street pole के transformer, उस wireless charging pad, induction cooktop, और airport के metal detector के पीछे का सिद्धांत है। सब एक ही physics.

इस coupling को नापने वाली quantity है mutual inductance, जिसे M लिखते हैं। बड़ा M मतलब दोनों coils आपस में ज़ोरदार बात करती हैं, तो एक में मामूली बदलाव दूसरी में अच्छी ख़ासी emf बना देता है। छोटा M मतलब वो एक दूसरे को मुश्किल से ही notice करती हैं।
अब एक ख़ूबसूरत बात जो पकड़े रखनी चाहिए, क्योंकि ये problems में सचमुच मेहनत बचाती है। Mutual induction पूरी तरह reciprocal है।

Coil one, coil two पर ठीक उतना ही असर डालती है जितना coil two, coil one पर। लगभग नहीं, आम तौर पर नहीं। बिलकुल बराबर। तो जोड़ी के लिए एक ही number M होता है, और M one two equals M two one. हम इसे थोड़ी देर में prove करेंगे, और फिर इसका इस्तेमाल एक बेहद कष्टदायक integral से बचने में करेंगे।

sections.title: What L and M actually depend on, and what they never do

board_events.text: The single most important property of L and M
They depend ONLY on geometry and the surrounding medium. Number of turns, area, length, core permeability, separation and relative orientation. They do NOT depend on the current or the emf.
Exactly like capacitance, which is fixed by plate geometry and the dielectric. A larger current gives more energy and more emf, but L itself is unchanged.
The solenoid formula has a hidden assumption
$L = \mu_0 n^2 A l$ assumes a LONG solenoid, so the interior field is uniform and end effects are negligible.
