board_events.text: Mutual inductance is largest when the coils share flux fully: coaxial, wound on the same core, with k tending to 1. It vanishes when their axes are perpendicular, k tending to 0.
In general $M = k\sqrt{L_1 L_2}$ with k between 0 and 1. And finally: a steady current, however large, induces no self or mutual emf. Only a CHANGING current does.

segments.text: Four conditions again, and the first one is the single most important property of these two quantities. Get this one wrong and a whole class of conceptual questions goes with it.

<whisper> L and M depend only on geometry and the surrounding medium. The number of turns, the area, the length, the permeability of the core, the separation between the coils and their relative orientation. That is the complete list. They do not depend on the current, and they do not depend on the emf.

The analogy that makes this stick is capacitance. A capacitor's capacitance is fixed by its plate geometry and its dielectric. Charging it up does not change its capacitance. Inductance works identically. Push a larger current through a coil and you get more stored energy and a larger emf, but L itself has not moved at all. N E E T asks this directly, in the form what does M not depend on, and the answer is the current.
Second condition, and this one is a hidden assumption inside a formula you are about to memorise.

The solenoid result, L equals mu nought n squared A l, assumes a long solenoid. Long enough that the field inside is genuinely uniform and the messy field near the two ends can be ignored. For a short, squat coil the formula is not reliable.
Third, look at the three arrangements on the board, running from perfect coupling to none at all.

Mutual inductance is largest when the coils share their flux fully, which means coaxial, wound tightly on the same core, with k approaching one. It falls as they separate and flux escapes. And it vanishes completely when their axes are perpendicular, with k going to zero, because then the flux of one simply does not thread the other.

In general M equals k times the square root of L one L two, with k lying between zero and one. And fourth, the condition that runs through this entire chapter: a steady current, however large, induces no self emf and no mutual emf. Only a changing current does anything at all.
फिर से चार conditions, और पहली वाली इन दोनों quantities की सबसे अहम property है। यही ग़लत हुई तो conceptual questions की एक पूरी श्रेणी हाथ से निकल जाती है।

<whisper> L और M सिर्फ़ geometry और आसपास के medium पर depend करते हैं। Turns की संख्या, area, length, core की permeability, coils के बीच की दूरी और उनका relative orientation. बस, पूरी list यही है। वो current पर depend नहीं करते, और emf पर भी नहीं।

जो analogy इसे चिपका देती है वो है capacitance. किसी capacitor की capacitance उसकी plate geometry और dielectric से तय होती है। उसे charge करने से capacitance नहीं बदलती। Inductance ठीक ऐसे ही चलती है। Coil में बड़ा current भेजिए तो ज़्यादा stored energy और बड़ी emf मिलेगी, लेकिन L ज़रा भी नहीं हिला। N E E T यही सीधे पूछता है, इस रूप में कि M किस पर depend नहीं करता, और जवाब है current.
दूसरी condition, और ये उस formula के अंदर छिपी हुई assumption है जिसे आप अभी याद करने वाले हैं।

Solenoid वाला result, L equals mu nought n squared A l, ये मानकर चलता है कि solenoid लंबा है। इतना लंबा कि अंदर की field सचमुच uniform हो और दोनों सिरों के पास की गड़बड़ field नज़रअंदाज़ की जा सके। छोटी, मोटी coil के लिए ये formula भरोसेमंद नहीं है।
तीसरी, board पर तीनों arrangements देखिए, perfect coupling से लेकर बिलकुल शून्य तक।

Mutual inductance सबसे बड़ी तब होती है जब coils अपनी flux पूरी तरह साझा करें, यानी coaxial, एक ही core पर कसकर लिपटी हुई, k एक के क़रीब। जैसे-जैसे वो दूर होती हैं और flux बाहर निकलती है, ये घटती है। और तब पूरी तरह ग़ायब हो जाती है जब उनकी axes perpendicular हों, k शून्य की तरफ़, क्योंकि तब एक की flux दूसरी से गुज़रती ही नहीं।

आम तौर पर M equals k times square root of L one L two, जहाँ k शून्य और एक के बीच होता है। और चौथी, वो condition जो पूरे chapter में दौड़ती है: steady current, चाहे कितना भी बड़ा हो, न self emf induce करता है न mutual. सिर्फ़ बदलता हुआ current ही कुछ करता है।

sections.title: Self-inductance: definition, solenoid, and stored energy

board_events.text: Defining self-inductance from flux linkage
The emf it produces
For a long solenoid

board_events.latex: L = \mu_0 n^2 A l = \frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l} \qquad \text{(with a core, multiply by } \mu_r)

board_events.text: Crucially $L \propto N^2$ for fixed coil geometry. Not N. Doubling the turns QUADRUPLES the inductance.
SI unit of L is the henry: 1 H equals 1 Wb per A, equals 1 V second per A, equals 1 ohm second, equals 1 J per A squared. Dimensional formula $[ML^2T^{-2}A^{-2}]$.

segments.text: Here is the formula set for self-inductance. Five results, and as before, notice they are one definition followed by its consequences.

We define L through flux linkage. The total flux linkage, N times the flux per turn, is proportional to the current driving it, and L is the constant of proportionality. So L equals N phi over I. That is the definition, and it works for any shape of coil, not just a solenoid.
From that definition and Faraday's law, the emf follows immediately.
Induced emf equals minus L times d I by d t. That minus sign is Lenz again, telling you it is a back-emf, opposing the change in current, not opposing the current.
Now the specific case you will use constantly: the long solenoid.

L equals mu nought n squared A l, or equivalently mu nought N squared A over l. Those two are the same formula, since n equals N over l. And if the solenoid has a magnetic core rather than air, you multiply by the relative permeability mu r, which can be in the hundreds or thousands.

<whisper> Now burn this in, because it is the single most common inductance mistake. L is proportional to N squared, not to N. Unwind a coil and rewind it with twice the turns on the same former, and the inductance does not double. It quadruples. J E E Main and N E E T both ask this, and both offer two L as the tempting wrong option.

Next, the energy. An inductor carrying current stores energy, one half L I squared. Notice it goes as I squared, exactly parallel to one half C V squared for a capacitor. And that energy is not sitting in the wire, it is stored in the magnetic field, with energy density B squared over two mu nought.

Finally the unit. The S I unit of inductance is the henry, and it has several equivalent forms worth recognising in a multiple choice question: one henry equals one weber per ampere, equals one volt second per ampere, equals one ohm second, equals one joule per ampere squared. The dimensional formula is M L squared T to the minus two A to the minus two, which is just the flux dimension divided by current.
ये रहा self-inductance का formula set. पाँच results, और पहले की तरह ग़ौर कीजिए कि ये एक definition और उसके नतीजे हैं।

हम L को flux linkage से define करते हैं। कुल flux linkage, यानी N times प्रति turn flux, उसे चलाने वाले current के proportional है, और L वही proportionality constant है। तो L equals N phi बटा I. यही definition है, और ये coil की किसी भी शक्ल के लिए चलती है, सिर्फ़ solenoid के लिए नहीं।
उसी definition और Faraday's law से emf तुरंत निकल आती है।
Induced emf equals minus L times d I by d t. वो minus sign फिर से Lenz है, जो बता रहा है कि ये back-emf है, current के बदलाव का विरोध करती हुई, current का नहीं।
अब वो ख़ास case जो आप लगातार इस्तेमाल करेंगे: लंबा solenoid.

L equals mu nought n squared A l, या बराबर रूप से mu nought N squared A बटा l. ये दोनों एक ही formula हैं, क्योंकि n equals N बटा l. और अगर solenoid में हवा की जगह magnetic core हो, तो relative permeability mu r से multiply कीजिए, जो सैकड़ों या हज़ारों में हो सकती है।

<whisper> अब इसे गाँठ बाँध लीजिए, क्योंकि inductance की सबसे common ग़लती यही है। L, N squared के proportional है, N के नहीं। Coil खोलकर उसी former पर दोगुने turns के साथ लपेटिए, inductance दोगुनी नहीं होती। चार गुनी होती है। J E E Main और N E E T दोनों यही पूछते हैं, और दोनों two L को लुभावने ग़लत option की तरह रखते हैं।

आगे, energy. Current ले जाता हुआ inductor energy store करता है, one half L I squared. ग़ौर कीजिए ये I squared के साथ जाती है, बिलकुल capacitor के one half C V squared के समानांतर। और वो energy तार में नहीं बैठी है, वो magnetic field में store है, जिसका energy density है B squared बटा two mu nought.

आख़िर में unit. Inductance का S I unit है henry, और इसके कई बराबर रूप हैं जिन्हें multiple choice में पहचानना चाहिए: one henry equals one weber per ampere, equals one volt second per ampere, equals one ohm second, equals one joule per ampere squared. Dimensional formula है M L squared T to the minus two A to the minus two, जो बस flux का dimension बटा current है।

sections.title: Mutual inductance, reciprocity, coupling, and combinations

board_events.text: Defining mutual inductance
Two coaxial solenoids

board_events.latex: M = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 A l = \frac{\mu_0 N_1 N_2 A}{l}

board_events.text: Reciprocity and coupling

board_events.latex: M_{12} = M_{21} = M \qquad M = k\sqrt{L_1 L_2}, \quad 0 \le k \le 1

board_events.text: M is the GEOMETRIC mean of the two self-inductances, scaled by k. Not the sum. Not the arithmetic mean.
Combinations, when mutual coupling is negligible: in series $L = L_1 + L_2$; in parallel $L = L_1L_2/(L_1+L_2)$. Note these follow the RESISTOR rules, not the capacitor ones.

segments.text: Now the mutual inductance set, and it mirrors the self-inductance set almost line for line, which makes it much less to remember than it looks.

The definition follows the same shape. The flux linkage in coil two, N two phi two, is proportional to the current in coil one, and M is that constant of proportionality. So M equals N two phi two over I one. Note carefully which subscript is where: flux in the second coil, current in the first.
And the emf follows immediately. The emf induced in coil two is minus M times d I one by d t. Again, changing current in coil one, emf in coil two, coupled through M.
Now the standard geometry you must know, two coaxial solenoids with one sitting inside the other.
For that pair, which is the C B S E derivation, the result is mu nought n one n two A l, or equivalently mu nought N one N two A over l.
Notice how symmetric that expression is in the two coils. It contains n one and n two on completely equal footing. That symmetry is not an accident, and it is already hinting at the next result.
Reciprocity: M one two equals M two one equals a single M. And then the coupling relation, M equals k times the square root of L one L two, with k between zero and one.

<excited> Now the trap hidden in that square root, and it catches people every single year. M is the geometric mean of the two self-inductances, scaled by k. It is not the sum. It is not the arithmetic mean. So for two millihenry and eight millihenry perfectly coupled, M is the square root of sixteen, which is four millihenry, not ten and not five.

Finally, combinations, for the case where the mutual coupling between the two inductors is negligible. In series, L equals L one plus L two. In parallel, the product over the sum. And here is the memory hook: inductors combine by the resistor rules, not the capacitor rules. Students who have just finished capacitors often get these exactly backwards.
अब mutual inductance का set, और ये self-inductance वाले set की लगभग line दर line नक़ल है, जिससे ये दिखने में जितना है उससे कहीं कम याद करना पड़ता है।

Definition वही शक्ल लेती है। Coil two की flux linkage, N two phi two, coil one के current के proportional है, और M वही proportionality constant है। तो M equals N two phi two बटा I one. ध्यान से देखिए कौन सा subscript कहाँ है: flux दूसरी coil की, current पहली का।
और emf तुरंत निकल आती है। Coil two में induce होने वाली emf है minus M times d I one by d t. फिर वही, coil one में बदलता current, coil two में emf, और बीच में M का जोड़।
अब वो standard geometry जो आपको आनी ही चाहिए, दो coaxial solenoids जिनमें एक दूसरे के अंदर बैठा है।
उस जोड़ी के लिए, जो कि C B S E derivation है, result है mu nought n one n two A l, या बराबर रूप से mu nought N one N two A बटा l.
ग़ौर कीजिए वो expression दोनों coils के मामले में कितना symmetric है। उसमें n one और n two बिलकुल बराबरी के दर्जे पर हैं। ये symmetry इत्तेफ़ाक़ नहीं है, और ये अगले result का इशारा पहले ही दे रही है।
Reciprocity: M one two equals M two one equals एक ही M. और फिर coupling relation, M equals k times square root of L one L two, जहाँ k शून्य और एक के बीच है।

<excited> अब उस square root में छिपा trap, जो हर साल लोगों को पकड़ता है। M दोनों self-inductances का geometric mean है, k से scaled. वो sum नहीं है। वो arithmetic mean भी नहीं है। तो two millihenry और eight millihenry perfectly coupled के लिए M है square root of sixteen, यानी four millihenry, न कि ten और न five.

आख़िर में combinations, उस हालत के लिए जब दोनों inductors के बीच mutual coupling नज़रअंदाज़ करने लायक़ हो। Series में L equals L one plus L two. Parallel में product बटा sum. और ये रहा याद रखने का हुक: inductors, resistors के नियमों से जुड़ते हैं, capacitors के नियमों से नहीं। जो students अभी-अभी capacitors ख़त्म करके आए हैं वो अक्सर इन्हें बिलकुल उल्टा कर देते हैं।

board_events.text: The field inside a long solenoid is uniform, which is the whole reason we insisted on long:
Flux through ONE turn is $\Phi_B = BA = \mu_0 n I A$. Now multiply by the number of turns to get total flux linkage:

board_events.latex: N\Phi_B = (nl)(\mu_0 n I A) = \mu_0 n^2 A l \, I
\text{But } N\Phi_B = LI, \text{ so comparing: } \quad L = \mu_0 n^2 A l = \frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l}

segments.text: This is a three mark C B S E derivation that appears almost every year, so let us do it cleanly, in the order an examiner wants to read it.

Set up the geometry first and state it explicitly. A long solenoid of length l, cross-sectional area A, wound with n turns per unit length, so the total number of turns is N equals n l. It carries a current I.
Look at the figure while we work. Coils along the length, uniform field arrows running straight down the middle, area A across the face.

Now quote the field inside. For a long solenoid the interior field is uniform, and this is the entire reason we insisted on the word long. If it were short, the field would sag near the ends and none of what follows would be clean.
That field is mu nought n I. Straight from the previous chapter, and in a derivation question you are allowed to quote it, but you should say where it comes from.
Next, the flux through one single turn. It is B times A, which is mu nought n I A. Note this is per turn, and that distinction is where students slip.
Now multiply by the number of turns to get the total flux linkage. N is n l, so the linkage is n l times mu nought n I A, which collects to mu nought n squared A l, all multiplied by I.

<excited> And now the finish, which is pure pattern matching. By definition, flux linkage equals L I. We have just shown flux linkage equals mu nought n squared A l times I. So L must be mu nought n squared A l. Substituting n equals N over l gives the other form, mu nought N squared A over l. And look at what the answer contains: n, A, l and the medium. Geometry only. No current anywhere. The derivation has confirmed exactly what intuition promised.
ये तीन marks की C B S E derivation है जो लगभग हर साल आती है, तो इसे साफ़-सुथरे तरीक़े से करते हैं, उसी क्रम में जिसमें examiner पढ़ना चाहता है।
पहले geometry set कीजिए और साफ़-साफ़ लिखिए। एक लंबा solenoid, length l, cross-sectional area A, प्रति unit length n turns के साथ लिपटा हुआ, तो कुल turns हैं N equals n l. उसमें current I बह रहा है।
काम करते हुए figure देखते रहिए। लंबाई भर coils, बीचोंबीच सीधी जाती uniform field की arrows, और सामने की तरफ़ area A.

अब अंदर की field लिखिए। लंबे solenoid के लिए अंदर की field uniform होती है, और शब्द लंबा पर हमारे ज़ोर देने की पूरी वजह यही है। अगर वो छोटा होता, तो सिरों के पास field ढल जाती और आगे कुछ भी साफ़ न रहता।
वो field है mu nought n I. सीधे पिछले chapter से, और derivation वाले question में आप इसे quote कर सकते हैं, लेकिन ये बताना चाहिए कि ये कहाँ से आई।
अगला क़दम, एक अकेले turn से गुज़रती flux. वो है B into A, यानी mu nought n I A. ध्यान दीजिए ये प्रति turn है, और यहीं students फिसलते हैं।
अब turns की संख्या से multiply करके कुल flux linkage निकालिए। N है n l, तो linkage है n l times mu nought n I A, जो सिमटकर बनता है mu nought n squared A l, और ये सब I से multiplied.

<excited> और अब समापन, जो शुद्ध pattern matching है। Definition के मुताबिक़ flux linkage equals L I. हमने अभी दिखाया कि flux linkage equals mu nought n squared A l times I. तो L ज़रूर mu nought n squared A l होगा। n equals N बटा l रखने पर दूसरा रूप मिलता है, mu nought N squared A बटा l. और देखिए answer में क्या है: n, A, l और medium. सिर्फ़ geometry. कहीं कोई current नहीं। Derivation ने ठीक वही पक्का कर दिया जो intuition ने वादा किया था।

board_events.text: The clever choice: pass current through the OUTER one. Its interior field is uniform and simple, and it threads every turn of the inner coil.
Flux linkage with S1, which has $N_1 = n_1 l$ turns, is the field times the area times the number of turns:

board_events.latex: N_1\Phi_1 = (n_1 l)(\mu_0 n_2 I_2)(A) = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 A l\, I_2 \;\Rightarrow\; M_{12} = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 A l

board_events.text: Driving the inner solenoid instead and computing the linkage with the outer returns the SAME expression. Hence $M_{12} = M_{21} = M$. That is the reciprocity theorem, and it is a genuine labour-saver.

segments.text: Now the companion derivation, mutual inductance of two coaxial solenoids. This is the other three mark C B S E favourite, and it contains one genuinely clever choice.

Set up the geometry. An inner solenoid, call it S one, with n one turns per unit length and cross-sectional area A, sits fully inside an outer solenoid S two, which has n two turns per unit length. Both have the same length l.
Look at the figure. Outer winding in blue, inner winding in red sitting inside it, both sharing the same axis and the same length.

Now the clever choice, and this is the step worth understanding rather than copying. We pass the current through the outer solenoid, not the inner one. Why? Because the field inside a long solenoid is the simple uniform result we already know, and the inner coil sits entirely within that uniform region. Every turn of the inner coil is threaded by the same clean field.
So the outer solenoid's interior field is mu nought n two I two, where I two is the current we chose to drive through it.

Now compute the flux linkage with the inner coil. The inner coil has N one equals n one l turns, each of area A, each threaded by that field. So the linkage is n one l times mu nought n two I two times A.

Collect the terms and it becomes mu nought n one n two A l, all multiplied by I two. And since flux linkage equals M one two times I two by definition, we simply read off M one two equals mu nought n one n two A l.

<whisper> Now the part that earns marks and saves time. If instead you drive the inner solenoid and compute the linkage with the outer one, the algebra returns exactly the same expression. So M one two equals M two one. That is the reciprocity theorem, and it is a genuine labour-saver: when one direction is easy to calculate and the other is horrid, compute the easy one and reciprocity hands you the answer for free. We exploit that trick directly in worked example four.
अब साथ वाली derivation, दो coaxial solenoids की mutual inductance. ये दूसरी तीन marks वाली C B S E favourite है, और इसमें एक सचमुच चालाक चुनाव छिपा है।

Geometry set कीजिए। एक भीतरी solenoid, इसे S one कहिए, जिसमें प्रति unit length n one turns और cross-sectional area A है, वो पूरी तरह एक बाहरी solenoid S two के अंदर रखा है, जिसमें प्रति unit length n two turns हैं। दोनों की length एक ही l है।
Figure देखिए। नीले रंग में बाहरी winding, उसके अंदर लाल रंग में भीतरी winding, दोनों की एक ही axis और एक ही length.

अब वो चालाक चुनाव, और यही वो क़दम है जिसे नक़ल करने की जगह समझना चाहिए। हम current बाहरी solenoid में भेजते हैं, भीतरी में नहीं। क्यों? क्योंकि लंबे solenoid के अंदर की field वही simple uniform result है जो हमें पहले से पता है, और भीतरी coil पूरी तरह उसी uniform इलाक़े में बैठी है। भीतरी coil का हर turn उसी साफ़ field से गुज़रता है।
तो बाहरी solenoid के अंदर की field है mu nought n two I two, जहाँ I two वो current है जिसे हमने चलाने के लिए चुना।

अब भीतरी coil के साथ flux linkage निकालिए। भीतरी coil में N one equals n one l turns हैं, हर एक का area A, और हर एक उसी field से गुज़र रहा है। तो linkage है n one l times mu nought n two I two times A.

Terms इकट्ठा कीजिए और बनता है mu nought n one n two A l, ये सब I two से multiplied. और चूँकि definition से flux linkage equals M one two times I two, हम सीधे पढ़ लेते हैं M one two equals mu nought n one n two A l.

<whisper> अब वो हिस्सा जो marks दिलाता है और time बचाता है। अगर इसकी जगह आप भीतरी solenoid चलाएँ और बाहरी के साथ linkage निकालें, तो algebra बिलकुल वही expression लौटाता है। तो M one two equals M two one. यही reciprocity theorem है, और ये सचमुच मेहनत बचाता है: जब एक दिशा में निकालना आसान हो और दूसरी में भयानक, तो आसान वाली निकालिए और reciprocity आपको दूसरी का जवाब मुफ़्त में दे देता है। Worked example चार में हम यही चाल सीधे इस्तेमाल करेंगे।

board_events.text: The work done in pushing charge $dq = I\,dt$ against this emf in time dt is:
Again the dt cancels. Integrating from zero to the final current:
This energy is NOT lost. It is stored in the magnetic field itself.

board_events.latex: u_B = \frac{U}{Al} = \frac{\tfrac{1}{2}\mu_0 n^2 A l\, I_0^2}{Al} = \tfrac{1}{2}\mu_0 n^2 I_0^2 = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}

segments.text: Last derivation of this subtopic, and it answers a question you should already be asking: if the coil fights the current rising, then getting the current up there must have cost something. Where did that energy go?

So set the problem up. To build the current from zero to a final value I nought, an external source must do work against the back-emf, which is L times d I by d t. The coil resists the whole way, and the source pays for it.
Look at the graph while we work. L I plotted against I, a straight line through the origin, and the work is the shaded area underneath it.
Consider a small step. In time d t, a charge d q equals I d t is pushed against the back-emf. Work is emf times charge.

So d W equals L d I by d t, multiplied by I d t. And once again, exactly as in the induced-charge derivation, the d t cancels completely, leaving d W equals L I d I. That is one thin strip of the shaded area on the graph.
Again the d t cancels, exactly as it did in the induced-charge derivation. Now integrate both sides, from zero up to the final current I nought.
The integral of I d I is I squared over two, so the total work is one half L I nought squared. And that is the stored energy U.

<excited> Now the physically important question. This energy is not lost. It has not become heat, because we did no work against resistance. It is stored, and it is stored in the magnetic field itself.

To see that, divide the energy by the volume of the solenoid, which is A l. Substitute L equals mu nought n squared A l, and the A l cancels beautifully against the volume, leaving one half mu nought n squared I nought squared. And since B equals mu nought n I nought, that expression is exactly B squared over two mu nought. That is the magnetic energy density, and it is the direct analogue of one half epsilon nought E squared stored in a capacitor's electric field.

इस subtopic की आख़िरी derivation, और ये उस सवाल का जवाब देती है जो आपके मन में अब तक आ जाना चाहिए: अगर coil current के चढ़ने से लड़ती है, तो current को वहाँ तक पहुँचाने में कुछ तो ख़र्च हुआ होगा। वो energy गई कहाँ?

तो problem set कीजिए। Current को zero से आख़िरी value I nought तक बनाने के लिए, किसी बाहरी source को back-emf के ख़िलाफ़ काम करना पड़ता है, जो है L times d I by d t. Coil पूरे रास्ते विरोध करती है, और source उसकी क़ीमत चुकाता है।
काम करते हुए graph देखिए। I के सामने L I plotted, origin से जाती एक सीधी रेखा, और work उसके नीचे का shaded area है।
एक छोटा क़दम सोचिए। Time d t में, एक charge d q equals I d t को back-emf के ख़िलाफ़ धकेला जाता है। Work होता है emf into charge.

तो d W equals L d I by d t, into I d t. और एक बार फिर, बिलकुल induced-charge वाली derivation की तरह, d t पूरी तरह cancel हो जाता है, और बचता है d W equals L I d I. Graph पर shaded area की वही एक पतली पट्टी है।
एक बार फिर d t cancel हो जाता है, ठीक जैसे induced-charge वाली derivation में हुआ था। अब दोनों तरफ़ integrate कीजिए, zero से आख़िरी current I nought तक।
I d I का integral है I squared बटा two, तो कुल work है one half L I nought squared. और यही stored energy U है।
<excited> अब असली physical सवाल। ये energy खोई नहीं है। ये heat नहीं बनी, क्योंकि हमने resistance के ख़िलाफ़ कोई काम किया ही नहीं। ये store हुई है, और store हुई है ख़ुद magnetic field में।

ये देखने के लिए, energy को solenoid के volume से भाग दीजिए, जो है A l. उसमें L equals mu nought n squared A l रखिए, और A l बड़ी सफ़ाई से volume के साथ cancel हो जाता है, बचता है one half mu nought n squared I nought squared. और चूँकि B equals mu nought n I nought, वो expression बिलकुल B squared बटा two mu nought है। यही magnetic energy density है, और ये capacitor की electric field में जमा one half epsilon nought E squared का सीधा जुड़वाँ है।

board_events.text: Given: l = 0.40 m, N = 800, A = 5.0 cm squared = 5.0 times 10 to the minus 4 square metres, and dI/dt = 200 A per second.
Use the total-turns form here, since the question gives N and not n. Mixing the two forms is the classic error.

segments.text: A straightforward C B S E numerical to lock the solenoid formula in place. Two parts, and the second one falls out in a single line once you have the first.

A long air-cored solenoid is zero point four zero metres long, has eight hundred turns, and a cross-sectional area of five point zero square centimetres. Find its self-inductance, and then the magnitude of the self-induced emf when the current through it changes at two hundred amperes per second.
Look at the figure to keep the three quantities straight: N is the total turns, A is the face area, l is the length. Those three plus the medium are the entire answer.

Write your given values and do the conversion straight away. Length zero point four zero metres. Eight hundred turns. Area five point zero square centimetres, which is five point zero times ten to the minus four square metres. And the rate of change of current, two hundred amperes per second.

<whisper> Now a decision that costs marks if you get it wrong. There are two forms of the solenoid formula, one using little n which is turns per metre, and one using capital N which is total turns. The question gives you eight hundred turns in total, so use the capital N form. Plugging a total-turns number into the little n formula is the classic error here, and it will be off by a factor of l squared.

So L equals mu nought N squared A over l. Substitute: four pi times ten to the minus seven, times eight hundred squared, times five point zero times ten to the minus four, all over zero point four zero.

Work it in pieces. Eight hundred squared is six point four times ten to the five. Mu nought is one point two five six six times ten to the minus six. Multiply those together, multiply by the area, divide by the length, and you get one point zero times ten to the minus three henry, which is one point zero millihenry.

Part b is now immediate, and this is why part a was worth doing carefully. The magnitude of the self-induced emf is L times d I by d t, which is one point zero times ten to the minus three, times two hundred, giving zero point two zero volts. Note we take magnitudes and mention separately that the sign indicates a back-emf opposing the change.
एक सीधा-सादा C B S E numerical, solenoid वाले formula को पक्का करने के लिए। दो parts, और पहला निकल जाए तो दूसरा एक ही line में आ जाता है।

एक लंबा air-cored solenoid zero point four zero metres लंबा है, उसमें eight hundred turns हैं, और cross-sectional area five point zero square centimetres है। उसकी self-inductance निकालिए, और फिर self-induced emf का magnitude जब उसमें current two hundred amperes per second की दर से बदल रहा हो।
तीनों quantities साफ़ रखने के लिए figure देखिए: N कुल turns, A सामने का area, l लंबाई। यही तीन और medium मिलकर पूरा answer हैं।

अपनी given values लिखिए और conversion फ़ौरन कर लीजिए। Length zero point four zero metres. Eight hundred turns. Area five point zero square centimetres, यानी five point zero times ten to the minus four square metres. और current के बदलने की दर, two hundred amperes per second.

<whisper> अब एक फ़ैसला जो ग़लत हुआ तो marks ले जाता है। Solenoid formula के दो रूप हैं, एक छोटे n वाला जो प्रति metre turns है, और एक बड़े N वाला जो कुल turns है। Question आपको कुल eight hundred turns दे रहा है, तो बड़े N वाला रूप इस्तेमाल कीजिए। कुल turns का number छोटे n वाले formula में डालना यहाँ की classic ग़लती है, और answer l squared के factor से ग़लत आएगा।

तो L equals mu nought N squared A बटा l. Substitute कीजिए: four pi times ten to the minus seven, into eight hundred squared, into five point zero times ten to the minus four, ये सब बटा zero point four zero.

टुकड़ों में कीजिए। Eight hundred squared है six point four times ten to the five. Mu nought है one point two five six six times ten to the minus six. दोनों को multiply कीजिए, area से multiply कीजिए, length से भाग दीजिए, और मिलता है one point zero times ten to the minus three henry, यानी one point zero millihenry.

Part b अब तुरंत निकल आता है, और इसीलिए part a को ध्यान से करना ज़रूरी था। Self-induced emf का magnitude है L times d I by d t, यानी one point zero times ten to the minus three, into two hundred, जो देता है zero point two zero volts. ध्यान रहे हम magnitude ले रहे हैं और अलग से लिख देते हैं कि sign बताता है ये back-emf है जो change का विरोध करती है।

board_events.text: The trap: students reach for add them, giving 10 mH, or average them, giving 5 mH. Both wrong.
The fast, correct read
Mutual inductance from self-inductances is a GEOMETRIC mean, not a sum and not an arithmetic mean.
Memorise the FORM, not just the answer: perfect coupling gives the largest possible M, and that largest value is the geometric mean of the two self-inductances.

segments.text: Now a N E E T speed question, and this one is a pure formula-recognition trap. It takes about five seconds if you know the form and it goes badly wrong if you guess.

Two coils of self-inductance two millihenry and eight millihenry are wound tightly one over the other on the same core, so the coupling is essentially perfect, with k approximately equal to one. Estimate their mutual inductance.

Look at the leftmost arrangement in the figure. Tightly wound on a shared core is precisely the k approaching one case, where the two coils share essentially all of their flux. That is the maximum-coupling situation.

<curious> Here is the trap. Faced with two inductances and asked to combine them, students reach for the operations they know. Add them, and you get ten millihenry. Or average them, and you get five millihenry. Both of those numbers will be sitting in the options, waiting.
So let us get the correct read, and it is one line.
Mutual inductance obtained from two self-inductances is a geometric mean. Not a sum, not an arithmetic mean. The relation is M equals k times the square root of the product.
Substituting: k is one for perfect coupling, and the product of two and eight is sixteen. The square root of sixteen is four. So M is four millihenry.

<whisper> And here is the exam habit worth taking away. Do not memorise this answer, memorise the form. M equals k root L one L two. Perfect coupling gives the largest possible M, and that largest possible value is the geometric mean of the two self-inductances. Once the form is in your head, any version of this question, with any two numbers, takes seconds.
अब एक N E E T speed question, और ये शुद्ध formula-पहचान का trap है। Form पता हो तो पाँच second लगते हैं, और अंदाज़े से किया तो बुरी तरह ग़लत होता है।

Two millihenry और eight millihenry की self-inductance वाली दो coils एक ही core पर एक के ऊपर एक कसकर लपेटी गई हैं, तो coupling practically perfect है, k लगभग one. उनकी mutual inductance का अंदाज़ा लगाइए।

Figure में सबसे बाईं arrangement देखिए। एक ही core पर कसकर लिपटी हुई, यही तो k के one की तरफ़ जाने वाला case है, जहाँ दोनों coils practically अपनी पूरी flux साझा करती हैं। यही maximum coupling वाली हालत है।

<curious> अब trap देखिए। दो inductances सामने हों और उन्हें मिलाने को कहा जाए, तो students वही operations उठाते हैं जो उन्हें आते हैं। जोड़ दीजिए, मिलता है ten millihenry. या औसत निकाल लीजिए, मिलता है five millihenry. ये दोनों numbers options में बैठे इंतज़ार कर रहे होंगे।
तो सही पढ़ाई कर लेते हैं, और वो एक line की है।
दो self-inductances से निकलने वाली mutual inductance एक geometric mean होती है। न sum, न arithmetic mean. Relation है M equals k times square root of product.
Substitute कीजिए: perfect coupling के लिए k है one, और two तथा eight का गुणनफल है sixteen. Sixteen का square root है four. तो M है four millihenry.

<whisper> और अब वो exam की आदत जो साथ ले जाने लायक़ है। इस answer को मत रटिए, form को रटिए। M equals k root L one L two. Perfect coupling सबसे बड़ी संभव M देती है, और वो सबसे बड़ी value दोनों self-inductances का geometric mean होती है। एक बार form दिमाग़ में बैठ जाए, तो इस question का कोई भी रूप, किन्हीं भी दो numbers के साथ, seconds में निकलता है।

board_events.text: Find (a) the mutual inductance, (b) the emf induced in the secondary, and (c) the total charge that flows through the secondary.
For part (c), reuse the induced-charge logic from Subtopic 01, with flux linkage = MI. The time does not appear.

segments.text: This problem links the mutual-inductance derivation with Faraday's law and with the induced-charge result all the way back in subtopic one. Three subtopics in one question, which is exactly why J E E Main likes it.

Two coaxial solenoids of equal length zero point five zero metres and equal cross-sectional area four point zero square centimetres. The inner is wound with two thousand turns per metre, the outer with one thousand turns per metre. The outer one is the primary, and it carries a current that is switched off, dropping from five point zero amperes to zero in zero point zero one zero seconds. The secondary circuit has total resistance ten ohms.
The geometry is exactly the pair we derived. Look at the figure and note that the area A in the formula is the area of the inner solenoid, the one whose turns are being linked.
Three parts: the mutual inductance, the emf induced in the secondary, and the total charge that flows through the secondary.

Part a is a direct substitution into our derived formula. M equals mu nought n one n two A l. That is four pi times ten to the minus seven, times two thousand, times one thousand, times four point zero times ten to the minus four, times zero point five zero. Multiplying through gives five point zero times ten to the minus four henry, which is zero point five zero millihenry.

Part b. The emf in the secondary is M times the rate of change of primary current. The current falls by five point zero amperes in zero point zero one zero seconds, so the rate is five hundred amperes per second. Multiply by M and you get zero point two five volts.

<whisper> Part c is where the marks hide, because the shortcut is not obvious unless you spotted the connection. You could compute the current and multiply by time, and that would work here because the rate is uniform. But there is a cleaner route.

Recall from subtopic one that charge equals the change in flux linkage divided by R, with no dependence on time. Here the flux linkage is M times I, so the change in linkage is M times the change in current. So q equals M delta I over R, which is five point zero times ten to the minus four, times five point zero, over ten. That gives two point five times ten to the minus four coulomb, or zero point two five millicoulomb. Notice the zero point zero one zero seconds never entered part c at all.
ये problem mutual-inductance की derivation को Faraday's law से और subtopic एक वाले induced-charge result से जोड़ती है। एक question में तीन subtopics, और ठीक इसीलिए J E E Main को ये पसंद है।

दो coaxial solenoids, बराबर length zero point five zero metres और बराबर cross-sectional area four point zero square centimetres. भीतरी में two thousand turns per metre, बाहरी में one thousand turns per metre. बाहरी वाला primary है, और उसका current switch off किया जाता है, five point zero amperes से गिरकर zero, zero point zero one zero seconds में। Secondary circuit की कुल resistance ten ohms है।
Geometry बिलकुल वही जोड़ी है जो हमने derive की थी। Figure देखिए और ध्यान रखिए कि formula में area A भीतरी solenoid का है, वही जिसके turns link हो रहे हैं।
तीन parts: mutual inductance, secondary में induce हुई emf, और secondary से बहने वाला कुल charge.

Part a हमारे derived formula में सीधा substitution है। M equals mu nought n one n two A l. यानी four pi times ten to the minus seven, into two thousand, into one thousand, into four point zero times ten to the minus four, into zero point five zero. गुणा करने पर मिलता है five point zero times ten to the minus four henry, यानी zero point five zero millihenry.

Part b. Secondary की emf है M times primary current के बदलने की दर। Current zero point zero one zero seconds में five point zero amperes गिरता है, तो दर है five hundred amperes per second. M से multiply कीजिए और मिलता है zero point two five volts.

<whisper> Part c में ही असली marks छिपे हैं, क्योंकि shortcut तब तक नहीं दिखता जब तक connection न पकड़ें। आप current निकालकर time से multiply कर सकते हैं, और यहाँ चल भी जाएगा क्योंकि दर uniform है। लेकिन एक साफ़ रास्ता है।

Subtopic एक याद कीजिए: charge equals flux linkage का बदलाव बटा R, time पर कोई निर्भरता नहीं। यहाँ flux linkage है M into I, तो linkage का बदलाव है M into current का बदलाव। तो q equals M delta I बटा R, यानी five point zero times ten to the minus four, into five point zero, बटा ten. मिलता है two point five times ten to the minus four coulomb, या zero point two five millicoulomb. ग़ौर कीजिए zero point zero one zero seconds part c में कहीं घुसा ही नहीं।

board_events.text: A small coil of 50 turns and radius 1.0 cm at the centre of a large coplanar coaxial coil

The large coil has 200 turns and radius 0.20 m, with R much greater than r. Find the mutual inductance, and the emf induced in the small coil when the current in the large coil changes at 100 A per second.

board_events.caption: Driving the large coil is easy; driving the small coil is horrid. Reciprocity lets you choose.

board_events.text: The clever step: choose WHICH coil carries the current. Reciprocity guarantees the same M either way, so pick the easy direction.

Drive current through the LARGE coil. Its field at the centre is the simple, uniform result, and because R is much greater than r, that field is essentially constant over the entire tiny area of the small coil.

board_events.latex: B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 N_1 I_1}{2R} \;\Rightarrow\; N_2\Phi_2 = N_2 \frac{\mu_0 N_1 I_1}{2R}\pi r^2 \;\Rightarrow\; M = \frac{\mu_0 N_1 N_2 \pi r^2}{2R}

segments.text: This is where reciprocity stops being a pretty theorem and starts saving you ten minutes. J E E Advanced sets this problem precisely to see whether you spotted the trick.

A small circular coil of fifty turns and radius one point zero centimetres is placed at the centre of a large coplanar, coaxial coil of two hundred turns and radius zero point two zero metres, with R much greater than r. Find the mutual inductance, and the emf induced in the small coil when the current in the large coil changes at one hundred amperes per second.
Look at the two boxes on the right of the figure, because they are the whole problem. One direction is easy. The other is horrid.

<excited> Here is the clever step. The definition of M requires you to put current in one coil and compute the flux linkage in the other. But which coil you drive is your choice, and reciprocity guarantees the same M either way. So choose the easy direction.

Drive the current through the large coil. Its field at the centre is the simple, standard result you already know, mu nought N one I one over two R. And crucially, because R is much larger than r, that field is essentially uniform across the entire tiny area of the small coil sitting at the centre. Uniform field over a small flat area is exactly the case where B A applies with no integration at all.

So the flux linkage with the small coil is N two, times that field, times the small area pi r squared. Divide by I one and the current cancels, leaving M equals mu nought N one N two pi r squared, all over two R.

Substituting: four pi times ten to the minus seven, times two hundred, times fifty, times pi times zero point zero one zero squared, divided by two times zero point two zero. That works out to nine point nine times ten to the minus six henry, about nine point nine microhenry.

<whisper> The emf is then just M times the rate of change, nine point nine times ten to the minus six times one hundred, giving nine point nine times ten to the minus four volts, roughly zero point nine nine millivolts. And now see what you avoided. Had you instead put the current in the small coil, you would have had to integrate its messy dipole field over the entire area of the large coil, which is a genuinely unpleasant calculation. Reciprocity let you walk around it.
यहीं reciprocity एक प्यारा theorem होना बंद करके आपके दस मिनट बचाना शुरू करता है। J E E Advanced ये problem ठीक ये देखने के लिए देता है कि आपने चाल पकड़ी या नहीं।

Fifty turns और one point zero centimetres radius वाली एक छोटी circular coil, two hundred turns और zero point two zero metres radius वाली बड़ी coplanar, coaxial coil के केंद्र में रखी है, जहाँ R, r से बहुत बड़ा है। Mutual inductance निकालिए, और छोटी coil में induce होने वाली emf जब बड़ी coil का current one hundred amperes per second की दर से बदल रहा हो।
Figure के दाईं तरफ़ के दोनों boxes देखिए, क्योंकि वही पूरी problem हैं। एक दिशा आसान है। दूसरी भयानक।

<excited> अब वो चालाक क़दम। M की definition कहती है कि एक coil में current डालो और दूसरी की flux linkage निकालो। लेकिन कौन सी coil चलानी है, ये आपकी मर्ज़ी है, और reciprocity गारंटी देता है कि M दोनों तरह से वही आएगा। तो आसान दिशा चुनिए।

Current बड़ी coil में भेजिए। उसके केंद्र की field वही simple, standard result है जो आपको पहले से आता है, mu nought N one I one बटा two R. और अहम बात, चूँकि R, r से बहुत बड़ा है, वो field केंद्र में बैठी छोटी coil के पूरे नन्हे area पर practically uniform है। छोटे flat area पर uniform field, यही तो वो case है जहाँ B A बिना किसी integration के लग जाता है।
तो छोटी coil की flux linkage है N two, into वो field, into छोटा area pi r squared. I one से भाग दीजिए और current cancel हो जाता है, बचता है M equals mu nought N one N two pi r squared, बटा two R.

Substitute कीजिए: four pi times ten to the minus seven, into two hundred, into fifty, into pi into zero point zero one zero squared, बटा two into zero point two zero. निकलता है nine point nine times ten to the minus six henry, लगभग nine point nine microhenry.

<whisper> Emf फिर बस M into बदलने की दर है, nine point nine times ten to the minus six into one hundred, यानी nine point nine times ten to the minus four volts, लगभग zero point nine nine millivolts. और अब देखिए आपने किस चीज़ से बचाव किया। अगर आपने current छोटी coil में डाला होता, तो उसकी उलझी हुई dipole field को बड़ी coil के पूरे area पर integrate करना पड़ता, जो सचमुच एक तकलीफ़देह calculation है। Reciprocity ने आपको उसके बग़ल से निकाल दिया।

sections.title: The four pitfalls of inductance, and the parallel worth memorising

board_events.text: Pitfall 1: believing L or M depends on current or emf
They depend only on geometry and the medium, exactly like capacitance. A larger current gives more energy and a larger emf, but L itself is unchanged.
Pitfall 2: the linear-in-N error
L is proportional to N SQUARED, not N. Doubling the turns quadruples the inductance. Likewise stored energy goes as I squared.
Pitfall 3: mixing n and N in the solenoid formula
$L = \mu_0 n^2 A l$ uses turns per unit length. $L = \mu_0 N^2 A/l$ uses total turns. They are the same formula since n = N/l, but never plug a total-turns number into the n-squared version.
Pitfall 4: forgetting the changing-current requirement
No emf, self or mutual, arises from a steady current, however large. Only a non-zero rate of change of current matters.

Pro-tip: when self-inductances are known and you need the mutual, skip the geometry entirely and use M = k root L1 L2, taking k = 1 for tightly wound coils. And for inductor energy, lean on the capacitor parallel: half L I squared mirrors half C V squared, with the energy living in the magnetic field.

segments.text: Four pitfalls for this subtopic, and then a parallel that will let you reconstruct half of it from memory of a different chapter.

Pitfall one, and it is the conceptual heart of the subtopic. Believing that L or M depends on the current or the emf. They do not. They depend only on geometry and the surrounding medium, exactly like capacitance depends only on plate geometry and dielectric. Push a larger current and you get more stored energy and a larger emf, but L itself has not budged.
Pitfall two, the linear-in-N error, and this is the single most common inductance mistake in any exam.

<whisper> L is proportional to N squared, not to N. Doubling the number of turns quadruples the inductance. And while we are on squares, the stored energy goes as I squared as well. Whenever a question doubles something, stop and check whether that variable is squared in the formula before you answer.
Pitfall three is a careless one rather than a conceptual one, but it costs full marks on a numerical.

The formula with mu nought n squared A l uses little n, turns per unit length. The formula with mu nought N squared A over l uses capital N, total turns. They are the same formula, since n equals N over l. But if you plug a total-turns number into the n squared version, your answer is wrong by a factor of l squared. Read which one the question gives you before you write anything.
Pitfall four is the theme running through this whole chapter, appearing here in its inductance clothing.
No emf, self or mutual, arises from a steady current, however large that current is. Only a non-zero rate of change of current does anything at all.

Now the pro-tip, in two halves. First: when the self-inductances are known and you are asked for the mutual, do not go anywhere near the geometry. Use M equals k root L one L two, taking k as one for tightly wound coils. Second, and more valuable: lean on the capacitor parallel throughout. Half L I squared mirrors half C V squared. L behaves like C, current behaves like voltage, and the energy lives in the magnetic field with density B squared over two mu nought instead of in the electric field. If you know capacitors well, you already half know this subtopic.
इस subtopic के चार pitfalls, और फिर एक समानांतर रिश्ता जो आपको इसका आधा हिस्सा किसी दूसरे chapter की याद से दोबारा बनाने देगा।

Pitfall एक, और यही इस subtopic का conceptual दिल है। ये मान लेना कि L या M, current या emf पर depend करते हैं। नहीं करते। वो सिर्फ़ geometry और आसपास के medium पर depend करते हैं, ठीक वैसे जैसे capacitance सिर्फ़ plate geometry और dielectric पर। बड़ा current भेजिए तो ज़्यादा stored energy और बड़ी emf मिलेगी, लेकिन L ज़रा भी नहीं हिला।
Pitfall दो, N में linear मान लेने की ग़लती, और किसी भी exam में inductance की सबसे common ग़लती यही है।

<whisper> L, N squared के proportional है, N के नहीं। Turns दोगुने करने से inductance चार गुनी हो जाती है। और जब squares की बात चल ही रही है, stored energy भी I squared के साथ जाती है। जब भी कोई question किसी चीज़ को दोगुना करे, रुककर देखिए कि वो variable formula में squared तो नहीं है, फिर जवाब दीजिए।
Pitfall तीन conceptual नहीं, लापरवाही वाली है, लेकिन numerical में पूरे marks ले जाती है।

Mu nought n squared A l वाला formula छोटे n यानी प्रति unit length turns इस्तेमाल करता है। Mu nought N squared A बटा l वाला formula बड़े N यानी कुल turns इस्तेमाल करता है। ये एक ही formula हैं, क्योंकि n equals N बटा l. लेकिन अगर आपने कुल turns का number n squared वाले रूप में डाल दिया, तो answer l squared के factor से ग़लत है। कुछ भी लिखने से पहले पढ़िए कि question कौन सा दे रहा है।
Pitfall चार वही theme है जो पूरे chapter में दौड़ रही है, यहाँ inductance के कपड़ों में।
Steady current से न self emf आती है न mutual, चाहे वो current कितना भी बड़ा हो। सिर्फ़ current के बदलने की non-zero दर ही कुछ करती है।

अब pro-tip, दो हिस्सों में। पहला: जब self-inductances पता हों और mutual पूछी जाए, तो geometry के पास मत जाइए। M equals k root L one L two इस्तेमाल कीजिए, कसकर लिपटी coils के लिए k को one लेकर। दूसरा, और ज़्यादा क़ीमती: पूरे subtopic में capacitor वाले समानांतर रिश्ते का सहारा लीजिए। Half L I squared, half C V squared की नक़ल है। L, C की तरह बर्ताव करता है, current, voltage की तरह, और energy electric field की जगह magnetic field में रहती है जिसका density है B squared बटा two mu nought. अगर capacitors अच्छे से आते हैं, तो ये subtopic आपको आधा पहले से आता है।

sections.title: From detecting induction to harnessing it

board_events.text: Everything so far has been about DETECTING induced emf
The AC generator is where we HARNESS it. It is the machine that lights your home.
It is nothing more than Faraday's law put to work on an industrial scale.
An AC generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. It is, in effect, an electric motor run in reverse.
The most relatable version: the old bicycle dynamo
As you pedal, a small coil spins inside a magnet. The faster you pedal, the brighter the lamp glows.
That is the entire principle: spin a coil in a magnetic field and an emf appears across its ends.
Scale that up, replace your legs with water in a hydro dam or steam in a thermal plant, and you have a power station.

segments.text: Step back for a moment and notice what we have been doing for three subtopics. Galvanometers twitching, needles deflecting, tiny emfs appearing in rods and coils. All of it has been about detecting induction.

The A C generator is where we stop detecting and start harnessing. This is the machine that lights your home, runs your fan, and charges your phone. Every unit of electricity you have ever used came out of one of these.

<excited> And here is the thing worth appreciating. It is nothing more than Faraday's law put to work on an industrial scale. There is no new physics coming in this subtopic. It is the same law you already know, arranged into a machine.

Formally, an A C generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. Something must turn the shaft, and the electricity comes out. It is, in effect, an electric motor run in reverse: a motor takes current and gives you rotation, a generator takes rotation and gives you current.
The most relatable version of this machine is the old bicycle dynamo, the little device you press against the tyre to power the cycle lamp.

As you pedal, a small coil spins inside a magnet. And you will remember the behaviour if you have ever used one: pedal slowly and the lamp is dim, pedal hard and it glows bright. Stop, and it goes out entirely.

That is the entire principle, and you can state it in one line. Spin a coil in a magnetic field, and an emf appears across its ends. Everything else in this subtopic is the mathematics of that sentence and the engineering around it.

And the scaling is remarkable. Keep the physics identical, replace your legs with falling water in a hydroelectric dam, or steam in a thermal plant, or wind in a turbine, and you have a power station. Same coil, same magnet, same law.
एक पल रुककर देखिए कि हम तीन subtopics से क्या कर रहे थे। Galvanometers का काँपना, needles का घूमना, rods और coils में नन्हीं emfs का आना। ये सब induction को detect करने के बारे में था।

A C generator वो जगह है जहाँ हम detect करना छोड़कर उसे harness करना शुरू करते हैं। यही वो machine है जो आपका घर रोशन करती है, पंखा चलाती है, phone charge करती है। आपने ज़िंदगी में जितनी बिजली इस्तेमाल की, वो सब इन्हीं में से किसी एक से निकली।

<excited> और अब सराहने लायक़ बात। ये Faraday's law को औद्योगिक पैमाने पर काम पर लगाने से ज़्यादा कुछ नहीं है। इस subtopic में कोई नई physics नहीं आ रही। वही law है जो आपको पहले से आता है, बस एक machine की शक्ल में सजा हुआ।

औपचारिक रूप से, A C generator mechanical energy को electrical energy में बदलता है। कुछ न कुछ shaft घुमाना ही पड़ेगा, तभी बिजली निकलेगी। ये असल में उल्टा चलता हुआ electric motor है: motor current लेकर घुमाव देता है, generator घुमाव लेकर current देता है।
इस machine का सबसे जाना-पहचाना रूप है पुराना bicycle dynamo, वो छोटी सी चीज़ जिसे टायर से सटाकर cycle की lamp जलाई जाती थी।

जैसे-जैसे आप pedal मारते हैं, एक छोटी coil magnet के अंदर घूमती है। और अगर आपने कभी इस्तेमाल किया हो तो बर्ताव याद होगा: धीरे pedal मारिए तो lamp मद्धम, ज़ोर से मारिए तो तेज़ चमकती है। रुक जाइए, तो बुझ जाती है।

यही पूरा सिद्धांत है, और इसे एक line में कहा जा सकता है। Magnetic field में coil घुमाइए, और उसके सिरों पर emf आ जाती है। इस subtopic में बाक़ी सब उसी वाक्य का गणित है और उसके इर्द-गिर्द की engineering.

और इसका scaling क़माल का है। Physics बिलकुल वही रखिए, अपनी टाँगों की जगह hydroelectric dam का गिरता पानी रख दीजिए, या thermal plant की भाप, या turbine की हवा, और आपके पास power station है। वही coil, वही magnet, वही law.

board_events.text: As the coil rotates, theta equals omega t sweeps continuously. So cos omega t oscillates, the flux oscillates, and Faraday's law delivers a continuously varying emf.
Because the rotation is steady and the field uniform, the output is a clean sine wave. That is alternating current.
So the chapter is not four unrelated topics. It is one formula with three things you can vary, plus the bulk-conductor case of eddy currents.

segments.text: Before we build the machine, let me show you exactly where it sits in the logic of this chapter, because this is the moment the whole chapter clicks into place.
Recall the flux formula: phi equals B A cos theta. Now count your options. There are exactly three quantities in there that you could vary in order to change the flux, and therefore to induce an emf.

We have already used two of them. In subtopics one and three we changed B, the field itself, whether by moving a magnet or by changing a current through inductance. In subtopic two we changed A, the effective area, by sliding a conductor and sweeping out new area.
<excited> That leaves exactly one. The generator changes the third variable: the angle theta. And once you see it that way, you realise the generator was inevitable. It was the one option left.

Look at the diagram. One central idea, changing magnetic flux, and three arrows branching out to the three ways of changing it. Change B goes to induction. Change A goes to motional emf. Change theta goes to the A C generator.

So here is the mechanism. As the coil rotates steadily, theta equals omega t, and that angle sweeps continuously through all values. So cos omega t oscillates smoothly between plus one and minus one, the flux oscillates with it, and Faraday's law delivers a continuously varying emf.

And now notice why the output has the shape it does. Because the rotation is steady and the field is uniform, the flux is a clean cosine, so its rate of change is a clean sine. The output is a smooth sine wave, and that is precisely what we call alternating current.

So step back and see what has happened to this chapter. It is not four unrelated topics that you have to memorise separately. It is one formula with three things you can vary, plus one bonus case, eddy currents, for when the conductor is a solid block instead of a wire. That is the entire syllabus on one line.
Machine बनाने से पहले, मैं दिखाती हूँ कि ये इस chapter के तर्क में ठीक कहाँ बैठता है, क्योंकि यही वो पल है जब पूरा chapter अपनी जगह पर आकर बैठ जाता है।
Flux formula याद कीजिए: phi equals B A cos theta. अब अपने विकल्प गिनिए। इसमें ठीक तीन quantities हैं जिन्हें आप बदलकर flux बदल सकते हैं, और इस तरह emf induce कर सकते हैं।

दो का इस्तेमाल हम कर चुके हैं। Subtopic एक और तीन में हमने B यानी field ख़ुद बदली, चाहे magnet हिलाकर या inductance के ज़रिए current बदलकर। Subtopic दो में हमने A यानी असरदार area बदला, conductor सरकाकर नया area बुहारते हुए।
<excited> तो ठीक एक बचता है। Generator तीसरा variable बदलता है: angle theta. और एक बार ऐसे देख लीजिए तो समझ आता है कि generator अनिवार्य था। यही एक विकल्प बचा हुआ था।

Diagram देखिए। बीच में एक idea, बदलती हुई magnetic flux, और तीन तीर निकलकर उसे बदलने के तीन तरीक़ों तक जाते हुए। Change B जाता है induction तक। Change A जाता है motional emf तक। Change theta जाता है A C generator तक।

तो mechanism ये है। जैसे-जैसे coil एक समान गति से घूमती है, theta equals omega t, और वो angle लगातार हर value से गुज़रता जाता है। तो cos omega t plus one और minus one के बीच smoothly झूलता है, flux उसके साथ झूलती है, और Faraday's law एक लगातार बदलती emf दे देता है।

और अब ग़ौर कीजिए कि output की शक्ल ऐसी क्यों है। चूँकि घुमाव एक समान है और field uniform, इसलिए flux एक साफ़ cosine है, तो उसके बदलने की दर एक साफ़ sine है। Output एक चिकनी sine wave है, और इसी को हम alternating current कहते हैं।

तो थोड़ा पीछे हटकर देखिए कि इस chapter का क्या हुआ। ये चार अलग-अलग topics नहीं हैं जिन्हें अलग-अलग रटना पड़े। ये एक formula है जिसमें तीन चीज़ें बदली जा सकती हैं, और एक bonus case, eddy currents, उस हालत के लिए जब conductor तार की जगह ठोस block हो। पूरा syllabus एक line में।

sections.title: The swinging gate: why emf peaks exactly where flux vanishes

board_events.text: Picture the coil as a swinging gate in a stream of field lines
When the coil's plane is PARALLEL to the field, its sides are slicing straight across the field lines.

board_events.caption: Edge-on the coil cuts lines fastest; face-on the lines glide along it

board_events.text: It is cutting lines as fast as possible. The flux is momentarily ZERO but changing FASTEST, so the emf is at its PEAK.
A quarter-turn later, when the plane is PERPENDICULAR to the field, the flux is maximum but momentarily not changing. The sides are gliding along the lines, not cutting them. So the emf is ZERO.

board_events.caption: Flux as a cosine, emf as a sine, a quarter cycle out of step

board_events.text: This is the single most important and most counter-intuitive fact of the topic: emf is maximum exactly when flux is zero, and zero exactly when flux is maximum.
If it feels wrong, remember what Faraday's law actually takes: the SLOPE of the flux curve. And a curve at its peak has zero slope.

segments.text: <curious> Now the idea that trips up more students in this subtopic than everything else combined. And the picture that fixes it is a gate swinging in a stream.
Picture the coil as a swinging gate standing in a stream of field lines flowing past. As the gate turns, sometimes it slices across the flow, and sometimes it lies along it.
Look at the left panel. When the coil's plane is parallel to the field, the coil is edge-on, and its sides are slicing straight across the field lines.

So at that instant it is cutting lines as fast as it possibly can. Now here is the subtlety. Because it is edge-on, essentially no lines are threading through it, so the flux is momentarily zero. But it is changing at its fastest possible rate. And Faraday cares about the rate. So the emf is at its peak.

A quarter-turn later, look at the right panel. Now the plane is perpendicular to the field, face-on, and the maximum number of lines are threading through it. The flux is at its maximum. But the sides are now gliding along the lines rather than cutting them, so the flux is momentarily not changing at all. And so the emf is exactly zero.

The graphs make this precise. Flux is a cosine, emf is a sine, and they are a quarter cycle, ninety degrees, out of step. Trace down the dashed lines and check it at each one: flux maximum sits directly above emf zero, and flux zero sits directly above emf maximum.

This is the single most important and most counter-intuitive fact of this topic, so let me state it flatly. The emf is maximum exactly when the flux is zero, and the emf is zero exactly when the flux is maximum.

<whisper> And if it still feels wrong, hold onto this one reminder, because it dissolves the confusion permanently. Faraday's law does not take the flux. It takes the slope of the flux curve. And a curve sitting at its peak has zero slope. That is all this is.
<curious> अब वो idea जो इस subtopic में बाक़ी सब मिलाकर से भी ज़्यादा students को गिराता है। और जो तस्वीर इसे ठीक कर देती है वो है बहती धारा में झूलता हुआ फाटक।
Coil को एक झूलता हुआ फाटक सोचिए जो field lines की बहती धारा में खड़ा है। जैसे-जैसे फाटक घूमता है, कभी वो धारा को काटता है, कभी उसके साथ-साथ लेट जाता है।
बायाँ panel देखिए। जब coil का plane field के parallel होता है, तो coil edge-on है, और उसकी sides सीधे field lines को काटती हुई गुज़र रही हैं।

तो उस पल वो lines को उतनी तेज़ी से काट रहा है जितनी तेज़ी से काट सकता है। अब यहाँ subtlety देखिए। Edge-on होने की वजह से practically कोई line उससे होकर नहीं गुज़र रही, तो flux उस पल zero है। लेकिन वो अपनी सबसे तेज़ संभव दर से बदल रही है। और Faraday को दर से मतलब है। तो emf अपने peak पर है।

एक चौथाई चक्कर बाद, दायाँ panel देखिए। अब plane field के perpendicular है, face-on, और सबसे ज़्यादा lines उससे होकर गुज़र रही हैं। Flux अपने maximum पर है। लेकिन अब sides lines को काटने की जगह उनके साथ-साथ सरक रही हैं, तो flux उस पल बिलकुल नहीं बदल रही। और इसलिए emf ठीक zero है।

Graphs इसे सटीक बना देते हैं। Flux एक cosine है, emf एक sine, और दोनों एक चौथाई चक्र यानी ninety degrees अलग हैं। Dashed lines के साथ नीचे तक देखिए और हर एक पर जाँचिए: flux maximum ठीक emf zero के ऊपर बैठा है, और flux zero ठीक emf maximum के ऊपर।
ये इस topic की सबसे अहम और सबसे उल्टी लगने वाली बात है, तो मैं इसे सीधे-सीधे कह देती हूँ। Emf तब maximum होती है जब flux ठीक zero हो, और emf तब zero होती है जब flux ठीक maximum हो।

<whisper> और अगर अब भी ग़लत लगे, तो ये एक याददिहानी पकड़े रखिए, क्योंकि ये उलझन को हमेशा के लिए घोल देती है। Faraday's law flux नहीं लेता। वो flux curve की ढलान लेता है। और अपने शिखर पर बैठे curve की ढलान zero होती है। बस इतनी ही बात है।
