board_events.text: ARMATURE: a rectangular coil of many turns wound on a soft-iron core. It is the rotating part. The core concentrates the flux and raises the peak emf.
FIELD MAGNET: supplies the uniform field B. A permanent magnet in small units, an electromagnet in power-station alternators.
The axle is turned by a prime mover: water in a hydro dam, steam in a thermal plant, wind in a turbine.
SLIP RINGS: two conducting rings that rotate with the coil. BRUSHES: fixed carbon contacts pressing on the rings to tap the output.
The slip rings are what keep the output ALTERNATING. Each coil end stays connected to the same external terminal, so as the coil emf reverses every half-turn, the output reverses too.
Replace the two slip rings with a single SPLIT ring, a commutator, and you get pulsating DC instead. That is the ONLY construction difference between an AC and a DC generator.

segments.text: Now let us build the machine, and you will find the construction follows directly from the principle rather than being a list to memorise.
Look at the full diagram. Coil between the poles on the left, rings and brushes below it, and the sine wave output on the right. Four named parts, and C B S E awards descriptive marks for each.

First, the armature. This is a coil of many turns wound on a soft-iron core, and it is the rotating part. Two details earn marks here: many turns, because the emf is proportional to N, and the soft-iron core, because it concentrates the flux through the coil and so raises the peak emf.

Second, the field magnet. Its job is simply to supply the uniform field B in which the coil turns. In small units, like your bicycle dynamo, it is a permanent magnet. In power-station alternators it is an electromagnet, because you need a far stronger and controllable field.

The axle itself is turned by what engineers call a prime mover. In a hydroelectric dam that is falling water. In a thermal plant it is steam driving a turbine. In a wind farm it is the wind. The generator does not care which, it only needs the shaft to turn.

Third and fourth, the pair that gets the electricity out. The slip rings are two conducting rings mounted on the axle, rotating with the coil. The brushes are fixed carbon contacts that press against those rings and tap the output into the external circuit.

<excited> Now, why rings at all? Because the coil is spinning, and if you simply wired it to the outside, the leads would twist up and snap within a second. The rings let a rotating coil stay connected to a stationary circuit. And crucially, each end of the coil stays connected to the same external terminal throughout. So as the emf in the coil reverses every half-turn, the output reverses too. The slip rings are what keep the output alternating.

<whisper> Which brings us to the single most-asked structural question in this subtopic. Replace the two slip rings with one split ring, called a commutator, and the connections swap over every half-turn, so the output no longer reverses. You get pulsating D C instead. That ring is the only construction difference between an A C and a D C generator. Everything else is identical.
अब machine बनाते हैं, और आप पाएँगे कि construction सीधे सिद्धांत से निकलता है, ये कोई रटने वाली list नहीं है।
पूरा diagram देखिए। बाईं तरफ़ poles के बीच coil, उसके नीचे rings और brushes, और दाईं तरफ़ sine wave output. चार नामज़द parts, और C B S E हर एक के descriptive marks देता है।

पहला, armature. ये कई turns वाली coil है जो soft-iron core पर लिपटी है, और यही घूमने वाला हिस्सा है। यहाँ दो details marks दिलाती हैं: कई turns, क्योंकि emf, N के proportional है, और soft-iron core, क्योंकि वो coil से गुज़रती flux को केंद्रित करता है और इस तरह peak emf बढ़ाता है।

दूसरा, field magnet. इसका काम बस इतना है कि वो uniform field B दे जिसमें coil घूमे। छोटी units में, जैसे आपका bicycle dynamo, ये permanent magnet होता है। Power station के alternators में ये electromagnet होता है, क्योंकि वहाँ कहीं ज़्यादा strong और नियंत्रित field चाहिए।

Axle को ख़ुद वो चीज़ घुमाती है जिसे engineers prime mover कहते हैं। Hydroelectric dam में वो गिरता हुआ पानी है। Thermal plant में turbine चलाती भाप। Wind farm में हवा। Generator को इससे मतलब नहीं कि कौन, उसे बस shaft का घूमना चाहिए।

तीसरा और चौथा, वो जोड़ी जो बिजली बाहर निकालती है। Slip rings दो conducting rings हैं जो axle पर लगी हैं और coil के साथ घूमती हैं। Brushes स्थिर carbon contacts हैं जो उन rings से दबकर टिके रहते हैं और output को बाहरी circuit तक पहुँचाते हैं।

<excited> अब, rings की ज़रूरत ही क्यों? क्योंकि coil घूम रही है, और अगर आप उसे सीधे बाहर तार से जोड़ दें तो तार एक second में ऐंठकर टूट जाएँगे। Rings एक घूमती हुई coil को स्थिर circuit से जुड़े रहने देती हैं। और अहम बात, coil का हर सिरा पूरे वक़्त उसी बाहरी terminal से जुड़ा रहता है। तो हर आधे चक्कर पर जब coil की emf पलटती है, output भी पलट जाता है। Slip rings ही output को alternating रखती हैं।

<whisper> और यहीं से आता है इस subtopic का सबसे ज़्यादा पूछा जाने वाला structural सवाल। दो slip rings की जगह एक split ring लगा दीजिए, जिसे commutator कहते हैं, तो हर आधे चक्कर पर connections आपस में बदल जाते हैं, और output पलटना बंद कर देता है। तब आपको pulsating D C मिलता है। वही एक ring, A C और D C generator के बीच का इकलौता construction का फ़र्क़ है। बाक़ी सब कुछ बिलकुल एक जैसा है।

sections.title: Three conditions on the clean sinusoidal output

board_events.text: Condition 1: what makes the output a clean sine
The result $\varepsilon = \varepsilon_0\sin\omega t$ assumes a UNIFORM field and a UNIFORM angular velocity omega.
Non-uniform rotation, or a non-uniform field, distorts the waveform. Real alternators work hard to keep both uniform.
Condition 2: amplitude and frequency are locked together
Peak emf $\varepsilon_0 = NBA\omega$ depends on omega. So the output AMPLITUDE and the output FREQUENCY rise together with rotation speed. You cannot raise one without the other.
This is why mains frequency is regulated so tightly. You cannot simply spin faster to get more voltage without also changing the frequency the whole grid runs on.
Condition 3: what maximum emf means
Maximum emf always refers to the AMPLITUDE, the peak value, reached when the coil plane is parallel to the field.
It does not mean the largest emf that this generator could ever produce with a different design. Read the word maximum as amplitude every time.

segments.text: Three conditions before the formulas, and the second one has a genuinely interesting engineering consequence.
Condition one. The clean result, emf equals epsilon nought sine omega t, assumes two things are uniform: the magnetic field, and the angular velocity of the rotation.

If the rotation is jerky, or the field varies from place to place, the output is still alternating but it is no longer a clean sine. It becomes a distorted waveform. Real alternators go to considerable trouble to keep both uniform, precisely because the grid needs a clean sine.
Condition two is worth thinking about rather than just noting.

<curious> The peak emf is N B A omega, so it depends on omega. But the frequency of the output is also set by omega, since the coil produces one full cycle per rotation. So the amplitude and the frequency are locked together. You cannot raise one without raising the other.

And that has a real consequence you can see in the world. It is why mains frequency is regulated so tightly, at fifty hertz here in India. A power station cannot simply spin its alternator faster to push out more voltage, because that would also change the frequency that the entire grid, and every clock and motor on it, depends on. Voltage is raised with transformers instead, which is the next chapter.
Condition three is about reading exam language correctly, which sounds trivial until it costs you a mark.
Maximum emf always refers to the amplitude, epsilon nought, the peak of the sine wave, which is reached when the coil plane is parallel to the field.
It does not mean the largest emf that this generator could ever produce with a different design or a different speed. So whenever a question says maximum emf, read it as amplitude, every single time.
Formulas से पहले तीन conditions, और दूसरी वाली का एक सचमुच दिलचस्प engineering नतीजा है।
Condition एक। साफ़ result, emf equals epsilon nought sine omega t, ये मानकर चलता है कि दो चीज़ें uniform हैं: magnetic field, और घुमाव की angular velocity.

अगर घुमाव झटकेदार हो, या field जगह-जगह बदलती हो, तो output alternating तो रहेगा लेकिन साफ़ sine नहीं रहेगा। वो बिगड़ी हुई waveform बन जाता है। असली alternators दोनों को uniform रखने में काफ़ी मेहनत करते हैं, ठीक इसीलिए कि grid को साफ़ sine चाहिए।
Condition दो सिर्फ़ नोट करने की नहीं, सोचने की चीज़ है।

<curious> Peak emf है N B A omega, तो वो omega पर depend करती है। लेकिन output की frequency भी omega से ही तय होती है, क्योंकि coil हर चक्कर में एक पूरा cycle बनाती है। तो amplitude और frequency आपस में बँधे हुए हैं। एक को बढ़ाए बिना दूसरा नहीं बढ़ता।

और इसका एक असली नतीजा है जो आपको दुनिया में दिखता है। इसीलिए mains frequency इतनी कसकर नियंत्रित की जाती है, भारत में fifty hertz पर। कोई power station ज़्यादा voltage के लिए अपना alternator तेज़ नहीं घुमा सकता, क्योंकि उससे वो frequency भी बदल जाएगी जिस पर पूरा grid, और उस पर लगी हर घड़ी और हर motor टिकी है। Voltage इसकी जगह transformers से बढ़ाया जाता है, जो अगला chapter है।
Condition तीन exam की भाषा सही पढ़ने के बारे में है, जो मामूली लगती है जब तक एक mark न ले जाए।
Maximum emf हमेशा amplitude की बात करती है, epsilon nought, sine wave का शिखर, जो तब आता है जब coil का plane field के parallel हो।
इसका मतलब ये नहीं कि किसी और design या किसी और speed पर ये generator सबसे बड़ी कितनी emf बना सकता है। तो जब भी question कहे maximum emf, उसे हर बार amplitude पढ़िए।

sections.title: The generator formula set, from flux to average power

board_events.text: Instantaneous flux linkage, coil at angle theta = omega t from the field
Instantaneous induced emf
Peak emf
Bridge to AC circuits: $\varepsilon_{rms} = \varepsilon_0/\sqrt{2}$ and $P_{avg} = \varepsilon_0^2/2R = \varepsilon_{rms}I_{rms}$.

Units: emf in volt, omega in radians per second, f in hertz. In India the mains frequency is 50 Hz, so omega is 100 pi, about 314 radians per second. Peak emf carries the usual emf dimension $[ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}]$.

segments.text: Here is the complete formula set for the generator. Six lines, and every one of them descends from the first.

Start with the flux linkage. The coil has N turns of area A in a field B, and its area vector makes an angle theta with the field. With steady rotation theta equals omega t. So the flux linkage is N B A cos omega t. That is just the flux formula with the angle written as a function of time.
Now apply Faraday's law and differentiate that linkage.

You get the instantaneous emf: N B A omega sine omega t. The cosine differentiates to minus sine, the minus signs cancel, and an omega drops out of the chain rule. That omega is important, so notice where it came from.
The amplitude of that sine is what we call the peak emf.

It is epsilon nought equals N B A omega. And since omega equals two pi f, you can also write it as N B A times two pi f, which is the form you need whenever a question gives frequency in hertz rather than angular velocity.

Then the routine relations. Omega equals two pi f. And the current into a load resistance R is just the emf over R at every instant, so it is also a sine wave, with peak current I nought equals epsilon nought over R.

<whisper> Now the bridge to A C circuits, which is where the next chapter picks up and where J E E Main likes to fuse questions. The root mean square emf is the peak divided by root two. And the average power delivered is epsilon nought squared over two R, which also equals epsilon r m s times I r m s. That factor of two in the denominator is the whole content of r m s, and forgetting it halves or doubles your answer.

On units: emf in volts, omega in radians per second, frequency f in hertz, and peak emf carries the usual emf dimension, M L squared T to the minus three A to the minus one. And one number is worth committing to memory because it appears constantly: in India the mains frequency is fifty hertz, so omega is one hundred pi, about three hundred and fourteen radians per second. If you see three hundred and fourteen in a generator problem, that is where it came from.
ये रहा generator का पूरा formula set. छह lines, और हर एक पहली से ही निकली है।

शुरुआत flux linkage से। Coil में N turns हैं, हर एक का area A, field B में, और उसका area vector field के साथ theta angle बनाता है। एक समान घुमाव में theta equals omega t. तो flux linkage है N B A cos omega t. ये बस flux वाला formula है जिसमें angle को time के फलन के रूप में लिख दिया गया है।
अब Faraday's law लगाइए और उस linkage को differentiate कीजिए।

मिलती है instantaneous emf: N B A omega sine omega t. Cosine का differentiation minus sine देता है, minus signs cancel हो जाते हैं, और chain rule से एक omega बाहर गिरता है। वो omega अहम है, तो ध्यान रखिए वो आया कहाँ से।
उस sine का amplitude ही वो चीज़ है जिसे हम peak emf कहते हैं।

वो है epsilon nought equals N B A omega. और चूँकि omega equals two pi f, इसे N B A into two pi f भी लिख सकते हैं, और यही वो रूप है जो तब चाहिए जब question frequency hertz में दे, angular velocity में नहीं।
फिर बाक़ी सामान्य relations. Omega equals two pi f. और load resistance R में current हर पल बस emf बटा R है, तो वो भी sine wave है, जिसका peak current है I nought equals epsilon nought बटा R.

<whisper> अब A C circuits का पुल, जहाँ से अगला chapter शुरू होता है और जहाँ J E E Main questions मिलाना पसंद करता है। Root mean square emf है peak बटा root two. और delivered average power है epsilon nought squared बटा two R, जो epsilon r m s into I r m s के भी बराबर है। नीचे वाला two ही r m s की पूरी कहानी है, और उसे भूलने पर answer आधा या दोगुना हो जाता है।

Units की बात: emf volts में, omega radians per second में, frequency f hertz में, और peak emf वही सामान्य emf वाला dimension रखती है, M L squared T to the minus three A to the minus one. और एक number याद कर लेने लायक़ है क्योंकि वो लगातार आता है: भारत में mains frequency fifty hertz है, तो omega है one hundred pi, लगभग three hundred and fourteen radians per second. किसी generator problem में three hundred fourteen दिखे, तो वो यहीं से आया है।

sections.title: Board derivation: the sinusoidal emf, and reading the physics off it

board_events.text: Set up the rotation
A coil of N turns and area A rotates with constant angular velocity omega in a uniform field B, with the rotation axis perpendicular to B. The coil's area vector makes angle theta with B.
With uniform rotation, theta = omega t, taking the area vector along B at t = 0.
The flux through one turn is $\Phi_1 = BA\cos\omega t$, so the total flux linkage over N turns is:
By Faraday's law the induced emf is the negative rate of change of this linkage:

Reading the physics off the result: emf peaks when sine omega t equals 1, so at omega t = 90 degrees, when the coil plane is parallel to B. It is zero at omega t = 0 or 180 degrees, when the plane is perpendicular to B. And it reverses sign every half rotation, which is precisely why the output alternates.

segments.text: This is the guaranteed C B S E derivation of the subtopic. Three marks, almost every year, usually paired with construction. It is short, so do it cleanly.

Set up the rotation and state your assumptions explicitly, because that is where the first mark lives. A coil of N turns and area A rotates with constant angular velocity omega in a uniform magnetic field B, and the axis of rotation is perpendicular to the field.

Now define the angle. The coil's area vector makes an angle theta with the field. With uniform rotation that angle grows linearly, so theta equals omega t, and we take the area vector to be along the field at time zero. Stating that starting condition is worth writing down.

So the flux through one turn is B A cos omega t. Multiply by N turns and the total flux linkage is N B A cos omega t. Notice the flux is a cosine, starting at its maximum, exactly as our starting condition demands.
Now apply Faraday's law: the emf is the negative rate of change of that linkage.

Differentiate. The derivative of cos omega t is minus omega sine omega t. So we have minus N B A times minus omega sine omega t. The two minus signs cancel, and out comes N B A omega sine omega t. Writing the amplitude as epsilon nought equals N B A omega, that is the clean sinusoid epsilon nought sine omega t.

<excited> Now read the physics off the answer, because this is what separates a derivation that scores from one that just ends. The emf peaks when sine omega t equals one, which is at omega t equals ninety degrees. And at ninety degrees, the coil plane is parallel to the field, where the flux is zero and changing fastest. Exactly what the swinging-gate picture told us.

And the emf is zero when omega t is zero or one hundred and eighty degrees, where the plane is perpendicular to the field, flux maximum, momentarily constant. Finally, notice that the sine function reverses sign every half rotation. That is not a mathematical accident. That is precisely why the output of this machine is alternating.
ये इस subtopic की पक्की C B S E derivation है। तीन marks, लगभग हर साल, आम तौर पर construction के साथ जोड़कर। ये छोटी है, तो साफ़-सुथरी कीजिए।

घुमाव set कीजिए और अपनी assumptions साफ़ लिखिए, क्योंकि पहला mark वहीं है। N turns और area A वाली coil, uniform magnetic field B में constant angular velocity omega से घूम रही है, और घुमाव की axis field के perpendicular है।

अब angle define कीजिए। Coil का area vector field के साथ theta angle बनाता है। एक समान घुमाव में वो angle रैखिक रूप से बढ़ता है, तो theta equals omega t, और हम मानते हैं कि time zero पर area vector field के साथ है। वो शुरुआती condition लिखना अपने आप में क़ीमती है।

तो एक turn से गुज़रती flux है B A cos omega t. N turns से multiply कीजिए और कुल flux linkage है N B A cos omega t. ग़ौर कीजिए flux एक cosine है, अपने maximum से शुरू होती हुई, ठीक जैसा हमारी शुरुआती condition माँगती है।
अब Faraday's law लगाइए: emf उस linkage के बदलने की दर का ऋणात्मक है।

Differentiate कीजिए। Cos omega t का derivative है minus omega sine omega t. तो हमारे पास है minus N B A into minus omega sine omega t. दोनों minus signs cancel हो जाते हैं, और निकलता है N B A omega sine omega t. Amplitude को epsilon nought equals N B A omega लिखने पर, यही वो साफ़ sinusoid है, epsilon nought sine omega t.

<excited> अब answer से physics पढ़िए, क्योंकि यही उस derivation को जो marks दिलाती है उससे अलग करता है जो बस ख़त्म हो जाती है। Emf तब peak करती है जब sine omega t equals one, यानी omega t equals ninety degrees पर। और ninety degrees पर coil का plane field के parallel होता है, जहाँ flux zero है और सबसे तेज़ी से बदल रही है। बिलकुल वही जो झूलते फाटक वाली तस्वीर ने बताया था।

और emf तब zero है जब omega t हो zero या one hundred eighty degrees, जहाँ plane field के perpendicular है, flux maximum, और उस पल स्थिर। आख़िर में ग़ौर कीजिए कि sine function हर आधे चक्कर पर sign बदलता है। ये कोई गणितीय इत्तेफ़ाक़ नहीं है। ठीक इसीलिए इस machine का output alternating होता है।

board_events.text: The step students skip: the formula needs omega, and the question gives f. Convert FIRST.
The peak emf is about 314 V, which should look reassuringly familiar.
India's mains supply is about 220 V rms, and the peak of that is 220 times root 2, which is about 311 V. Our answer is essentially mains voltage.

segments.text: A clean C B S E numerical to lock in the generator formula, and the answer at the end has a satisfying twist.
A rectangular coil of one hundred turns and area zero point zero two zero square metres rotates at fifty hertz in a uniform magnetic field of zero point five zero tesla. Find the peak emf generated.
Look at the machine while you set up. We are computing the height of the peak on that sine wave on the right of the figure.

<whisper> Now here is the step students skip, and it is worth its own warning. The formula is epsilon nought equals N B A omega, and it needs omega, the angular velocity. But the question has given you f, the frequency in hertz. Those are different quantities. Convert first, before you touch anything else. Dropping the two pi is one of the most common errors in this entire subtopic.
So omega equals two pi f, which is two pi times fifty, equal to one hundred pi, which is three hundred fourteen point one six radians per second.

Now substitute everything into the peak emf formula. One hundred turns, times zero point five zero tesla, times zero point zero two zero square metres, times three hundred fourteen point one six. That gives three hundred and fourteen volts.
The peak emf is about three hundred and fourteen volts. And if that number looks familiar, it should.

<excited> India's mains supply is quoted as about two hundred and twenty volts, but that is the r m s value, not the peak. The peak of a two hundred and twenty volt r m s supply is two hundred and twenty times root two, which is about three hundred and eleven volts. So our textbook coil is producing essentially mains voltage. That is not a coincidence in the question design, and noticing it in your answer shows the examiner you understand what r m s actually means.
Generator formula को पक्का करने के लिए एक साफ़ C B S E numerical, और आख़िर में answer में एक मज़ेदार मोड़ है।
One hundred turns और zero point zero two zero square metres area वाली एक rectangular coil, zero point five zero tesla की uniform magnetic field में fifty hertz पर घूम रही है। Peak emf निकालिए।
Setup करते हुए machine देखिए। हम figure के दाईं तरफ़ की उस sine wave के शिखर की ऊँचाई निकाल रहे हैं।

<whisper> अब वो क़दम जो students छोड़ देते हैं, और वो अपनी अलग चेतावनी का हक़दार है। Formula है epsilon nought equals N B A omega, और उसे omega चाहिए, यानी angular velocity. लेकिन question ने आपको f दिया है, hertz में frequency. ये दो अलग quantities हैं। कुछ भी छूने से पहले convert कीजिए। दो pi छोड़ देना इस पूरे subtopic की सबसे common ग़लतियों में से एक है।
तो omega equals two pi f, यानी two pi into fifty, बराबर one hundred pi, यानी three hundred fourteen point one six radians per second.

अब सब कुछ peak emf वाले formula में रखिए। One hundred turns, into zero point five zero tesla, into zero point zero two zero square metres, into three hundred fourteen point one six. मिलता है three hundred and fourteen volts.
Peak emf है लगभग three hundred and fourteen volts. और अगर ये number जाना-पहचाना लगे, तो लगना ही चाहिए।

<excited> भारत की mains supply लगभग two hundred and twenty volts बताई जाती है, लेकिन वो r m s value है, peak नहीं। Two hundred twenty volt r m s supply का peak है two hundred twenty into root two, यानी लगभग three hundred and eleven volts. तो हमारी textbook वाली coil practically mains voltage बना रही है। ये question की design में इत्तेफ़ाक़ नहीं है, और अपने answer में इसे notice करना examiner को दिखाता है कि आप समझते हैं r m s का असली मतलब क्या है।

sections.title: NEET speed trap: what doubling the spin actually changes

board_events.text: A simple AC generator produces peak emf eps-nought at output frequency f
The prime mover is then adjusted so the coil spins at TWICE the angular speed. What happens to (a) the peak emf and (b) the frequency of the output?
The trap: students change the peak emf but forget the frequency also changes. Or they over-correct and quadruple the emf.

board_events.caption: Both the height and the horizontal spacing of the wave are set by the same omega

board_events.text: The fast, correct read
Both the amplitude and the output frequency are tied to the SAME omega. Peak emf is NBA omega, and the output frequency IS the rotation frequency.
The one-line rule: spin faster and you get a bigger AND a faster-alternating output, in lock-step. You cannot buy one without the other.

segments.text: A N E E T conceptual question now, and this one catches students in two different directions, which is what makes it a good trap.

A simple A C generator produces a peak emf epsilon nought at output frequency f. The prime mover is then adjusted so the coil spins at twice the angular speed. What happens to the peak emf, and what happens to the frequency of the output?

<curious> Here is the trap, and notice it has two jaws. Some students correctly double the peak emf but then forget that the frequency changes at all, and they answer that only the emf doubles. Others over-correct, half remember that something in this chapter goes as a square, and quadruple the emf. Both wrong answers will be sitting in the options.
Look at the wave. Doubling omega changes two things about that picture at once: the height of the peaks, and how tightly packed they are horizontally. Both are controlled by the same omega.
So here is the fast, correct read, and once you see the structure it takes seconds.

Both quantities are tied to the same omega. The peak emf is N B A omega, so it is directly proportional to omega, with no square anywhere. And the output frequency simply is the rotation frequency, since the coil produces one cycle per revolution. So both scale linearly.
Therefore the peak emf doubles, and the output frequency doubles. Both by exactly a factor of two, and nothing gets a factor of four.

<whisper> The one-line rule to carry into the exam hall: spin faster and you get a bigger and a faster-alternating output, in lock-step. You cannot buy one without the other. And if you remember why that matters practically, from our conditions discussion, it is exactly why power stations raise voltage with transformers rather than by simply spinning the alternator faster.
अब एक N E E T conceptual question, और ये students को दो अलग-अलग दिशाओं में पकड़ता है, जो इसे अच्छा trap बनाता है।

एक simple A C generator, output frequency f पर peak emf epsilon nought बनाता है। फिर prime mover को इस तरह adjust किया जाता है कि coil दोगुनी angular speed से घूमे। Peak emf का क्या होगा, और output की frequency का क्या होगा?

<curious> अब trap देखिए, और ग़ौर कीजिए इसके दो जबड़े हैं। कुछ students peak emf तो सही दोगुनी कर देते हैं लेकिन भूल जाते हैं कि frequency भी बदलती है, और जवाब देते हैं कि सिर्फ़ emf दोगुनी हुई। कुछ दूसरे ज़्यादा सुधार कर बैठते हैं, उन्हें आधा-अधूरा याद रहता है कि इस chapter में कुछ square के साथ जाता है, और emf चार गुनी कर देते हैं। दोनों ग़लत जवाब options में बैठे होंगे।
Wave देखिए। Omega दोगुना करने से उस तस्वीर में एक साथ दो चीज़ें बदलती हैं: शिखरों की ऊँचाई, और वो horizontally कितने पास-पास हैं। दोनों उसी एक omega से नियंत्रित हैं।
तो ये रही तेज़, सही पढ़ाई, और एक बार बनावट दिख जाए तो seconds लगते हैं।

दोनों quantities उसी एक omega से बँधी हैं। Peak emf है N B A omega, तो वो सीधे omega के proportional है, कहीं कोई square नहीं। और output की frequency तो घुमाव की frequency है ही, क्योंकि coil हर चक्कर में एक cycle बनाती है। तो दोनों रैखिक रूप से बदलते हैं।
इसलिए peak emf दोगुनी होती है, और output frequency दोगुनी होती है। दोनों ठीक दो के factor से, और किसी को चार का factor नहीं मिलता।

<whisper> Exam hall में ले जाने वाला एक-line नियम: तेज़ घुमाइए और आपको बड़ा तथा ज़्यादा तेज़ी से बदलता output मिलेगा, दोनों साथ-साथ। एक को दूसरे के बिना नहीं ख़रीदा जा सकता। और अगर याद हो कि practically ये क्यों मायने रखता है, हमारी conditions वाली बात से, तो ठीक इसीलिए power stations voltage transformers से बढ़ाते हैं, alternator तेज़ घुमाकर नहीं।

sections.title: JEE Main level: bridging the generator to AC power

board_events.text: The coil of the previous example, peak emf 314 V at 50 Hz
It is connected across a load resistor R = 100 ohm. Find the rms emf, the rms current, and the average power delivered.
This is the bridge from generator output to AC-circuit power, and it is where the factor of root 2 earns its keep.
Always check by the other route, using peak values directly:

segments.text: This problem bridges the generator output to A C circuit power, which is the natural fusion J E E Main reaches for, and it is where the factor of root two finally earns its keep.

We take the coil from the previous example, with peak emf three hundred fourteen volts at fifty hertz, and connect it across a load resistor of one hundred ohms. Find the r m s emf, the r m s current, and the average power delivered.

Before computing, be clear about why r m s exists at all. The instantaneous emf is swinging between plus and minus its peak, so its average over a cycle is simply zero, which tells us nothing useful about the power. The r m s value is the steady D C value that would deliver the same average power, and that is why every A C rating you have ever seen is quoted in r m s.
So, r m s emf is the peak divided by root two. Three hundred fourteen point one six divided by one point four one four gives two hundred and twenty two volts.

R m s current is then just Ohm's law with r m s values. Two hundred and twenty two over one hundred gives two point two two amperes. Note that you can use Ohm's law directly like this because the load is a pure resistor, with no phase shift between voltage and current.
Average power is r m s emf times r m s current, two hundred twenty two times two point two two, which is about four hundred and ninety three watts.

<whisper> Now check it by the other route, because you have the peak values sitting right there and the check costs one line. Average power also equals peak emf squared over two R. That is three hundred fourteen point one six squared, over two hundred, which is again about four hundred and ninety three watts. They agree, so your root two has gone in the right direction.

And that last point matters more than it sounds. The most common error in this calculation is dividing by root two when you should multiply, or forgetting the factor of two in the denominator of the peak form. Running both routes catches that instantly, and it costs you almost nothing.
ये problem generator के output को A C circuit power से जोड़ती है, जो कि वो स्वाभाविक मिलाव है जिसे J E E Main पकड़ता है, और यहीं root two का factor अपनी क़ीमत वसूल करता है।

हम पिछले example वाली coil लेते हैं, जिसकी peak emf है three hundred fourteen volts, fifty hertz पर, और उसे one hundred ohms के load resistor से जोड़ देते हैं। R m s emf, r m s current, और delivered average power निकालिए।

गणना से पहले साफ़ कर लीजिए कि r m s का वजूद ही क्यों है। Instantaneous emf अपने peak के plus और minus के बीच झूल रही है, तो एक cycle पर उसका औसत सीधे zero है, जो power के बारे में कुछ काम का नहीं बताता। R m s value वो steady D C value है जो उतनी ही average power देती। इसीलिए आपने आज तक जो भी A C rating देखी है, वो r m s में बताई गई है।
तो r m s emf है peak बटा root two. Three hundred fourteen point one six बटा one point four one four देता है two hundred and twenty two volts.

R m s current फिर बस r m s values के साथ Ohm's law है। Two hundred twenty two बटा one hundred देता है two point two two amperes. ध्यान दीजिए आप Ohm's law सीधे इसीलिए लगा पा रहे हैं क्योंकि load शुद्ध resistor है, जिसमें voltage और current के बीच कोई phase shift नहीं।
Average power है r m s emf into r m s current, two hundred twenty two into two point two two, यानी लगभग four hundred and ninety three watts.

<whisper> अब दूसरे रास्ते से check कीजिए, क्योंकि peak values सामने ही रखी हैं और check में एक line लगती है। Average power, peak emf squared बटा two R के भी बराबर है। यानी three hundred fourteen point one six squared, बटा two hundred, जो फिर लगभग four hundred and ninety three watts देता है। दोनों मिल गए, तो आपका root two सही दिशा में गया है।

और ये आख़िरी बात सुनने में जितनी छोटी लगती है उससे ज़्यादा अहम है। इस calculation की सबसे common ग़लती है root two से भाग देना जहाँ गुणा करना था, या peak वाले रूप के denominator में two भूल जाना। दोनों रास्ते चलाने से ये तुरंत पकड़ में आ जाता है, और आपका कुछ ख़ास ख़र्च भी नहीं होता।

sections.title: JEE Advanced level: half the peak emf, but most of the flux

board_events.text: For an AC generator with peak emf eps-nought

Find (a) the angle of rotation theta, measured from the maximum-flux position, at which the instantaneous emf equals HALF its peak value, and (b) the fraction of the peak flux linking the coil at that same instant. Comment on the relationship.

board_events.caption: Emf follows a sine, flux follows a cosine, from the same angle

board_events.text: The setup that makes this easy: measure theta from the maximum-flux position, so flux goes as cosine and emf goes as sine of the SAME angle.
Comment: when the emf has dropped to just HALF its peak, the flux is still 86.6 percent of its maximum. This is the quantitative face of the 90 degree phase difference.
And at that instant, into a resistor R, the delivered power is eps squared over R, which is one QUARTER of the peak instantaneous power, since the emf is halved and power goes as emf squared.

segments.text: This is a lovely J E E Advanced question because it contains almost no arithmetic. It is testing whether you actually understand the phase relationship, or whether you only memorised the phrase ninety degrees out of phase.

For an A C generator with peak emf epsilon nought, find the angle of rotation theta, measured from the maximum-flux position, at which the instantaneous emf equals half its peak value. Then find what fraction of the peak flux is linking the coil at that same instant, and comment on the relationship.
Look at the two curves as we work, because the question is really asking you to read one point off both of them at once.

<curious> Now the setup detail that makes this easy, and it is hidden in the wording. Theta is measured from the maximum-flux position. That means at theta equals zero the flux is at its peak, so the flux goes as cosine theta, and from our derivation the emf goes as sine theta. Same angle, both functions. That single choice of origin is what makes the problem three lines long instead of thirty.
Part a. The emf is epsilon nought sine theta. Set that equal to half epsilon nought, and epsilon nought cancels from both sides, leaving sine theta equals one half. So theta is thirty degrees.

Part b. The flux linkage is phi nought cos theta, where phi nought equals N B A is the peak linkage. At thirty degrees, cos thirty is root three over two, which is zero point eight six six. So the flux is eighty six point six percent of its maximum.

<excited> And now the comment, which is where the marks are, because the question explicitly asks for it. When the emf has dropped all the way to half its peak, the flux is still sitting at nearly eighty seven percent of its maximum. That is the quantitative face of the ninety degree phase difference. Small emf coincides with large flux, and the two never peak together.

One extra observation worth adding if the question has room. At that same instant, delivering into a resistor R, the instantaneous power is emf squared over R. Since the emf is half its peak, and power goes as emf squared, the delivered power is only one quarter of the peak instantaneous power. Halving the voltage quarters the power, which is a habit of thinking worth carrying into the A C chapter.

ये एक बेहद प्यारा J E E Advanced question है क्योंकि इसमें लगभग कोई arithmetic है ही नहीं। ये देख रहा है कि आप phase relationship सचमुच समझते हैं, या आपने बस ninety degrees out of phase वाला वाक्य रट रखा है।

Peak emf epsilon nought वाले A C generator के लिए, वो rotation angle theta निकालिए, जो maximum-flux वाली position से नापा गया हो, जिस पर instantaneous emf अपनी peak value की आधी हो। फिर बताइए कि उसी पल coil से linked flux अपनी peak का कौन सा अंश है, और इस रिश्ते पर टिप्पणी कीजिए।
काम करते हुए दोनों curves देखते रहिए, क्योंकि question असल में आपसे कह रहा है कि एक ही पल को दोनों पर एक साथ पढ़िए।

<curious> अब वो setup वाली detail जो इसे आसान बनाती है, और वो wording में छिपी है। Theta को maximum-flux वाली position से नापा गया है। इसका मतलब theta equals zero पर flux अपने peak पर है, तो flux cosine theta के साथ चलती है, और हमारी derivation के मुताबिक़ emf sine theta के साथ। एक ही angle, दोनों functions. Origin का यही एक चुनाव इस problem को तीस lines की जगह तीन lines का बना देता है।
Part a. Emf है epsilon nought sine theta. उसे half epsilon nought के बराबर रखिए, दोनों तरफ़ से epsilon nought cancel हो जाता है, बचता है sine theta equals one half. तो theta है thirty degrees.

Part b. Flux linkage है phi nought cos theta, जहाँ phi nought equals N B A peak linkage है। Thirty degrees पर, cos thirty है root three बटा two, यानी zero point eight six six. तो flux अपने maximum का eighty six point six percent है।

<excited> और अब टिप्पणी, जहाँ असली marks हैं, क्योंकि question ने साफ़ माँगी है। जब emf गिरकर अपनी peak की पूरी आधी रह गई है, तब भी flux अपने maximum के लगभग सत्तासी percent पर बैठी है। यही ninety degree phase difference का संख्यात्मक चेहरा है। छोटी emf बड़ी flux के साथ आती है, और दोनों कभी एक साथ peak नहीं करते।

एक अतिरिक्त बात जो question में जगह हो तो जोड़ने लायक़ है। उसी पल, resistor R में देते हुए, instantaneous power है emf squared बटा R. चूँकि emf अपनी peak की आधी है, और power emf squared के साथ जाती है, delivered power peak instantaneous power की सिर्फ़ एक चौथाई है। Voltage आधा करने पर power एक चौथाई, और सोचने की यही आदत A C chapter में साथ ले जाने लायक़ है।

sections.title: The four pitfalls of the generator, and the one-breath summary

board_events.text: Pitfall 1: confusing maximum flux with maximum emf
They are 90 degrees out of phase. Emf peaks when flux is ZERO, with the coil plane parallel to B. Emf is zero when flux is MAXIMUM, with the plane perpendicular. Burn this in.
Pitfall 2: forgetting that the peak emf depends on omega
Speed up the rotation and the output grows in amplitude AND in frequency together. You cannot change one alone.
Pitfall 3: the AC versus DC generator mix-up
Slip rings give AC. A split-ring commutator gives pulsating DC. That ring is the entire structural difference. Everything else is identical.
Pitfall 4: dropping the 2 pi
When frequency is given in hertz, you must convert with omega = 2 pi f before plugging into the peak emf formula. This single slip is worth a whole numerical.

Pro-tip: memorise the output in one breath, emf = NBA omega sin omega t with peak NBA times 2 pi f. Whenever a question says maximum emf it means the amplitude, and at that instant the coil is edge-on to the field. For power questions jump straight to eps-nought squared over 2R.

segments.text: Four pitfalls to close this subtopic, and then a summary compact enough to recite in one breath before you walk into the exam.

<whisper> Pitfall one is the big one, and it has claimed more marks in this subtopic than the other three put together. Confusing maximum flux with maximum emf. They are ninety degrees out of phase. The emf peaks when the flux is zero, with the coil plane parallel to the field, edge-on. The emf is zero when the flux is maximum, with the plane perpendicular, face-on. Burn that in, because the exam will offer you the reversed version as a very tempting option.
Pitfall two, forgetting that the peak emf depends on omega.

Speed up the rotation and the output grows in amplitude and in frequency together, in lock-step. You cannot change one alone. Any question that adjusts the rotation speed is testing both halves of that, and answering only the emf half loses the mark.
Pitfall three, the A C versus D C generator mix-up, which is a favourite because it is a single-word difference.

Two slip rings give you A C. One split ring, a commutator, gives you pulsating D C. That ring is the entire structural difference between the two machines. Everything else, the armature, the field magnet, the brushes, the physics, is identical. If a question asks what to change to get D C, the answer is the rings and nothing else.
Pitfall four is pure arithmetic carelessness, but it costs a full numerical. Dropping the two pi.

When frequency is given in hertz, you must convert with omega equals two pi f before plugging into the peak emf formula. Every generator numerical you will meet gives frequency in hertz precisely because this trips people. Make the conversion the first line you write, before anything else.

Now the summary in one breath. Emf equals N B A omega sine omega t, with peak emf N B A times two pi f. Whenever a question says maximum emf, it means the amplitude, and at that instant the coil is edge-on to the field, plane parallel to B. And for any power question, jump straight to epsilon nought squared over two R without going through r m s at all. Those three sentences cover almost every question this subtopic will ever ask you.
इस subtopic को बंद करते हुए चार pitfalls, और फिर एक इतना छोटा summary कि exam में जाने से पहले एक साँस में दोहराया जा सके।

<whisper> Pitfall एक सबसे बड़ी है, और इसने इस subtopic में बाक़ी तीनों मिलाकर से ज़्यादा marks खाए हैं। Maximum flux को maximum emf समझ लेना। ये ninety degrees out of phase हैं। Emf तब peak करती है जब flux zero हो, coil का plane field के parallel, edge-on. Emf तब zero होती है जब flux maximum हो, plane perpendicular, face-on. इसे गाँठ बाँध लीजिए, क्योंकि exam आपको उल्टा version एक बेहद लुभावने option की तरह पेश करेगा।
Pitfall दो, ये भूल जाना कि peak emf omega पर depend करती है।

घुमाव तेज़ कीजिए और output amplitude तथा frequency दोनों में साथ-साथ बढ़ता है। एक को अकेले नहीं बदला जा सकता। जो भी question rotation speed बदलता है, वो दोनों हिस्सों का test है, और सिर्फ़ emf वाला आधा जवाब देने पर mark चला जाता है।
Pitfall तीन, A C बनाम D C generator की उलझन, जो इसलिए favourite है क्योंकि फ़र्क़ सिर्फ़ एक शब्द का है।

दो slip rings आपको A C देती हैं। एक split ring, यानी commutator, आपको pulsating D C देता है। वही एक ring दोनों machines के बीच का पूरा structural फ़र्क़ है। बाक़ी सब कुछ, armature, field magnet, brushes, physics, बिलकुल एक जैसा। अगर question पूछे कि D C पाने के लिए क्या बदलेंगे, तो जवाब है rings, और कुछ नहीं।
Pitfall चार शुद्ध arithmetic की लापरवाही है, लेकिन पूरा numerical ले जाती है। दो pi छोड़ देना।

जब frequency hertz में दी हो, तो peak emf formula में डालने से पहले omega equals two pi f से convert करना ही होगा। हर generator numerical आपको frequency hertz में ही देगा, ठीक इसीलिए कि यहाँ लोग फिसलते हैं। उस conversion को अपनी लिखी हुई पहली line बनाइए, बाक़ी सब उसके बाद।

अब एक साँस वाला summary. Emf equals N B A omega sine omega t, और peak emf N B A into two pi f. जब भी question कहे maximum emf, मतलब amplitude, और उस पल coil field के edge-on है, plane field के parallel. और किसी भी power वाले question में सीधे epsilon nought squared बटा two R पर कूदिए, r m s के रास्ते जाए बिना। ये तीन वाक्य लगभग हर वो question ढक लेते हैं जो ये subtopic आपसे कभी पूछेगा।

board_events.text: Flux is $\Phi_B = BA\cos\theta$. There are exactly THREE things you can change to make flux vary, and each one is a subtopic of this chapter.
Change B, the field: self and mutual induction, transformers. That was Subtopic 03.
Change A, the area, by moving a conductor: motional emf, the rod-on-rails generator. That was Subtopic 02.
Change theta, the orientation, by rotating the coil: the AC generator. That was Subtopic 04.
And one bonus case: when the conductor is a solid block rather than a wire, the induced currents swirl as eddy currents. That is the entire chapter on one page.

segments.text: We have reached the point where everything can be zoomed out and seen at once. And what you will find is that this chapter is far smaller than it looked from inside it.

Every single result in this chapter, all four subtopics, every formula and every worked example, is a consequence of one sentence. A changing magnetic flux induces an emf, and the induced effects oppose the change that produced them. Faraday in the first half, Lenz in the second.
Look at the diagram, because this is the map of the chapter. One box in the middle, three arrows branching out, and one side branch.

The flux is B A cos theta. Now count. There are exactly three quantities in that expression that you can change in order to make the flux vary. Three, no more. And each one turned into a subtopic of this chapter.
Change B, the field itself. That gives you self and mutual induction, inductors and transformers, everything built on L and M. That was subtopic three.
Change A, the effective area, by moving a conductor so the circuit sweeps out new area. That gives you motional emf and the rod-on-rails generator, emf equals B v l. That was subtopic two.
Change theta, the orientation, by rotating the coil in a fixed field. That gives you the A C generator, emf equals N B A omega sine omega t. That was subtopic four.

<excited> And there is one bonus case, hanging off the side of the diagram. When the conductor is a solid block rather than a neat thin wire, the induced currents have nowhere particular to go, so they swirl as eddy currents. That is the whole chapter, on one page. If you can rebuild this diagram from memory, you can rebuild the chapter from it.
अब हम उस मुक़ाम पर हैं जहाँ सब कुछ एक साथ, दूर से देखा जा सकता है। और आप पाएँगे कि ये chapter अंदर से जितना बड़ा लगता था, उससे कहीं छोटा है।

इस chapter का हर एक result, चारों subtopics, हर formula और हर worked example, एक वाक्य का नतीजा है। बदलती हुई magnetic flux emf induce करती है, और induced असर उसी change का विरोध करते हैं जिसने उन्हें पैदा किया। पहले आधे में Faraday, दूसरे में Lenz.
Diagram देखिए, क्योंकि यही इस chapter का नक़्शा है। बीच में एक box, तीन तीर बाहर निकलते हुए, और एक बग़ल की शाखा।
Flux है B A cos theta. अब गिनिए। उस expression में ठीक तीन quantities हैं जिन्हें बदलकर आप flux को बदल सकते हैं। तीन, इससे ज़्यादा नहीं। और हर एक इस chapter का एक subtopic बन गई।
B यानी field ख़ुद बदलिए। इससे मिलता है self और mutual induction, inductors और transformers, L तथा M पर बना सब कुछ। वो subtopic तीन था।
A यानी असरदार area बदलिए, conductor को हिलाकर ताकि circuit नया area बुहारे। इससे मिलता है motional emf और rod-on-rails generator, emf equals B v l. वो subtopic दो था।
Theta यानी orientation बदलिए, स्थिर field में coil घुमाकर। इससे मिलता है A C generator, emf equals N B A omega sine omega t. वो subtopic चार था।

<excited> और एक bonus case है, diagram की बग़ल से लटका हुआ। जब conductor साफ़-सुथरे पतले तार की जगह ठोस block हो, तो induced currents के पास जाने की कोई ख़ास जगह नहीं होती, तो वो eddy currents की तरह भँवर बनाते हैं। यही पूरा chapter है, एक पन्ने पर। अगर आप ये diagram याद से बना सकते हैं, तो उससे पूरा chapter बना सकते हैं।

board_events.text: Find (a) the induced emf, (b) the current, (c) the force required, (d) the total charge as the loop fully exits, and (e) the heat generated.
The key reading: while the loop STRADDLES the boundary, only one side cuts field lines. So it is a motional-emf problem, and the rod-on-rails chain applies directly.

segments.text: Now three boss-level problems that deliberately combine subtopics, the way real exam problems do. This first one fuses subtopic one and subtopic two.

A square loop of side zero point one zero metres, resistance zero point two zero ohms, is pulled out of a region of uniform field of zero point five zero tesla at a constant two point zero metres per second, as it crosses the boundary.
Look at the figure before you write. The loop is straddling the boundary. Part of it is still in the field, part has left.
Five parts to find: the emf, the current, the force required, the total charge as the loop fully exits, and the heat generated.

<curious> Now the key reading, and it decides the whole approach. While the loop straddles the boundary, only one side is still inside the field cutting lines. The other three sides contribute nothing, either because they are outside or because they run parallel to the motion. So this is a motional emf problem, and the rod-on-rails chain applies directly, with that one side playing the part of the rod.

So run the chain. Emf equals B v a, which is zero point five zero times two point zero times zero point one zero, giving zero point one zero volts. Current is emf over R, zero point one zero over zero point two zero, giving zero point five zero amperes. Force is B I a, which is zero point five zero times zero point five zero times zero point one zero, giving zero point zero two five newtons.

Part d switches tools deliberately. For total charge, do not integrate the current. Go straight to the subtopic-one result, charge equals change in flux over R. The loop loses all of its flux, which is B times a squared, so q equals zero point five zero times zero point zero one, over zero point two zero, giving zero point zero two five coulombs.

<whisper> Part e needs the time, so get it from the geometry: the loop must travel its own side length to fully exit, so t equals a over v, which is zero point zero five seconds. Then heat is I squared R t, giving two point five times ten to the minus three joules. And here is the check that confirms everything: that heat equals the mechanical work F v t, exactly as energy conservation demands. Whenever a problem gives you both an energy and a force, run that check.
अब तीन boss-level problems, जो जानबूझकर subtopics को मिलाती हैं, ठीक जैसे असली exam problems करती हैं। ये पहली subtopic एक और दो को जोड़ती है।

Zero point one zero metres भुजा वाला square loop, resistance zero point two zero ohms, zero point five zero tesla की uniform field वाले इलाक़े से constant two point zero metres per second पर बाहर खींचा जा रहा है, जब वो boundary पार कर रहा है।
लिखने से पहले figure देखिए। Loop boundary पर आधा-आधा है। उसका कुछ हिस्सा अभी field में है, कुछ बाहर निकल चुका है।
पाँच parts निकालने हैं: emf, current, ज़रूरी force, loop के पूरी तरह बाहर निकलने तक कुल charge, और पैदा हुई heat.

<curious> अब वो अहम पढ़ाई, जो पूरा तरीक़ा तय कर देती है। जब तक loop boundary पर आधा-आधा है, सिर्फ़ एक भुजा field के अंदर lines काट रही है। बाक़ी तीन कुछ contribute नहीं करतीं, या तो इसलिए कि वो बाहर हैं या इसलिए कि वो motion के parallel हैं। तो ये motional emf की problem है, और rod-on-rails वाली chain सीधे लगती है, जिसमें वो एक भुजा rod का किरदार निभा रही है।

तो chain चलाइए। Emf equals B v a, यानी zero point five zero into two point zero into zero point one zero, जो देता है zero point one zero volts. Current है emf बटा R, zero point one zero बटा zero point two zero, यानी zero point five zero amperes. Force है B I a, यानी zero point five zero into zero point five zero into zero point one zero, जो देता है zero point zero two five newtons.

Part d जानबूझकर औज़ार बदलता है। कुल charge के लिए current को integrate मत कीजिए। सीधे subtopic एक वाले result पर जाइए, charge equals flux का बदलाव बटा R. Loop अपनी पूरी flux खो देता है, जो है B into a squared, तो q equals zero point five zero into zero point zero one, बटा zero point two zero, यानी zero point zero two five coulombs.

<whisper> Part e के लिए time चाहिए, तो वो geometry से निकालिए: पूरी तरह बाहर निकलने के लिए loop को अपनी ही भुजा जितना चलना है, तो t equals a बटा v, यानी zero point zero five seconds. फिर heat है I squared R t, जो देता है two point five times ten to the minus three joules. और ये रहा वो check जो सब कुछ पक्का कर देता है: वो heat, mechanical work F v t के बराबर है, ठीक जैसा energy conservation माँगता है। जब भी problem आपको energy और force दोनों दे, ये check ज़रूर चलाइए।

board_events.text: The move: differentiate the sinusoidal current, and the omega drops out front. That omega is the whole point of the problem.
Note the structural echo of the AC generator: a sinusoidal drive gives a sinusoidal output, shifted by 90 degrees. Sine in, cosine out.

segments.text: The second boss problem fuses subtopic three with subtopic four. It looks like a mutual inductance question, but the machinery of the A C generator is hiding inside it.

Two coaxial solenoids have a mutual inductance of two point zero millihenry. The primary carries an alternating current given by I nought sine omega t, with I nought equal to three point zero amperes and a frequency of fifty hertz. Find the peak emf induced in the secondary.

Notice what is different from our earlier mutual inductance problem. There, the current was switched off and we used a simple change over a time interval. Here the current is continuously sinusoidal, so we need calculus rather than a difference.
Look at the diagram to keep the structure clear: changing current in coil one, emf in coil two, coupled through M and nothing else.

<excited> Now the move that solves it. The emf in the secondary is minus M times the derivative of the primary current. So differentiate I nought sine omega t. The derivative of sine omega t is omega cos omega t, and that omega drops out in front. That factor of omega is the entire point of the problem, and it is what students forget.
So the secondary emf is minus M I nought omega cos omega t. It is a cosine, oscillating at the same frequency, and its amplitude is M I nought omega.

Substitute. M is two point zero times ten to the minus three. I nought is three point zero. And omega is two pi times fifty, which is three hundred fourteen point one six. Multiplying those together gives about one point nine volts.

<whisper> And now the observation worth carrying away, because it is why this problem sits in the synthesis section. Look at the structural echo of the A C generator. A sinusoidal drive gives a sinusoidal output, shifted by ninety degrees. Sine went in and cosine came out, exactly as flux and emf were a quarter cycle apart in the generator. It is the same mathematics, because it is the same law being differentiated.
दूसरी boss problem subtopic तीन को subtopic चार से मिलाती है। दिखने में ये mutual inductance का question है, लेकिन इसके अंदर A C generator की मशीनरी छिपी है।

दो coaxial solenoids की mutual inductance है two point zero millihenry. Primary में alternating current बह रहा है, I nought sine omega t, जहाँ I nought है three point zero amperes और frequency fifty hertz. Secondary में induce होने वाली peak emf निकालिए।

ग़ौर कीजिए ये हमारी पहले वाली mutual inductance problem से कैसे अलग है। वहाँ current switch off हुआ था और हमने एक time interval पर सीधा बदलाव इस्तेमाल किया था। यहाँ current लगातार sinusoidal है, तो अंतर की जगह calculus चाहिए।
बनावट साफ़ रखने के लिए diagram देखिए: coil one में बदलता current, coil two में emf, और बीच में सिर्फ़ M का जोड़, और कुछ नहीं।

<excited> अब वो चाल जो इसे हल करती है। Secondary की emf है minus M times primary current का derivative. तो I nought sine omega t को differentiate कीजिए। Sine omega t का derivative है omega cos omega t, और वो omega आगे निकलकर बैठ जाता है। Omega का वही factor इस problem की पूरी जान है, और यही students भूलते हैं।
तो secondary emf है minus M I nought omega cos omega t. ये एक cosine है, उसी frequency पर झूलती हुई, और इसका amplitude है M I nought omega.

Substitute कीजिए। M है two point zero times ten to the minus three. I nought है three point zero. और omega है two pi into fifty, यानी three hundred fourteen point one six. इन्हें गुणा करने पर मिलता है लगभग one point nine volts.

<whisper> और अब वो बात जो साथ ले जाने लायक़ है, क्योंकि इसीलिए ये problem synthesis वाले हिस्से में है। A C generator की संरचनात्मक गूँज देखिए। Sinusoidal drive, sinusoidal output देता है, ninety degrees खिसका हुआ। Sine अंदर गया और cosine बाहर आया, ठीक वैसे जैसे generator में flux और emf एक चौथाई चक्र अलग थे। ये वही गणित है, क्योंकि यही वही law है जिसे differentiate किया जा रहा है।

board_events.text: Find (a) the peak emf, (b) the rms current, and (c) the average power delivered.
Notice part (c) never needed the rms current. Going straight from peak emf to average power is the faster route, and it removes one chance to misplace a root 2.

segments.text: The third boss problem takes the generator all the way through to delivered power, which is the complete end-to-end calculation an exam can ask for.

An A C generator has a coil of fifty turns, area zero point zero two zero square metres, in a field of zero point three zero tesla, rotating at fifty hertz, connected across a load of twenty ohms. Find the peak emf, the r m s current, and the average power delivered.
The machine is the one we built. Coil, field magnet, slip rings, brushes, and now a real resistive load drawing power out of it.
Three parts, and notice they take you from pure induction physics at one end to A C circuit power at the other.

Part a. Convert the frequency first, as always: omega equals two pi times fifty, which is three hundred fourteen point one six radians per second. Then peak emf is N B A omega, which is fifty times zero point three zero times zero point zero two zero times three hundred fourteen point one six. That gives about ninety four volts.

Part b. The r m s current is the r m s emf divided by R, and the r m s emf is the peak over root two. So it is ninety four point two five divided by one point four one four, then divided by twenty. That gives about three point three amperes.
Part c. Average power is peak emf squared over two R. Ninety four point two five squared, divided by forty, giving about two hundred and twenty two watts.

<whisper> And notice something about that last step, because it is a habit worth adopting. Part c never needed the r m s current at all. We could have gone straight from the peak emf to the average power, skipping part b entirely. That route is faster, and more importantly it removes one opportunity to divide by root two when you should have multiplied. Whenever a question asks only for average power, jump straight to epsilon nought squared over two R.
तीसरी boss problem generator को पूरे रास्ते delivered power तक ले जाती है, यानी वो पूरी शुरू-से-आख़िर तक की calculation जो exam पूछ सकता है।

एक A C generator में fifty turns की coil है, area zero point zero two zero square metres, zero point three zero tesla की field में, fifty hertz पर घूमती हुई, और twenty ohms के load से जुड़ी। Peak emf, r m s current, और delivered average power निकालिए।
Machine वही है जो हमने बनाई थी। Coil, field magnet, slip rings, brushes, और अब एक असली resistive load जो उससे power खींच रहा है।
तीन parts, और ग़ौर कीजिए ये आपको एक सिरे की शुद्ध induction physics से दूसरे सिरे की A C circuit power तक ले जाते हैं।

Part a. हमेशा की तरह पहले frequency convert कीजिए: omega equals two pi into fifty, यानी three hundred fourteen point one six radians per second. फिर peak emf है N B A omega, यानी fifty into zero point three zero into zero point zero two zero into three hundred fourteen point one six. मिलता है लगभग ninety four volts.
Part b. R m s current है r m s emf बटा R, और r m s emf है peak बटा root two. तो ninety four point two five बटा one point four one four, फिर बटा twenty. मिलता है लगभग three point three amperes.
Part c. Average power है peak emf squared बटा two R. Ninety four point two five squared, बटा forty, यानी लगभग two hundred and twenty two watts.

<whisper> और उस आख़िरी क़दम के बारे में एक बात ध्यान दीजिए, क्योंकि ये अपनाने लायक़ आदत है। Part c को r m s current की ज़रूरत थी ही नहीं। हम सीधे peak emf से average power पर जा सकते थे, part b को पूरी तरह छोड़कर। वो रास्ता तेज़ है, और उससे भी अहम, वो root two से भाग देने का एक मौक़ा हटा देता है जहाँ गुणा करना था। जब भी question सिर्फ़ average power पूछे, सीधे epsilon nought squared बटा two R पर कूदिए।

sections.title: Choosing the right tool, and the traps that span subtopics

board_events.text: A fast diagnostic when you face an unfamiliar question
Is something MOVING, sweeping area? Reach for motional emf, B v l, or half B omega l squared if it rotates about an end.
Is a CURRENT changing in a coil? Reach for inductance: minus L dI/dt in the same coil, or minus M dI1/dt in a neighbouring one.
Is a coil ROTATING in a field? It is an AC generator: N B A omega sin omega t. Is the FIELD itself changing in time? Go straight to Faraday and differentiate.
Asked only for TOTAL CHARGE? Skip emf and current entirely, use q = N delta-phi over R. Need a DIRECTION or a sign? That is always Lenz.
Cross-topic traps, the ones that span subtopics

Flux versus rate of flux: a large constant flux gives ZERO emf. The most-failed idea in the chapter. And the angle theta is always from the area vector, so a field at angle alpha to the PLANE gives B A sin alpha.
Flux and emf are 90 degrees out of phase. L goes as N squared, U goes as I squared, but peak emf goes only as omega. Check the power of each variable before answering.
The minus sign is direction, not magnitude. Conductor type decides eddy currents: insulators have none. And slip rings mean AC while a split ring means DC.

segments.text: Before the formula sheet, let me give you the two things that turn a pile of formulas into a working exam strategy: a diagnostic for choosing the right tool, and then the traps that span subtopics. The diagnostic is a short series of questions to ask yourself when an unfamiliar problem lands in front of you.
Is something moving, sweeping out area? Then reach for motional emf, B v l, or half B omega l squared if it is rotating about one end.
Is a current changing in a coil? Then reach for inductance. Minus L d I by d t if the emf you want is in the same coil, or minus M d I one by d t if it is in a neighbouring one.

Is a coil rotating in a field? Then it is an A C generator, N B A omega sine omega t. Or is the field itself changing with time? Then go straight to Faraday and differentiate the flux, with whatever is time-dependent.

<whisper> Two special cases that override everything else. If you are asked only for the total charge that flowed, skip emf and current entirely and go straight to q equals N delta phi over R. And if you need a direction or a sign, that is always Lenz's law: whatever the induced effect is, it opposes the change.
Now the cross-topic traps, the ones that catch students precisely because they span subtopics.

First and largest: flux versus rate of flux. A large constant flux gives exactly zero emf. That is the most-failed idea in this chapter and it appears in every subtopic. And close behind it, the angle theta is always measured from the area vector, so a field given at angle alpha to the plane gives flux B A sin alpha, not cosine.

Then the ones about powers and phases. Flux and emf are ninety degrees out of phase. L goes as N squared. Stored energy goes as I squared. But peak emf goes only as omega, linearly. Square and linear laws are easy to mix up, so check the power of each variable before you answer.

And finally the three that decide single-mark questions: the minus sign is direction and not magnitude, conductor type decides whether eddy currents exist at all since insulators have none, and slip rings mean A C while a split ring means D C.

Formula sheet से पहले, मैं आपको वो दो चीज़ें देती हूँ जो formulas के ढेर को काम की exam strategy बना देती हैं: सही औज़ार चुनने की diagnostic, और फिर वो traps जो subtopics के आर-पार फैले हैं। Diagnostic कुछ छोटे सवालों की कड़ी है, जो अनजानी problem सामने आने पर ख़ुद से पूछने हैं।
क्या कुछ हिल रहा है, area बुहार रहा है? तो motional emf उठाइए, B v l, या half B omega l squared अगर वो एक सिरे के गिर्द घूम रहा है।
क्या किसी coil में current बदल रहा है? तो inductance उठाइए। Minus L d I by d t अगर emf उसी coil में चाहिए, या minus M d I one by d t अगर पड़ोसी coil में।

क्या कोई coil field में घूम रही है? तो ये A C generator है, N B A omega sine omega t. या क्या field ख़ुद समय के साथ बदल रही है? तो सीधे Faraday पर जाइए और flux को differentiate कीजिए, जो भी time पर निर्भर हो उसके साथ।

<whisper> दो ख़ास मामले जो बाक़ी सब पर भारी पड़ते हैं। अगर सिर्फ़ कुल बहा हुआ charge पूछा गया है, तो emf और current दोनों छोड़कर सीधे q equals N delta phi बटा R पर जाइए। और अगर direction या sign चाहिए, तो वो हमेशा Lenz's law है: induced असर जो भी हो, वो change का विरोध करता है।
अब cross-topic traps, वो जो students को ठीक इसलिए पकड़ते हैं क्योंकि वो subtopics के आर-पार फैले हैं।

पहली और सबसे बड़ी: flux बनाम flux की दर। बड़ी constant flux बिलकुल zero emf देती है। यही इस chapter का सबसे ज़्यादा गँवाया जाने वाला idea है और ये हर subtopic में आता है। और उसके ठीक पीछे, theta हमेशा area vector से नापा जाता है, तो plane से alpha angle पर दी गई field, flux B A sin alpha देती है, cosine नहीं।

फिर powers और phases वाले। Flux और emf ninety degrees out of phase हैं। L, N squared के साथ जाती है। Stored energy, I squared के साथ। लेकिन peak emf सिर्फ़ omega के साथ, रैखिक रूप से। Square और linear नियम आपस में उलझ जाते हैं, तो जवाब देने से पहले हर variable की power जाँचिए।

और आख़िर में वो तीन जो एक-एक mark वाले questions तय करते हैं: minus sign direction है magnitude नहीं, conductor का प्रकार तय करता है कि eddy currents होंगे भी या नहीं क्योंकि insulators में होते ही नहीं, और slip rings मतलब A C जबकि split ring मतलब D C.

sections.title: Your complete toolkit for Electromagnetic Induction

board_events.text: Everything in one place. This is your complete toolkit.

board_events.latex: N\Phi = LI,\quad \varepsilon = -L\frac{dI}{dt},\quad L = \mu_0 n^2 A l = \frac{\mu_0N^2A}{l},\quad U = \tfrac{1}{2}LI^2,\quad u_B = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}
N_2\Phi_2 = MI_1,\quad \varepsilon_2 = -M\frac{dI_1}{dt},\quad M = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 A l,\quad M = k\sqrt{L_1L_2}
\varepsilon = NBA\omega\sin\omega t,\quad \varepsilon_0 = NBA\omega = NBA(2\pi f),\quad P_{avg} = \frac{\varepsilon_0^2}{2R}

board_events.text: Units and dimensions: flux in weber, $[ML^2T^{-2}A^{-1}]$. Emf in volt, $[ML^2T^{-3}A^{-1}]$. Inductance in henry, $[ML^2T^{-2}A^{-2}]$.

segments.text: This section does not teach anything new. It hands you the complete toolkit for this chapter in one place, so use it for revision the night before, not for learning.
Flux, in both its forms. B dot A, which is B A cos theta, for a uniform field across a flat area. And the integral of B dot d A when the field varies from point to point.
The Faraday group. Emf is minus N times the rate of change of flux. Current is the magnitude of that emf divided by R. And total charge is N times the flux change over R, with no time in it.

The motional emf group, which is really one formula and its cascade. Emf equals B v l. Force equals B squared l squared v over R. Power equals B squared l squared v squared over R. And for a rod rotating about one end, half B omega l squared, with the length squared.
Terminal velocity for a rod falling on vertical rails: m g R over B squared l squared. Remember this comes from a force balance, not a differential equation.

The self-inductance group. Flux linkage equals L I. Emf is minus L d I by d t. For a solenoid, L is mu nought n squared A l, or equivalently mu nought N squared A over l. Stored energy is half L I squared, and the energy density is B squared over two mu nought.

The mutual inductance group, mirroring it line for line. Flux linkage in coil two equals M I one. Emf in coil two is minus M d I one by d t. For two coaxial solenoids, M is mu nought n one n two A l. And from the self-inductances, M equals k root L one L two.
The generator group. Emf equals N B A omega sine omega t, with peak emf N B A omega, which is N B A times two pi f. And average power into a resistor is peak emf squared over two R.
Finally the units: flux in weber, emf in volt, inductance in henry, with the dimensions written on the board. If you can reproduce this board from memory, you have the chapter.
ये section कुछ नया नहीं सिखाता। ये आपको इस chapter का पूरा toolkit एक जगह थमा देता है, तो इसे exam से एक रात पहले revision के लिए इस्तेमाल कीजिए, सीखने के लिए नहीं।
Flux, अपने दोनों रूपों में। B dot A, यानी B A cos theta, uniform field और flat area के लिए। और B dot d A का integral जब field एक point से दूसरे तक बदलती हो।
Faraday वाला समूह। Emf है minus N times flux के बदलने की दर। Current है उस emf का magnitude बटा R. और कुल charge है N times flux का बदलाव बटा R, जिसमें time है ही नहीं।

Motional emf वाला समूह, जो असल में एक formula और उसका झरना है। Emf equals B v l. Force equals B squared l squared v बटा R. Power equals B squared l squared v squared बटा R. और एक सिरे के गिर्द घूमते rod के लिए, half B omega l squared, जिसमें length squared है।
Vertical rails पर गिरते rod की terminal velocity: m g R बटा B squared l squared. याद रखिए ये force balance से आती है, differential equation से नहीं।

Self-inductance वाला समूह। Flux linkage equals L I. Emf है minus L d I by d t. Solenoid के लिए L है mu nought n squared A l, या बराबर रूप से mu nought N squared A बटा l. Stored energy है half L I squared, और energy density है B squared बटा two mu nought.

Mutual inductance वाला समूह, line दर line उसकी नक़ल करता हुआ। Coil two की flux linkage equals M I one. Coil two की emf है minus M d I one by d t. दो coaxial solenoids के लिए M है mu nought n one n two A l. और self-inductances से, M equals k root L one L two.
Generator वाला समूह। Emf equals N B A omega sine omega t, peak emf N B A omega के साथ, जो है N B A into two pi f. और resistor में average power है peak emf squared बटा two R.
आख़िर में units: flux weber में, emf volt में, inductance henry में, और dimensions board पर लिखे हुए। अगर आप ये board याद से बना सकें, तो chapter आपका है।

sections.title: Quick recall: the memory aids and the final checklist

board_events.text: The three memory aids that carry the chapter
Change, not amount (Faraday). Nature is lazy, it opposes change (Lenz). Theta is from the normal, not the plane (flux angle).
Motional emf: move a wire, make a battery. No conductor, no eddies, which is PVC versus copper. Laminate to resist, not to block.

Inductance is electrical inertia: it opposes change of current, not current. L goes as N squared. M is the geometric mean, perfectly coupled at k = 1. Energy hides in the field, B squared over 2 mu-nought.
Generator: edge-on for max emf, with the coil plane parallel to the field. Slip rings sing AC, split ring barks DC. Faster spin means bigger AND quicker.
Exam weightage at a glance
CBSE Boards: the derivations. Faraday and Lenz, motional emf B v l, solenoid L and coaxial M, the AC generator emf, plus short answers on eddy-current uses.
NEET: concept questions. Flux versus emf, Lenz direction, eddy-current applications, and the coil position for maximum or zero emf.

JEE Main: numericals on induced charge, the rod-on-rails chain, terminal velocity, inductance and energy, peak and instantaneous generator emf. JEE Advanced: flux by integration, rotating rods, coupled circuits, and fusions with mechanics and AC power.

segments.text: Final section of the chapter, and this one is built for the last twenty minutes before you walk into the exam hall. Memory aids first, then where the marks actually sit.

<whisper> Three phrases carry most of this chapter. Change, not amount, which is Faraday. Nature is lazy, it opposes change, which is Lenz. And theta is from the normal, not the plane, which is the flux angle. If you are ever stuck at the start of a question, run those three and one of them will usually unlock it.

For motional emf and eddy currents: move a wire, make a battery. No conductor, no eddies, which settles the P V C versus copper question instantly. And laminate to resist, not to block, which is the lamination answer in five words.

For inductance: it is electrical inertia, opposing change of current and not current itself. L goes as N squared, so doubling the turns quadruples it. M is the geometric mean of the two self-inductances, at its largest when perfectly coupled at k equals one. And energy hides in the field, at B squared over two mu nought.

For the generator: edge-on for maximum emf, meaning the coil plane parallel to the field. Slip rings sing A C, split ring barks D C. And faster spin means bigger and quicker together, never one alone.
Now where the marks actually are, exam by exam, so you can spend your last revision hours in the right place.

C B S E Boards want the derivations. Faraday and Lenz including Lenz as energy conservation, motional emf B v l by both routes, the solenoid self-inductance and the coaxial mutual inductance, and the A C generator emf with construction. Plus short answers on eddy-current uses.

N E E T wants concepts, almost never derivations. Flux versus emf, Lenz direction, eddy-current applications like laminations and the falling-magnet pipe demo, and the coil position for maximum or zero emf.

And J E E Main wants numericals: induced charge, the rod-on-rails chain, terminal velocity, inductance and energy, peak and instantaneous generator emf. J E E Advanced goes further still, with flux by integration near a wire, rotating rods, coupled circuits, and fusions with mechanics and A C power. That is the chapter. Go and get the marks.
Chapter का आख़िरी section, और ये उन आख़िरी बीस मिनटों के लिए बना है जो exam hall में जाने से पहले होते हैं। पहले memory aids, फिर ये कि marks असल में कहाँ बैठे हैं।

<whisper> तीन वाक्य इस chapter का ज़्यादातर हिस्सा उठा लेते हैं। बदलाव, मात्रा नहीं, यानी Faraday. Nature आलसी है, वो बदलाव का विरोध करती है, यानी Lenz. और theta normal से है, plane से नहीं, यानी flux का angle. अगर कभी question की शुरुआत में अटक जाएँ, तो ये तीनों चलाइए और आम तौर पर इनमें से एक ताला खोल देगा।

Motional emf और eddy currents के लिए: तार हिलाओ, battery बनाओ। कोई conductor नहीं, तो कोई eddies नहीं, जो P V C बनाम copper वाला सवाल तुरंत निपटा देता है। और laminate resistance बढ़ाने को, रोकने को नहीं, जो पाँच शब्दों में lamination का जवाब है।

Inductance के लिए: ये electrical inertia है, current के बदलाव का विरोध करती है, current का नहीं। L, N squared के साथ जाती है, तो turns दोगुने करने पर चार गुनी। M दोनों self-inductances का geometric mean है, और सबसे बड़ी तब जब perfectly coupled हो, k equals one पर। और energy field में छिपी रहती है, B squared बटा two mu nought पर।
Generator के लिए: maximum emf के लिए edge-on, यानी coil का plane field के parallel. Slip rings A C गाती हैं, split ring D C भौंकता है। और तेज़ घुमाव मतलब बड़ा और तेज़ दोनों साथ, कभी अकेला एक नहीं।
अब marks असल में कहाँ हैं, exam दर exam, ताकि आप revision के आख़िरी घंटे सही जगह लगाएँ।

C B S E Boards को derivations चाहिए। Faraday और Lenz, जिसमें Lenz को energy conservation के रूप में समझाना शामिल है, motional emf B v l दोनों रास्तों से, solenoid की self-inductance और coaxial की mutual inductance, और A C generator की emf construction के साथ। साथ में eddy-current के उपयोगों पर short answers.

N E E T को concepts चाहिए, derivations लगभग कभी नहीं। Flux बनाम emf, Lenz की direction, eddy-current के उपयोग जैसे laminations और गिरते magnet वाला pipe demo, और maximum या zero emf के लिए coil की position.

और J E E Main को numericals चाहिए: induced charge, rod-on-rails की chain, terminal velocity, inductance और energy, peak तथा instantaneous generator emf. J E E Advanced उससे भी आगे जाता है, wire के पास integration से flux, rotating rods, coupled circuits, और mechanics तथा A C power के साथ मिलाव। यही पूरा chapter है। जाइए और marks लेकर आइए।
